2.16.s:
bṛhaspatiruvāca
ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi dānāni ca phalāni ca /
tāraṇaṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ svargamārgasukhāvaham //
2.16.d:
बृहस्पतिरुवाच
अतः परं प्रवक्ष्यामि दानानि च फलानि च ।
तारणं सर्वभूतानां स्वर्गमार्गसुखावहम् ॥
2.16.m: Bṛhaspati said: / Hereafter I shall explain the gifts and their fruits, / which deliver all beings and bring the happiness of the celestial path.

2.16.s:
loke śreṣṭhatam sarvamātmanaścaiva yatpriyam /
sarvaṃ pitṝṇāṃ dātavyaṃ teṣāmevājñayārthinā //
2.16.d:
लोके श्रेष्ठतम् सर्वमात्मनश्चैव यत्प्रियम् ।
सर्वं पितॄणां दातव्यं तेषामेवाज्ञयार्थिना ॥
2.16.m: Whatever in the world is most excellent, and whatever is dear to oneself, / should all be given to the ancestors by one seeking to fulfill their command.

2.16.s:
jāṃbūnadamayaṃ divyaṃ vimānaṃ sūryasannibham /
divyāpsarobhiḥ saṃpūrṇamannado labhate 'kṣayam //
2.16.d:
जांबूनदमयं दिव्यं विमानं सूर्यसन्निभम् ।
दिव्याप्सरोभिः संपूर्णमन्नदो लभते ऽक्षयम् ॥
2.16.m: A giver of food attains an imperishable, celestial aerial chariot / made of gold, resembling the sun, filled with divine Apsarases.

2.16.s:
savyañjanaṃ tu yo dadyādahataṃ śrāddhakarmaṇi /
āyuḥ prākāśyamaiśvaryaṃ rūpaṃ ca labhate śubham //
2.16.d:
सव्यञ्जनं तु यो दद्यादहतं श्राद्धकर्मणि ।
आयुः प्राकाश्यमैश्वर्यं रूपं च लभते शुभम् ॥
2.16.m: He who gives [garments] unworn along with side dishes in an ancestral rite / obtains longevity, splendor, sovereignty, and auspicious beauty.

2.16.s:
yajñopavītaṃ yo dadyācchrāddhakāle tu yajñavit /
pāvanaṃ sarva viprāṇāṃ brahmadānasya tatphalam //
2.16.d:
यज्ञोपवीतं यो दद्याच्छ्राद्धकाले तु यज्ञवित् ।
पावनं सर्व विप्राणां ब्रह्मदानस्य तत्फलम् ॥
2.16.m: He who knows the sacrifice, who gives a sacrificial thread at the time of an ancestral rite, / which purifies all Brāhmaṇas, gains the fruit of the gift of Brahman.

2.16.s:
plutaṃ vipreṣu yo dadyācchrāddhakāle kamaḍalum /
madhukṣīrājyadadhibhirdātāramupatiṣṭhate //
2.16.d:
प्लुतं विप्रेषु यो दद्याच्छ्राद्धकाले कमडलुम् ।
मधुक्षीराज्यदधिभिर्दातारमुपतिष्ठते ॥
2.16.m: He who gives a flowing water-pot to the Brāhmaṇas at the time of an ancestral rite / is served with honey, milk, clarified butter, and curds.

2.16.s:
cakrāviddhaṃ ca yo dadyācchrāddhakāle kamaṇḍalum /
dhenuṃ salabhate divyāṃ payodāṃ sukhado hinīm //
2.16.d:
चक्राविद्धं च यो दद्याच्छ्राद्धकाले कमण्डलुम् ।
धेनुं सलभते दिव्यां पयोदां सुखदो हिनीम् ॥
2.16.m: He who gives a potter's-wheel-turned water-pot at the time of an ancestral rite / obtains a celestial cow, giving milk and easily milked, which bestows happiness.

2.16.s:
tūlapūrṇe ca yo dadyātpāduke śrāddhakarmaṇi /
śobhanaṃ labhate yānaṃ pādayoḥ sukhamedhate //
2.16.d:
तूलपूर्णे च यो दद्यात्पादुके श्राद्धकर्मणि ।
शोभनं लभते यानं पादयोः सुखमेधते ॥
2.16.m: He who gives sandals filled with cotton in an ancestral rite / obtains a splendid vehicle, and comfort for his feet increases.

2.16.s:
vyacanaṃ tālavṛntaṃ ca dattvā viprāya satkṛtam /
prāpnuyātsarvapuṣpāṇi sugandhīni mṛdūni ca //
2.16.d:
व्यचनं तालवृन्तं च दत्त्वा विप्राय सत्कृतम् ।
प्राप्नुयात्सर्वपुष्पाणि सुगन्धीनि मृदूनि च ॥
2.16.m: Having given an honored fan and a palm leaf to a Brāhmaṇa, / he obtains all manner of fragrant, soft flowers.

2.16.s:
śrāddhe hyupānahau dattvā brāhmaṇebhyaḥ sadā budhaḥ /
divyaṃ sa labhate yānaṃ vājiyuktaṃ navaṃ tathā //
2.16.d:
श्राद्धे ह्युपानहौ दत्त्वा ब्राह्मणेभ्यः सदा बुधः ।
दिव्यं स लभते यानं वाजियुक्तं नवं तथा ॥
2.16.m: The wise man who ever gives shoes to Brāhmaṇas in an ancestral rite / obtains a celestial, new carriage yoked with horses.

2.16.s:
śrāddhe chatraṃ tu yo dadyātpuṣpamālānvitaṃ tathā /
prāsādo hyuttamo bhūtvā gacchantamanugacchati //
2.16.d:
श्राद्धे छत्रं तु यो दद्यात्पुष्पमालान्वितं तथा ।
प्रासादो ह्युत्तमो भूत्वा गच्छन्तमनुगच्छति ॥
2.16.m: He who gives an umbrella adorned with garlands of flowers in an ancestral rite— / it becomes an excellent palace that follows him as he travels.

2.16.s:
śaraṇaṃ ratnasaṃpūrṇaṃ saśayyābhojanaṃ budhaḥ /
śrāddhe dattvā yatibhyastu nākapṛṣṭhe mahīyate //
2.16.d:
शरणं रत्नसंपूर्णं सशय्याभोजनं बुधः ।
श्राद्धे दत्त्वा यतिभ्यस्तु नाकपृष्ठे महीयते ॥
2.16.m: A wise man who gives a shelter filled with jewels, with a bed and food, / to ascetics in an ancestral rite is glorified on the back of heaven.

2.16.s:
suktāvaidūryavāsāṃsi ratnāni vividhāni ca /
vāhanāni ca divyāni prayutānyarbudāni ca //
2.16.d:
सुक्तावैदूर्यवासांसि रत्नानि विविधानि च ।
वाहनानि च दिव्यानि प्रयुतान्यर्बुदानि च ॥
2.16.m: Pearls, cat's-eye gems, garments, various jewels, / celestial vehicles by the millions and hundreds of millions,

2.16.s:
sumahadvyomagaṃ puṇyaṃ sarvakāmasamanvitam /
candrasūryanibhaṃ divyaṃ vimānaṃ labhate 'kṣayam //
2.16.d:
सुमहद्व्योमगं पुण्यं सर्वकामसमन्वितम् ।
चन्द्रसूर्यनिभं दिव्यं विमानं लभते ऽक्षयम् ॥
2.16.m: and an imperishable, celestial aerial chariot, immense, moving through the sky, holy, / endowed with every desire, resembling the sun and moon, he obtains.

2.16.s:
apsarobhiḥ parivṛtaṃ kāmagaṃ sumanojavam /
vasetsa tu vimānāgre stūyamānaḥ samantataḥ //
2.16.d:
अप्सरोभिः परिवृतं कामगं सुमनोजवम् ।
वसेत्स तु विमानाग्रे स्तूयमानः समन्ततः ॥
2.16.m: Surrounded by Apsarases, moving at will, swift as thought, / he dwells at the head of that aerial chariot, praised on all sides.

2.16.s:
divyaiḥpuṣpaiścitaścāhurdānānāṃ paramaṃ budhāḥ /
suślakṣmāni suvarṇāni śrāddhe pātrāṇi dāpayet //
2.16.d:
दिव्यैःपुष्पैश्चितश्चाहुर्दानानां परमं बुधाः ।
सुश्लक्ष्मानि सुवर्णानि श्राद्धे पात्राणि दापयेत् ॥
2.16.m: Filled with divine flowers—the wise declare this the supreme among gifts. / One should provide very smooth golden vessels in an ancestral rite.

2.16.s:
rasāstamupatiṣṭhanti bhakṣyaṃ saubhāgyameva ca /
tilānikṣūṃstathā śrāddhe dvijebhyaḥ saṃprayacchati //
2.16.d:
रसास्तमुपतिष्ठन्ति भक्ष्यं सौभाग्यमेव च ।
तिलानिक्षूंस्तथा श्राद्धे द्विजेभ्यः संप्रयच्छति ॥
2.16.m: Flavours attend upon him, as do food and good fortune, / who gives sesame seeds and sugarcanes to the twice-born in a śrāddha.

2.16.s:
mitrāṇi labhate loke strīṣu saubhāgyameva ca /
yaḥ pātraṃ taijasaṃ dadyānmanojña śrāddhabhojanaiḥ //
2.16.d:
मित्राणि लभते लोके स्त्रीषु सौभाग्यमेव च ।
यः पात्रं तैजसं दद्यान्मनोज्ञ श्राद्धभोजनैः ॥
2.16.m: He obtains friends in the world and good fortune among women, / who gives a metal vessel with pleasing śrāddha meals.

2.16.s:
pātraṃ bhavati kāmānā rūpasya ca dhanasya ca /
rājataṃ kāñcanaṃ vāpi yo dadyācchrāddhakarmaṇi //
2.16.d:
पात्रं भवति कामाना रूपस्य च धनस्य च ।
राजतं काञ्चनं वापि यो दद्याच्छ्राद्धकर्मणि ॥
2.16.m: He becomes a vessel of desires, of beauty, and of wealth, / whoever gives silver or gold in the rite of śrāddha.

2.16.s:
dānāttu labhate kāmānprākāśyaṃ dhanameva ca /
dhenuṃ śrāddhe tu yo dadyādgṛṣṭiṃ kumbhāpadohanīm //
2.16.d:
दानात्तु लभते कामान्प्राकाश्यं धनमेव च ।
धेनुं श्राद्धे तु यो दद्याद्गृष्टिं कुम्भापदोहनीम् ॥
2.16.m: From the gift he obtains desires, fame, and wealth, / who gives in a śrāddha a milch cow, a heifer that yields a pot of milk.

2.16.s:
gāvastamupatiṣṭhanti naraṃ puṣṭistathaiva ca /
dadyādyaḥ śiśire cāgniṃ bahukāṣṭhaṃ prayatnataḥ //
2.16.d:
गावस्तमुपतिष्ठन्ति नरं पुष्टिस्तथैव च ।
दद्याद्यः शिशिरे चाग्निं बहुकाष्ठं प्रयत्नतः ॥
2.16.m: Cattle attend upon that man, as does nourishment, / who zealously gives fire with abundant firewood in the cold season.

2.16.s:
kāyāgnidīptiṃ prākāśyaṃ saubhāgyaṃ tabhate naraḥ /
indhanāni tu yo dadyā ddvijebhyaḥ śiśirāgame //
2.16.d:
कायाग्निदीप्तिं प्राकाश्यं सौभाग्यं तभते नरः ।
इन्धनानि तु यो दद्या द्द्विजेभ्यः शिशिरागमे ॥
2.16.m: A man obtains brightness of bodily fire, brilliance, and good fortune, / who gives fuels to the twice-born at the onset of the cold season.

2.16.s:
nityaṃ jayati saṃgrāme śriyā juṣṭastu jāyate /
surabhīṇi ca mālyāni gandhavanti tathaiva ca //
2.16.d:
नित्यं जयति संग्रामे श्रिया जुष्टस्तु जायते ।
सुरभीणि च माल्यानि गन्धवन्ति तथैव च ॥
2.16.m: He is always victorious in battle and is born attended by splendour; / and having worshipped, he should hospitably bestow / fragrant garlands and scents upon worthy recipients in a śrāddha.

2.16.s:
pūjayitvā tu pātrebhyaḥ śrāddhe satkṛtya dāpayet /
gandhamālyaṃ mahātmānaṃ sukhāni vividhāni ca //
2.16.d:
पूजयित्वा तु पात्रेभ्यः श्राद्धे सत्कृत्य दापयेत् ।
गन्धमाल्यं महात्मानं सुखानि विविधानि च ॥
2.16.m: Scents, garlands, noble mind, and manifold pleasures, / as well as devoted young wives, attend upon the giver.

2.16.s:
dātāramupatiṣṭhanti yuvatyaśca pativratāḥ /
śayanāsanayānāni bhūmayo vāhanāni ca //
2.16.d:
दातारमुपतिष्ठन्ति युवत्यश्च पतिव्रताः ।
शयनासनयानानि भूमयो वाहनानि च ॥
2.16.m: Beds, seats, carriages, lands, and mounts—

2.16.s:
śrāddheṣvetāni yo dadyādaśvamedhaphalaṃ labhet /
śrāddhakāle guṇavati vipre vai samupasthite //
2.16.d:
श्राद्धेष्वेतानि यो दद्यादश्वमेधफलं लभेत् ।
श्राद्धकाले गुणवति विप्रे वै समुपस्थिते ॥
2.16.m: whoever gives these in śrāddhas obtains the fruit of an horse sacrifice. / When a virtuous Brahmin has arrived at the time of a śrāddha,

2.16.s:
iṣṭadravyaṃ ca yo dadyātsmṛtiṃ medhāṃ ca vindati /
sarpiḥpūrṇāni pātrāṇi śrāddhe satkṛtya dāpayet //
2.16.d:
इष्टद्रव्यं च यो दद्यात्स्मृतिं मेधां च विन्दति ।
सर्पिःपूर्णानि पात्राणि श्राद्धे सत्कृत्य दापयेत् ॥
2.16.m: he who gives the desired article obtains memory and intellect. / One should hospitably give vessels filled with clarified butter in a śrāddha;

2.16.s:
kumbhopadohagṛṣṭīnāṃ bahvīnāṃ phalamaśnute /
śrāddhe yathepsitaṃ dattvā puṇḍarīkaphalaṃ labhet //
2.16.d:
कुम्भोपदोहगृष्टीनां बह्वीनां फलमश्नुते ।
श्राद्धे यथेप्सितं दत्त्वा पुण्डरीकफलं लभेत् ॥
2.16.m: he enjoys the fruit of many heifers that yield a pot of milk. / Giving what is desired in a śrāddha, he obtains the fruit of a Puṇḍarīka sacrifice.

2.16.s:
vanaṃ puṣpaphalopetaṃ dattvā gosavamaśnute /
kūpārāmataḍāgāni kṣetragoṣṭhagṛhāṇi ca //
2.16.d:
वनं पुष्पफलोपेतं दत्त्वा गोसवमश्नुते ।
कूपारामतडागानि क्षेत्रगोष्ठगृहाणि च ॥
2.16.m: Giving a garden endowed with flowers and fruits, he enjoys [the fruit of] a Gosava. / Wells, groves, ponds, fields, cowpens, and houses—

2.16.s:
dattvā modanti te svarge nityamācandratārakam /
svāstīrṇaṃ śayanaṃ dattvā śrāddheratnavibhūṣitam //
2.16.d:
दत्त्वा मोदन्ति ते स्वर्गे नित्यमाचन्द्रतारकम् ।
स्वास्तीर्णं शयनं दत्त्वा श्राद्धेरत्नविभूषितम् ॥
2.16.m: having given these, they rejoice in heaven constantly as long as the moon and stars endure. / Having given a well-spread couch adorned with gems in a śrāddha,

2.16.s:
pitarastasya tuṣyanti svargalokaṃ samaśanute /
asmiṃlloke ca saṃpannaṃ syandanaṃ ca suvāhanaiḥ //
2.16.d:
पितरस्तस्य तुष्यन्ति स्वर्गलोकं समशनुते ।
अस्मिंल्लोके च संपन्नं स्यन्दनं च सुवाहनैः ॥
2.16.m: his ancestors are pleased and he attains the heavenly world. / And in this world, [he is honoured] with an opulent chariot with fine mounts,

2.16.s:
aṣṭābhiḥ pūjyate cātra dhanadhānyaiśca varddhate /
parṇakauśeyapaṭṭorṇe tathā prāvārakaṃbalau //
2.16.d:
अष्टाभिः पूज्यते चात्र धनधान्यैश्च वर्द्धते ।
पर्णकौशेयपट्टोर्णे तथा प्रावारकंबलौ ॥
2.16.m: and is honoured here by eight [persons?], and prospers with wealth and grain. / Silk made of bark, Chinese silk, woven silk, wool, and also mantle-wraps and blankets,

2.16.s:
ajinaṃ kāñcanaṃ paṭṭaṃ praveṇīṃ mṛgalomakam /
dadyādetāni viprāṇāṃ bhojayitvā yathāvidhi //
2.16.d:
अजिनं काञ्चनं पट्टं प्रवेणीं मृगलोमकम् ।
दद्यादेतानि विप्राणां भोजयित्वा यथाविधि ॥
2.16.m: deer-skin, gold, silk cloth, a braided cloth, and cloth of deer-hair— / having fed the Brahmins according to the rule, he should give these.

2.16.s:
prāpnoti śraddhadhānastu vājapeyaphalaṃ naraḥ /
bahubhāryāḥ surūpāśca putrā bhṛtyāśca kiṅkarāḥ //
2.16.d:
प्राप्नोति श्रद्धधानस्तु वाजपेयफलं नरः ।
बहुभार्याः सुरूपाश्च पुत्रा भृत्याश्च किङ्कराः ॥
2.16.m: The faithful man obtains the fruit of the Vājapeya sacrifice. / Many beautiful wives, sons, servants, and attendants,

2.16.s:
vaśe tiṣṭhanti bhūtāni loke cāsminnirāmayam /
kauśeyaṃ kṣaumakārpāsaṃ dukūlaṃ gahanaṃ tathā //
2.16.d:
वशे तिष्ठन्ति भूतानि लोके चास्मिन्निरामयम् ।
कौशेयं क्षौमकार्पासं दुकूलं गहनं तथा ॥
2.16.m: creatures remain under his control, and he is free from disease in this world. / Chinese silk, linen, cotton, fine silk, and also woven garments—

2.16.s:
śrāddhe caitāni yo dadyātkāmānāpnotyanuttamān /
alakṣmīṃ nāśayantyete tamaḥ sūryodayo yathā //
2.16.d:
श्राद्धे चैतानि यो दद्यात्कामानाप्नोत्यनुत्तमान् ।
अलक्ष्मीं नाशयन्त्येते तमः सूर्योदयो यथा ॥
2.16.m: he who gives these in a śrāddha obtains unsurpassed desires. / These destroy misfortune just as sunrise destroys darkness.

2.16.s:
bhrājate ya vimānāgre nakṣatreṣviva candramāḥ /
vāso hi sarvadaivatye sarvadevairabhiṣṭutam //
2.16.d:
भ्राजते य विमानाग्रे नक्षत्रेष्विव चन्द्रमाः ।
वासो हि सर्वदैवत्ये सर्वदेवैरभिष्टुतम् ॥
2.16.m: He shines at the forefront of a celestial aerial chariot like the moon among the constellations. / For clothing belongs to all deities and is praised by all the gods.

2.16.s:
vastrābhāve kriyā nāsti ya5dānatapāṃsi ca /
tasmādvastrāṇi deyāni śrāddhakāle tu nityaśaḥ //
2.16.d:
वस्त्राभावे क्रिया नास्ति य5दानतपांसि च ।
तस्माद्वस्त्राणि देयानि श्राद्धकाले तु नित्यशः ॥
2.16.m: In the absence of clothing, there is no ritual, [no] gift, and [no] austerities; / therefore, garments should constantly be given at the time of a śrāddha.

2.16.s:
tāni sarvāṇyavāpnoti śrāddhe dattvā tu mānavaḥ /
nityaśrāddhe tu yo dadyātprayatastatparāyaṇaḥ //
2.16.d:
तानि सर्वाण्यवाप्नोति श्राद्धे दत्त्वा तु मानवः ।
नित्यश्राद्धे तु यो दद्यात्प्रयतस्तत्परायणः ॥
2.16.m: A person obtains all of them having given them in a śrāddha. / He who, restrained and wholly dedicated, gives in the daily śrāddha,

2.16.s:
sarvakāmānavāpnoti rājyaṃ svage tathava ca /
sarvakāmasamṛddhasya yajñasya phalamaśnute //
2.16.d:
सर्वकामानवाप्नोति राज्यं स्वगे तथव च ।
सर्वकामसमृद्धस्य यज्ञस्य फलमश्नुते ॥
2.16.m: obtains all desires and sovereignty in heaven likewise; / he enjoys the fruit of a sacrifice complete with all desires.

2.16.s:
bhakṣyajātaṃ tu sukṛtaṃ svastikādyaṃ saśarkaram /
kṛsara madhusarpiśca payaḥ pāyasameva ca //
2.16.d:
भक्ष्यजातं तु सुकृतं स्वस्तिकाद्यं सशर्करम् ।
कृसर मधुसर्पिश्च पयः पायसमेव च ॥
2.16.m: Well-prepared pastries, svastika cakes and the like, with sugar, / kṛsara, honey, clarified butter, milk, and milk-rice,

2.16.s:
snigdhaprāyāśca yo dadyādagniṣṭomaphalaṃ labhet /
dadhigavyamasaṃsṛṣṭaṃ bhakṣyānnānāvidhāṃstathā //
2.16.d:
स्निग्धप्रायाश्च यो दद्यादग्निष्टोमफलं लभेत् ।
दधिगव्यमसंसृष्टं भक्ष्यान्नानाविधांस्तथा ॥
2.16.m: and he who gives mostly rich, unctuous foods obtains the fruit of an Agniṣṭoma. / Pure cow's curd, and likewise various kinds of edible foods—

2.16.s:
dattvā na śocate śrāddhe varṣāsu ca maghāsu ca /
ghṛtena bhojayedviprānghṛtaṃ bhūmau samutsṛjot //
2.16.d:
दत्त्वा न शोचते श्राद्धे वर्षासु च मघासु च ।
घृतेन भोजयेद्विप्रान्घृतं भूमौ समुत्सृजोत् ॥
2.16.m: having given these in a śrāddha in the rainy season and during the Maghās, he does not grieve. / He should feed the Brahmins with clarified butter, and cast clarified butter upon the ground.

2.16.s:
chāyāyāṃ hastinaścaiva dattvā śrāddhena śocate /
odanaṃ pāyasaṃ sarpirmadhumūlaphalāni ca //
2.16.d:
छायायां हस्तिनश्चैव दत्त्वा श्राद्धेन शोचते ।
ओदनं पायसं सर्पिर्मधुमूलफलानि च ॥
2.16.m: And having given [food] in the shadow of an elephant in a śrāddha, he does not grieve. / Boiled rice, milk-rice, clarified butter, honey, roots, and fruits,

2.16.s:
bhakṣyāṃśca vividhāndattvā paratreha ca modate /
śarkarākṣīrasaṃyuktāḥ pṛthukā nityamakṣayāḥ //
2.16.d:
भक्ष्यांश्च विविधान्दत्त्वा परत्रेह च मोदते ।
शर्कराक्षीरसंयुक्ताः पृथुका नित्यमक्षयाः ॥
2.16.m: and having given various pastries, he rejoices here and in the hereafter. / Parched flattened rice mixed with sugar and milk [brings] eternal and inexhaustible [merit].

2.16.s:
syāttu saṃvatsaraṃ prītiḥ śākairmāṃsarasena ca /
saktulājāstathāpūpāḥ kulmāṣā vyañjanaiḥ saha //
2.16.d:
स्यात्तु संवत्सरं प्रीतिः शाकैर्मांसरसेन च ।
सक्तुलाजास्तथापूपाः कुल्माषा व्यञ्जनैः सह ॥
2.16.m: There would be satisfaction for a year with vegetables and meat broth. / Barley-meal, parched grain, cakes, half-cooked pulse-gruel along with side dishes,

2.16.s:
sarpiḥsnigdhāni sarvāṇi dadhnā saṃskṛtya bhojayet /
śrāddheṣvetāni yo dadyātpadmaṃ sa labhate nidhim //
2.16.d:
सर्पिःस्निग्धानि सर्वाणि दध्ना संस्कृत्य भोजयेत् ।
श्राद्धेष्वेतानि यो दद्यात्पद्मं स लभते निधिम् ॥
2.16.m: all rich with clarified butter, prepared with curds, he should offer to feed them. / He who gives these in śrāddhas obtains the Padma treasure.

2.16.s:
navasasyāniyo dadyācchrāddhe satkṛtya yatnataḥ /
sarvabhogānavāpnoti pūjyate ca divaṃ gataḥ //
2.16.d:
नवसस्यानियो दद्याच्छ्राद्धे सत्कृत्य यत्नतः ।
सर्वभोगानवाप्नोति पूज्यते च दिवं गतः ॥
2.16.m: He who diligently gives new grains with hospitality in a śrāddha / obtains all pleasures and, gone to heaven, is honoured.

2.16.s:
bhakṣyabhojyāni peyāni coṣyaleṅyavarāṇi ca /
bhojanāgrāsanaṃ dattvā atithibhyaḥ kṛtāñjaliḥ //
2.16.d:
भक्ष्यभोज्यानि पेयानि चोष्यलेङ्यवराणि च ।
भोजनाग्रासनं दत्त्वा अतिथिभ्यः कृताञ्जलिः ॥
2.16.m: Foods to chew, to eat, to drink, to suck, and excellent things to lick— / having given the foremost seat for dining to guests with palms folded in reverence,

2.16.s:
sarvayajñakratūnāṃ hi phalaṃ prāpnotyanuttamam /
kṣipramatyuṣṇamakliṣṭaṃ dadyādannaṃ bubhukṣate //
2.16.d:
सर्वयज्ञक्रतूनां हि फलं प्राप्नोत्यनुत्तमम् ।
क्षिप्रमत्युष्णमक्लिष्टं दद्यादन्नं बुभुक्षते ॥
2.16.m: he obtains the unsurpassed fruit of all sacrifices and rites. / One should quickly and attentively give hot, unblemished food to one who is hungry,

2.16.s:
savyañjanaṃ tathā snigdhaṃ bhaktyā satkṛtya yatnataḥ /
taruṇādityasaṃkāśaṃ vimānaṃ haṃsavāhanam //
2.16.d:
सव्यञ्जनं तथा स्निग्धं भक्त्या सत्कृत्य यत्नतः ।
तरुणादित्यसंकाशं विमानं हंसवाहनम् ॥
2.16.m: along with side dishes and rich, with devotion and zeal. / [He obtains] an aerial chariot resembling the morning sun, drawn by swans;

2.16.s:
annado labhate nityaṃ kanyākoṭīstathaiva ca /
annadānātparaṃ dānaṃ nānyatkiñcittu vidyate //
2.16.d:
अन्नदो लभते नित्यं कन्याकोटीस्तथैव च ।
अन्नदानात्परं दानं नान्यत्किञ्चित्तु विद्यते ॥
2.16.m: the giver of food constantly obtains crores of maiden-attendants. / There is no other gift greater than the gift of food.

2.16.s:
annādbhūtāni jāyante jīvanti prabhavanti ca /
jīvadānātparaṃ dānaṃ nānyatkiñcana vidyate //
2.16.d:
अन्नाद्भूतानि जायन्ते जीवन्ति प्रभवन्ति च ।
जीवदानात्परं दानं नान्यत्किञ्चन विद्यते ॥
2.16.m: From food beings are born, live, and thrive. / There is no other gift greater than the gift of life.

2.16.s:
annāllokāḥ pratiṣṭhanti lokadānasya tatphalam /
annaṃ prajāpatiḥ sākṣātte na sarvamidaṃ tatam //
2.16.d:
अन्नाल्लोकाः प्रतिष्ठन्ति लोकदानस्य तत्फलम् ।
अन्नं प्रजापतिः साक्षात्ते न सर्वमिदं ततम् ॥
2.16.m: From food the worlds endure; that is the fruit of giving a world. / Food is Prajāpati directly; by him all this is pervaded.

2.16.s:
tasmādannasamaṃ dānaṃ na bhūtaṃ na bhaviṣyati /
yāni ratnāni medinyāṃ vāhanāni striyastathā //
2.16.d:
तस्मादन्नसमं दानं न भूतं न भविष्यति ।
यानि रत्नानि मेदिन्यां वाहनानि स्त्रियस्तथा ॥
2.16.m: Therefore, equal to the gift of food there has never been nor will there ever be. / Whatever gems there are on earth, vehicles, and women—

2.16.s:
kṣipraṃ prāpnoti tatsarvaṃ pitṛbhaktastu yo naraḥ /
pratiśrayaṃ ca yo dadyādatithibyaḥ kṛtāñjaliḥ //
2.16.d:
क्षिप्रं प्राप्नोति तत्सर्वं पितृभक्तस्तु यो नरः ।
प्रतिश्रयं च यो दद्यादतिथिब्यः कृताञ्जलिः ॥
2.16.m: the man devoted to the ancestors quickly obtains all of that. / And he who gives shelter to guests with folded hands,

2.16.s:
devāstaṃ saṃpratīcchanti divyātithyaiḥ sahasraśaḥ /
sarvāṇyetāni yo dadyātpṛthivyāmekarāḍbhavet //
2.16.d:
देवास्तं संप्रतीच्छन्ति दिव्यातिथ्यैः सहस्रशः ।
सर्वाण्येतानि यो दद्यात्पृथिव्यामेकराड्भवेत् ॥
2.16.m: the gods welcome him with thousands of divine hospitalities. / He who gives all of these becomes the sole sovereign of the earth.

2.16.s:
tribhirdvābhyāmathaikena dānena tu sukhī bhadet /
dānāni paramo dharmaḥ sadbhiḥ satkṛtya pūjitaḥ //
2.16.d:
त्रिभिर्द्वाभ्यामथैकेन दानेन तु सुखी भदेत् ।
दानानि परमो धर्मः सद्भिः सत्कृत्य पूजितः ॥
2.16.m: By three, by two, or even by a single gift he becomes happy. / Gifts are the supreme dharma, honoured and venerated by the virtuous.

2.16.s:
trailokyasyā dhipatyaṃ hi dānenaiva dhruvaṃ sthitam /
arājā labhate rājyamadhanaścottamaṃ dhanam /
kṣīṇāyurlabhate cāyuḥ pitṛbhaktaḥ sadā naraḥ //
iti śrībrahmāṇḍe mahāpurāṇe vāyuprokte madhyabhāge tṛtīya upoddhātapāde
śrāddhakalpe dānapraśaṃsā nāma ṣoḍaśo 'dhyāyaḥ // 16//
2.16.d:
त्रैलोक्यस्या धिपत्यं हि दानेनैव ध्रुवं स्थितम् ।
अराजा लभते राज्यमधनश्चोत्तमं धनम् ।
क्षीणायुर्लभते चायुः पितृभक्तः सदा नरः ॥
इति श्रीब्रह्माण्डे महापुराणे वायुप्रोक्ते मध्यभागे तृतीय उपोद्धातपादे
श्राद्धकल्पे दानप्रशंसा नाम षोडशो ऽध्यायः ॥ 16॥
2.16.m:
For sovereignty over the three worlds is firmly established through gift alone. / A non-king obtains a kingdom, a poor man obtains excellent wealth, / and a man whose life is diminished obtains long life, when always devoted to the ancestors.

Thus ends the sixteenth chapter, entitled 'Praise of Gifts in the Ritual of Śrāddha', in the third part, the Upoddhātapāda, in the middle division of the glorious Brahmāṇḍa Mahāpurāṇa spoken by Vāyu.

2.17.s:
bṛhaspatiruvāca
ata ūrddhvaṃ pravakṣyāmi śrāddhakarmaṇi pūjitam /
kāmyaṃ naimittikājasraṃ śrāddhakarmaṇi nityaśaḥ //
2.17.d:
बृहस्पतिरुवाच
अत ऊर्द्ध्वं प्रवक्ष्यामि श्राद्धकर्मणि पूजितम् ।
काम्यं नैमित्तिकाजस्रं श्राद्धकर्मणि नित्यशः ॥
2.17.m: Bṛhaspati said: / Hereafter I shall declare what is honoured in the rite of śrāddha: / the optional, the occasional, and the constant in the regular rite of śrāddha.

2.17.s:
putradāranimittāḥ syuraṣṭakāstisna eva tu /
kṛṣṇapakṣe variṣṭhā hi pūrvākhaṇḍaladevatā //
2.17.d:
पुत्रदारनिमित्ताः स्युरष्टकास्तिस्न एव तु ।
कृष्णपक्षे वरिष्ठा हि पूर्वाखण्डलदेवता ॥
2.17.m: There are three Aṣṭakās having sons and wives as their occasion; / in the dark fortnight, they are indeed the best, having deities in the earlier half.

2.17.s:
prājāpatyā dvitīyā syāttṛtīyā vaiśvadevikā /
ādyāpūpaiḥ sadākāryā māṃsairanyā sadā bhavet //
2.17.d:
प्राजापत्या द्वितीया स्यात्तृतीया वैश्वदेविका ।
आद्यापूपैः सदाकार्या मांसैरन्या सदा भवेत् ॥
2.17.m: The second [aṣṭakā] belongs to Prajāpati; the third belongs to the Viśvedevas. / The first must always be performed with cakes; the other should always be with meats;

2.17.s:
śākaiḥ kāryā tṛtīyā syādevaṃ dravyagato vidhiḥ /
atrāpīṣṭaṃ pitṝṇāṃ vai nityameva vidhīyate //
2.17.d:
शाकैः कार्या तृतीया स्यादेवं द्रव्यगतो विधिः ।
अत्रापीष्टं पितॄणां वै नित्यमेव विधीयते ॥
2.17.m: the third should be performed with vegetables: such is the rule regarding the materials. / In this too, what is desired by the ancestors is prescribed continuously.

2.17.s:
yā cāpyanyā caturthī syāttāṃ ca kuryādviśeṣataḥ /
āsu śrāddhaṃ budhaḥ kurvansarvasvenāpi nityaśaḥ //
2.17.d:
या चाप्यन्या चतुर्थी स्यात्तां च कुर्याद्विशेषतः ।
आसु श्राद्धं बुधः कुर्वन्सर्वस्वेनापि नित्यशः ॥
2.17.m: And whatever fourth [aṣṭakā] there may be, one should perform that especially. / A wise man performing the śrāddha on these, constantly, even with all his wealth,

2.17.s:
kṣipramāpnoti hi śreyaḥ paratreha ca modate /
pitaraḥ parvakāleṣu tithikāleṣu devatāḥ //
2.17.d:
क्षिप्रमाप्नोति हि श्रेयः परत्रेह च मोदते ।
पितरः पर्वकालेषु तिथिकालेषु देवताः ॥
2.17.m: swiftly attains the highest good and rejoices here and in the hereafter. / The ancestors [arrive] at the parvan times, the deities at the tithi times;

2.17.s:
sarveṣu puruṣā yānti nipātamiva dhenavaḥ /
māsāṃte pratigaccheyuraṣṭakāsu hyapūjitāḥ //
2.17.d:
सर्वेषु पुरुषा यान्ति निपातमिव धेनवः ।
मासांते प्रतिगच्छेयुरष्टकासु ह्यपूजिताः ॥
2.17.m: men go to all of them, as cows to a watering place. / If unhonored on the aṣṭakās, they return at the end of the month;

2.17.s:
moghāstasya bhavantyāśāḥ paratreha ca sarvaśaḥ /
pūjakānāṃ samutkarṣo nāstikānāmadhogatiḥ //
2.17.d:
मोघास्तस्य भवन्त्याशाः परत्रेह च सर्वशः ।
पूजकानां समुत्कर्षो नास्तिकानामधोगतिः ॥
2.17.m: his hopes become futile in every respect, both here and in the hereafter. / The worshippers attain preeminence; the unbelievers sink to a low state.

2.17.s:
devāstu dāyino yānti tiryaggacchantyadāyinaḥ /
puṣṭiṃ prajāṃ smṛtiṃ medhāṃ putrānaiśvaryameva ca //
2.17.d:
देवास्तु दायिनो यान्ति तिर्यग्गच्छन्त्यदायिनः ।
पुष्टिं प्रजां स्मृतिं मेधां पुत्रानैश्वर्यमेव च ॥
2.17.m: The givers go to the gods; the non-givers go to the beasts. / Nourishment, offspring, memory, intellect, sons, and sovereign power—

2.17.s:
kurvāṇaḥ pūjanaṃ cāsu sarvaṃ pūrṇaṃ samaśnute /
pratipaddhanalābhāya labdhaṃ cāsya na naśyati //
2.17.d:
कुर्वाणः पूजनं चासु सर्वं पूर्णं समश्नुते ।
प्रतिपद्धनलाभाय लब्धं चास्य न नश्यति ॥
2.17.m: performing worship on these, one attains all of them in full. / [A śrāddha on] the first day leads to the acquisition of wealth, and what is acquired is not lost.

2.17.s:
dvitīyāyāṃ tu yaḥ kuryāddvipadādhiṃpatir bhavet /
varārthināṃ tṛtīyā tu śatrughnī pāpanāśinī //
2.17.d:
द्वितीयायां तु यः कुर्याद्द्विपदाधिंपतिर् भवेत् ।
वरार्थिनां तृतीया तु शत्रुघ्नी पापनाशिनी ॥
2.17.m: He who performs it on the second day becomes the lord of men. / But the third day, for those desiring boons, destroys enemies and ruins sin.

2.17.s:
caturthyāṃ tu prakurvāṇaḥ śatrucchidrāṇi paśyati /
pañcamyāṃ cāpikurvāṇaḥ prāpnoti mahatīṃ śriyam //
2.17.d:
चतुर्थ्यां तु प्रकुर्वाणः शत्रुच्छिद्राणि पश्यति ।
पञ्चम्यां चापिकुर्वाणः प्राप्नोति महतीं श्रियम् ॥
2.17.m: Performing it on the fourth day, he perceives the weaknesses of his enemies. / And performing it on the fifth, he attains great fortune.

2.17.s:
ṣaṣṭhyāṃ śrāddhāni kurvāṇaḥ saṃpūjyaḥ syātprayatnataḥ /
kurute yastu saptamyāṃ śrāddhāni satataṃ naraḥ //
2.17.d:
षष्ठ्यां श्राद्धानि कुर्वाणः संपूज्यः स्यात्प्रयत्नतः ।
कुरुते यस्तु सप्तम्यां श्राद्धानि सततं नरः ॥
2.17.m: Performing śrāddhas on the sixth day, he becomes worthy of worship with effort. / But the man who always performs śrāddhas on the seventh day

2.17.s:
mahīśatvamavāpnoti gaṇānāṃ cādhipo bhavet /
saṃpūrṇāmṛddhimāpnoti yo 'ṣṭamyāṃ kurute naraḥ //
2.17.d:
महीशत्वमवाप्नोति गणानां चाधिपो भवेत् ।
संपूर्णामृद्धिमाप्नोति यो ऽष्टम्यां कुरुते नरः ॥
2.17.m: attains kingship over the earth and becomes a ruler of hosts. / The man who performs it on the eighth day attains complete prosperity.

2.17.s:
śrāddhaṃ navamyāṃ karttavyamaiśvaryaṃ strīśca kāṅkṣatā /
kurvandaśamyāṃ tu naro brāhmīṃ śriyamavāpnuyāt //
2.17.d:
श्राद्धं नवम्यां कर्त्तव्यमैश्वर्यं स्त्रीश्च काङ्क्षता ।
कुर्वन्दशम्यां तु नरो ब्राह्मीं श्रियमवाप्नुयात् ॥
2.17.m: A śrāddha should be performed on the ninth day by one desiring sovereignty and women. / But performing it on the tenth, a man attains the fortune of Brahman;

2.17.s:
vedāṃścaivāpnuyātsarvānviprāṇāṃ samatāṃ vrajet /
ekādaśyāṃ paraṃ dānamaiśvarya satataṃ tathā //
2.17.d:
वेदांश्चैवाप्नुयात्सर्वान्विप्राणां समतां व्रजेत् ।
एकादश्यां परं दानमैश्वर्य सततं तथा ॥
2.17.m: he obtains all the Vedas and achieves equality with the brahmins. / On the eleventh day [it yields] supreme generosity and constant sovereignty;

2.17.s:
dvādaśyāṃ jayalābhaṃ ca rājyamāyurvasūni ca /
prajāvṛddhiṃ paśūnmedhāṃ svātantryaṃ puṣṭimuttamām //
2.17.d:
द्वादश्यां जयलाभं च राज्यमायुर्वसूनि च ।
प्रजावृद्धिं पशून्मेधां स्वातन्त्र्यं पुष्टिमुत्तमाम् ॥
2.17.m: on the twelfth day, obtaining victory, kingship, longevity, and wealth, / increase of offspring, cattle, intellect, independence, and excellent nourishment.

2.17.s:
dīrghamāyurathaiśvaryaṃ kurvāṇastu trayodaśīm /
yuvānaśca gṛhe yasya mṛtāstebhyaḥ pradāpayet //
2.17.d:
दीर्घमायुरथैश्वर्यं कुर्वाणस्तु त्रयोदशीम् ।
युवानश्च गृहे यस्य मृतास्तेभ्यः प्रदापयेत् ॥
2.17.m: He who performs it on the thirteenth day [gains] long life and sovereignty. / And those who have died young in one's house, to them he should offer [on that day].

2.17.s:
śastreṇa vā hatā ye ca teṣāṃ dadyāccaturdaśīm /
amāvāsyāṃ prayatnena śrāddhaṃ kuryātsadā śuciḥ //
2.17.d:
शस्त्रेण वा हता ये च तेषां दद्याच्चतुर्दशीम् ।
अमावास्यां प्रयत्नेन श्राद्धं कुर्यात्सदा शुचिः ॥
2.17.m: Or to those who have been killed by a weapon, he should make an offering on the fourteenth day. / On the new-moon day, being always purified, he should carefully perform the śrāddha.

2.17.s:
sarvakāmānavāpnoti svargaṃ cānantamaśnute /
tathāviṣamajātānāṃ yamalānāṃ ca sarvaśaḥ //
2.17.d:
सर्वकामानवाप्नोति स्वर्गं चानन्तमश्नुते ।
तथाविषमजातानां यमलानां च सर्वशः ॥
2.17.m: He attains all desires and enjoys endless heaven. / Likewise, for those born unevenly and twins, in every manner,

2.17.s:
śrāddhaṃ dadyādamāvāsyāṃ sarvakāmānavāpnuyāt /
maghāsu kurvañchrāddhāni sarvakāmānavāpnuyāt //
2.17.d:
श्राद्धं दद्यादमावास्यां सर्वकामानवाप्नुयात् ।
मघासु कुर्वञ्छ्राद्धानि सर्वकामानवाप्नुयात् ॥
2.17.m: one should offer śrāddha on the new-moon day: he attains all desires. / Performing śrāddhas under [the asterism] Maghā, he attains all desires.

2.17.s:
pratyakṣamarcitāstena bhavanti pitarastadā /
pitṛdavā maghā yasmāttasmāttāsvakṣayaṃ smṛtam //
iti śrībrahmāṇḍe mahāpurāṇe vāyuprokte madhyabhāge tṛtīya upoddhātapāde
śrāddhakalpe tithiśrāddhavarṇanaṃ nāma saptadaśo 'dhyāyaḥ // 17//
2.17.d:
प्रत्यक्षमर्चितास्तेन भवन्ति पितरस्तदा ।
पितृदवा मघा यस्मात्तस्मात्तास्वक्षयं स्मृतम् ॥
इति श्रीब्रह्माण्डे महापुराणे वायुप्रोक्ते मध्यभागे तृतीय उपोद्धातपादे
श्राद्धकल्पे तिथिश्राद्धवर्णनं नाम सप्तदशो ऽध्यायः ॥ 17॥
2.17.m:
The ancestors are then visibly honored by him. / Because Maghā belongs to the ancestors, what is [offered] under it is known to be inexhaustible.

Thus ends the seventeenth chapter, named 'Description of the Tithi Śrāddhas', in the ritual of śrāddha, in the third section, the Upoddhātapāda, in the middle part of the glorious and great Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa proclaimed by Vāyu. // 17

2.18.s:
bṛhaspatiruvāca
yamastu yāni śrāddhāni provāca śaśabindave /
tāni me śṛṇu kāryāṇi nakṣatreṣu pṛthak pṛthak //
2.18.d:
बृहस्पतिरुवाच
यमस्तु यानि श्राद्धानि प्रोवाच शशबिन्दवे ।
तानि मे शृणु कार्याणि नक्षत्रेषु पृथक् पृथक् ॥
2.18.m: Bṛhaspati said: / The śrāddhas which Yama declared to Śaśabindu, / hear from me those rites to be performed individually under the lunar mansions.

2.18.s:
śrāddhaṃ yaḥ kṛttikāyogaṃ kurute satataṃ naraḥ /
agnīnādhāya sa svarge rājate sudṛḍhavrataḥ //
2.18.d:
श्राद्धं यः कृत्तिकायोगं कुरुते सततं नरः ।
अग्नीनाधाय स स्वर्गे राजते सुदृढव्रतः ॥
2.18.m: The man who continually performs a śrāddha in conjunction with Kṛttikā, / having established the fires, shines in heaven, steadfast in his vows.

2.18.s:
apatyakāmo rohiṇyāṃ saumye tejasvinā bhavet /
prāyaśaḥ krūrakarmāṇi ārdrāyāṃ śrāddhamācaran //
2.18.d:
अपत्यकामो रोहिण्यां सौम्ये तेजस्विना भवेत् ।
प्रायशः क्रूरकर्माणि आर्द्रायां श्राद्धमाचरन् ॥
2.18.m: Desiring offspring, [he should perform it] under Rohiṇī; under Saumya (Mṛgaśīrṣa), he becomes full of brilliance; / usually [performing] cruel acts, performing a śrāddha under Ārdrā;

2.18.s:
kṣetrabhāgī bhavetputrī śrāddhaṃ kṛtvā punarvasau /
puṣṭikāmaḥ punastiṣye śrāddhaṃ kurvīta mānavaḥ //
2.18.d:
क्षेत्रभागी भवेत्पुत्री श्राद्धं कृत्वा पुनर्वसौ ।
पुष्टिकामः पुनस्तिष्ये श्राद्धं कुर्वीत मानवः ॥
2.18.m: having performed a śrāddha under Punarvasu, he becomes an owner of land and possesses sons; / desiring nourishment, a man should again perform a śrāddha under Tiṣya (Puṣya).

2.18.s:
āśleṣāsu pitṝnarcanvīrānputrānavāpnuyāt /
jātīnāṃ bhavati śreṣṭho maghāsu śrāddhamācaran //
2.18.d:
आश्लेषासु पितॄनर्चन्वीरान्पुत्रानवाप्नुयात् ।
जातीनां भवति श्रेष्ठो मघासु श्राद्धमाचरन् ॥
2.18.m: Worshipping the ancestors under the Āśleṣās, he attains heroic sons; / performing a śrāddha under Maghā, he becomes the best among his kinsmen.

2.18.s:
phālgunīṣu pitṝnarcansaubhāgyaṃ labhate naraḥ /
pradānaśīlaḥ sāpatya uttarāsu karoti yaḥ //
2.18.d:
फाल्गुनीषु पितॄनर्चन्सौभाग्यं लभते नरः ।
प्रदानशीलः सापत्य उत्तरासु करोति यः ॥
2.18.m: Worshipping the ancestors under the Phālgunīs, a man obtains good fortune; / he who performs it under Uttarā (Phālgunī) becomes generous and possesses offspring.

2.18.s:
saṃsatsu mukhyo bhavati haste 'bhyarcya pitṝnapi /
citrāyāṃ caiva yaḥ kuryātpaśyedrūpavataḥ sutān //
2.18.d:
संसत्सु मुख्यो भवति हस्ते ऽभ्यर्च्य पितॄनपि ।
चित्रायां चैव यः कुर्यात्पश्येद्रूपवतः सुतान् ॥
2.18.m: Worshipping the ancestors under Hasta, he becomes foremost in assemblies; / and he who performs it under Citrā sees handsome sons.

2.18.s:
svātinā caiva yaḥ kuryādvāṇijye lābhamāpnuyāt /
putrārthī tu viśākhāsu śrāddhamīheta mālavaḥ //
2.18.d:
स्वातिना चैव यः कुर्याद्वाणिज्ये लाभमाप्नुयात् ।
पुत्रार्थी तु विशाखासु श्राद्धमीहेत मालवः ॥
2.18.m: And he who performs it under Svāti obtains profit in trade; / desiring sons, a man should strive for a śrāddha under the Viśākhās.

2.18.s:
anurādhāsu kurvāṇo naraścakraṃ pravarttayet /
ādhipatyaṃ bhavecchreṣṭhaṃ jyeṣṭhāyāṃ satataṃ tu yaḥ //
2.18.d:
अनुराधासु कुर्वाणो नरश्चक्रं प्रवर्त्तयेत् ।
आधिपत्यं भवेच्छ्रेष्ठं ज्येष्ठायां सततं तु यः ॥
2.18.m: A man performing it under Anurādhā sets his wheel [of sovereignty] in motion; / he who [performs it] constantly under Jyeṣṭhā attains excellent dominion.

2.18.s:
mūlenārogyamicchanti hyāṣāḍhāsu mahadyaśaḥ /
uttarāsu tu kurvāṇo vītaśoko bhavennaraḥ //
2.18.d:
मूलेनारोग्यमिच्छन्ति ह्याषाढासु महद्यशः ।
उत्तरासु तु कुर्वाणो वीतशोको भवेन्नरः ॥
2.18.m: They desire freedom from disease through Mūla, and great fame under the Āṣāḍhās; / performing it under Uttarā (Āṣāḍhā), a man becomes free from sorrow.

2.18.s:
śravaṇena tu lokeṣu prāpnuyātparamāṃ gatim /
rājyabhāgī dhaniṣṭhāsu prāpnuyā dvipulaṃ dhanam //
2.18.d:
श्रवणेन तु लोकेषु प्राप्नुयात्परमां गतिम् ।
राज्यभागी धनिष्ठासु प्राप्नुया द्विपुलं धनम् ॥
2.18.m: Under Śravaṇa he attains the supreme state among the worlds; / under Dhaniṣṭhā he shares in kingship and obtains abundant wealth.
Having conquered the worlds through śrāddha, he obtains the Vedas with their auxiliary limbs; / performing it under the asterism belonging to Varuṇa (Śatabhiṣaj), a physician attains perfection.

2.18.s:
pūrvaprauṣṭha pade kurvanvindetājīvikānbahūn /
uttarāsvanatikramya vindedgā vai sahasraśaḥ //
2.18.d:
पूर्वप्रौष्ठ पदे कुर्वन्विन्देताजीविकान्बहून् ।
उत्तरास्वनतिक्रम्य विन्देद्गा वै सहस्रशः ॥
2.18.m: Performing it under Pūrvaprauṣṭhapadā, he finds many sources of livelihood; / not passing over the Uttarās (Uttaraproṣṭhapadā), he finds cows by the thousands.

2.18.s:
bahukupyakṛtaṃ dravyaṃ vindetkurvansurevatīm /
aśvānaśvayujā bhakto bharaṇyāṃ sādhusattamaḥ //
2.18.d:
बहुकुप्यकृतं द्रव्यं विन्देत्कुर्वन्सुरेवतीम् ।
अश्वानश्वयुजा भक्तो भरण्यां साधुसत्तमः ॥
2.18.m: Performing it under Revatī, he finds wealth consisting of abundant base metals; / devoted under Aśvayuj (Aśvinī), he attains horses; under Bharaṇī, he becomes the best of the virtuous.

2.18.s:
imaṃ śrāddhavidhiṃ kurvañchaśabindurmahīmimām /
kṛtsnāṃ balena so 'kliṣṭho labhdhvā ca praśaśāsa ha //
iti śrī brahāmāṇḍe mahāpurāṇe vāyuprokte madhyabhāge tṛtīya upoddhātapāde
śrāddhakalpe nakṣatraśrāddhaṃ nāma aṣṭādaśo 'dhyāyaḥ // 18//
2.18.d:
इमं श्राद्धविधिं कुर्वञ्छशबिन्दुर्महीमिमाम् ।
कृत्स्नां बलेन सो ऽक्लिष्ठो लभ्ध्वा च प्रशशास ह ॥
इति श्री ब्रहामाण्डे महापुराणे वायुप्रोक्ते मध्यभागे तृतीय उपोद्धातपादे
श्राद्धकल्पे नक्षत्रश्राद्धं नाम अष्टादशो ऽध्यायः ॥ 18॥
2.18.m:
Performing this rule of śrāddha, Śaśabindu, without difficulty, / having obtained this entire earth by his might, ruled it.

Thus ends the eighteenth chapter, named 'Nakṣatra Śrāddha', in the ritual of śrāddha, in the third section, the Upoddhātapāda, in the middle part of the glorious and great Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa proclaimed by Vāyu. // 18

2.19.s:
śaṃyuruvāca
kiṃ sviddattaṃ pitṝṇāṃ tu tṛptidaṃ vadatāṃ vara /
kiṃsvitsyāccirarātrāya kiṃ vānantyāya kalpate //
2.19.d:
शंयुरुवाच
किं स्विद्दत्तं पितॄणां तु तृप्तिदं वदतां वर ।
किंस्वित्स्याच्चिररात्राय किं वानन्त्याय कल्पते ॥
2.19.m: Śaṃyu said: / What offered to the ancestors gives satisfaction, O best of speakers? / What would last for a long night, or what leads to infinity?

2.19.s:
bṛhaspatiruvāca
havīṣi śrāddhakalpe tu yāni śrāddhavido viduḥ /
tāni me śṛṇu sarvāṇi phalaṃ caiṣāṃ yathātatham //
2.19.d:
बृहस्पतिरुवाच
हवीषि श्राद्धकल्पे तु यानि श्राद्धविदो विदुः ।
तानि मे शृणु सर्वाणि फलं चैषां यथातथम् ॥
2.19.m: Bṛhaspati said: / Hear from me all those oblations in the śrāddha ritual that the knowers of śrāddha know, / and their fruit as it truly is.

2.19.s:
tilairvrīhiyavaimāṣairadbhirmūlaphalaistathā /
dattena māsaṃ prīyante śrāddhena hi pitāmahāḥ //
2.19.d:
तिलैर्व्रीहियवैमाषैरद्भिर्मूलफलैस्तथा ।
दत्तेन मासं प्रीयन्ते श्राद्धेन हि पितामहाः ॥
2.19.m: By sesame seeds, rice, barley, beans, water, and roots and fruits / offered in a śrāddha, the grandfathers are pleased for a month.

2.19.s:
matsyaiḥ prīṇanti dvau māsau trīnmāsānhāriṇena tu /
śāśena caturo māsānpañca prīṇāti śākunaiḥ //
2.19.d:
मत्स्यैः प्रीणन्ति द्वौ मासौ त्रीन्मासान्हारिणेन तु ।
शाशेन चतुरो मासान्पञ्च प्रीणाति शाकुनैः ॥
2.19.m: With fish they are pleased for two months; for three months with venison; / with hare for four months; with birds he pleases them for five.

2.19.s:
vārāheṇa tu ṣaṇmāsāñchāgalaṃ saptamāsikam /
aṣṭamāsikamityuktaṃ yacca pārvatakaṃ bhavet //
2.19.d:
वाराहेण तु षण्मासाञ्छागलं सप्तमासिकम् ।
अष्टमासिकमित्युक्तं यच्च पार्वतकं भवेत् ॥
2.19.m: With wild boar for six months; that of goat lasts seven months; / that which comes from mountain [game] is said to last eight months.

2.19.s:
rauraveṇa tu prīyante nava māsānpitāmahāḥ /
gavayasya tu māṃsena tṛptiḥ syāddaśamāsikī //
2.19.d:
रौरवेण तु प्रीयन्ते नव मासान्पितामहाः ।
गवयस्य तु मांसेन तृप्तिः स्याद्दशमासिकी ॥
2.19.m: With the meat of the ruru deer the grandfathers are pleased for nine months; / with the meat of the gayal (gavaya) the satisfaction lasts ten months;

2.19.s:
aurabhreṇa ca māṃsena māsānekādaśaiva tu /
śrāddhe ca tṛptidaṃ gavyaṃ payaḥ saṃvatsaraṃ dvijāḥ //
2.19.d:
औरभ्रेण च मांसेन मासानेकादशैव तु ।
श्राद्धे च तृप्तिदं गव्यं पयः संवत्सरं द्विजाः ॥
2.19.m: and with mutton for eleven months; / and in a śrāddha, cows' milk gives satisfaction for a year, O twice-born.

2.19.s:
ānantyāya bhavettadvatkhaḍgamāṃsaṃ pitṛkṣaye /
pāyasaṃ madhusarpirbhyāṃ chāyāyāṃ kuñjarasya ca //
2.19.d:
आनन्त्याय भवेत्तद्वत्खड्गमांसं पितृक्षये ।
पायसं मधुसर्पिर्भ्यां छायायां कुञ्जरस्य च ॥
2.19.m: Likewise, rhinoceros meat leads to infinity on the anniversary of the father's death, / and rice cooked in milk with honey and clarified butter, in the shadow of an elephant.

2.19.s:
kṛṣṇacchāgasya māsena tṛptirbhavati śāśvatī /
atra gāthāḥ pitṛgītāḥ kīrtayanti purāvidaḥ //
2.19.d:
कृष्णच्छागस्य मासेन तृप्तिर्भवति शाश्वती ।
अत्र गाथाः पितृगीताः कीर्तयन्ति पुराविदः ॥
2.19.m:
With the meat of a black goat, there is eternal satisfaction.
On this subject, those learned in the past recite verses sung by the ancestors:

2.19.s:
tāste 'haṃ kīrttayiṣyāmi yathāvatsannibodha me /
api naḥ sa kule yāyādyo no dadyāt trayodaśīm //
2.19.d:
तास्ते ऽहं कीर्त्तयिष्यामि यथावत्सन्निबोध मे ।
अपि नः स कुले यायाद्यो नो दद्यात् त्रयोदशीम् ॥
2.19.m:
‘I shall recite them to you as they truly are; understand [them] from me:
May that man be born into our lineage who would offer to us on the thirteenth [tithi]

2.19.s:
ājena sarvalohena varṣāsu ca maghāsu ca /
eṣṭavyā bahavaḥ putrā yadyeko 'pi gayāṃ vrajet /
gaurīṃ vāpyudvahedbhāryāṃ nālaṃ vā vṛṣamutsṛjet //
2.19.d:
आजेन सर्वलोहेन वर्षासु च मघासु च ।
एष्टव्या बहवः पुत्रा यद्येको ऽपि गयां व्रजेत् ।
गौरीं वाप्युद्वहेद्भार्यां नालं वा वृषमुत्सृजेत् ॥
2.19.m:
‘With goat[-meat] that is completely red, during the rainy season and under the Maghās.
Many sons should be desired, [in hope] that even one might go to Gayā,
or marry a young maiden as wife, or release a blue bull.’

2.19.s:
śaṃyuruvāca
gayādīnāṃ phalaṃ tāta brūhi me paripṛcchataḥ /
dātṝṇāṃ caiva yatpuṇyaṃ nikhilena pravīhi me //
2.19.d:
शंयुरुवाच
गयादीनां फलं तात ब्रूहि मे परिपृच्छतः ।
दातॄणां चैव यत्पुण्यं निखिलेन प्रवीहि मे ॥

2.19.s:
bṛhaspatiruvāca
gayāyāmakṣayaṃ śrāddhañjapahomatapāṃsi ca /
pitṛkṣaye hi tatputra tasmāttatrākṣayaṃ smṛtam //
2.19.d:
बृहस्पतिरुवाच
गयायामक्षयं श्राद्धञ्जपहोमतपांसि च ।
पितृक्षये हि तत्पुत्र तस्मात्तत्राक्षयं स्मृतम् ॥
2.19.m:
Bṛhaspati said:
‘At Gayā, śrāddha, silent recitation, oblations, and austerities are inexhaustible.
For that is the destruction of the ancestors' [distress], my son; therefore it is taught to be inexhaustible there.’

2.19.s:
pūrṇāyāmekaviṃśaṃ tu gauryāmutpāditaḥ sutaḥ /
mahāmahāṃśca juhuyāditi tasya phalaṃ smṛtam /
phalaṃ vṛṣasya vakṣyāmi gadato me nibodhata //
2.19.d:
पूर्णायामेकविंशं तु गौर्यामुत्पादितः सुतः ।
महामहांश्च जुहुयादिति तस्य फलं स्मृतम् ।
फलं वृषस्य वक्ष्यामि गदतो मे निबोधत ॥
2.19.m:
‘A son begotten on a virgin wife [sanctifies] the twenty-first [generation],
and he should offer the great sacrifices—such is the fruit taught for that.
I shall describe the fruit of the bull; listen as I speak:

2.19.s: vṛṣotsraṣṭā punātyeva daśātītāndaśāvarān //
2.19.d: वृषोत्स्रष्टा पुनात्येव दशातीतान्दशावरान् ॥
2.19.m: The releaser of a bull indeed purifies ten past and ten future [generations].

2.19.s:
yatkiñcitspṛśate toyamavatīrṇo nadījale /
vṛṣotsarggatpitṝṇāṃ tu hyakṣayaṃ samudāhṛtam //
2.19.d:
यत्किञ्चित्स्पृशते तोयमवतीर्णो नदीजले ।
वृषोत्सर्ग्गत्पितॄणां तु ह्यक्षयं समुदाहृतम् ॥
2.19.m:
Whatever water [the bull] touches, having entered river water,
by the release of the bull, is declared to be inexhaustible for the ancestors.

2.19.s:
yenayena spṛśettoyaṃ lāṅgūlādibhiraṅgaśaḥ /
sarvaṃ tadakṣayaṃ tasya pitṝṇāṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ //
2.19.d:
येनयेन स्पृशेत्तोयं लाङ्गूलादिभिरङ्गशः ।
सर्वं तदक्षयं तस्य पितॄणां नात्र संशयः ॥
2.19.m:
With whatever limb, beginning with its tail, it touches the water,
all that becomes inexhaustible for his ancestors; there is no doubt of this.

2.19.s:
śṛṅgaiḥ khurairvā bhūmiṃ yāmullikhatyaniśaṃ vṛṣaḥ /
madhukulyāḥ pitṝṃstasya hyakṣayāśca bhavanti vai //
2.19.d:
शृङ्गैः खुरैर्वा भूमिं यामुल्लिखत्यनिशं वृषः ।
मधुकुल्याः पितॄंस्तस्य ह्यक्षयाश्च भवन्ति वै ॥
2.19.m:
Whatever ground the bull constantly scratches with its horns or hooves,
verily becomes rivers of honey, inexhaustible for his ancestors.

2.19.s:
sahasranalvamātreṇa taḍāgena yathāsrutiḥ /
tṛptistu yā pitṝṇāṃ vai sā vṛṣeṇeha kalpate //
2.19.d:
सहस्रनल्वमात्रेण तडागेन यथास्रुतिः ।
तृप्तिस्तु या पितॄणां वै सा वृषेणेह कल्पते ॥
2.19.m:
Just as from a reservoir measuring a thousand nalvas, by the flowing [water],
that satisfaction which belongs to the ancestors is brought about here by the bull.

2.19.s:
yo dadāti guḍonmiśratilāni śrāddhakarmaṇi /
madhu vāmadhumiśraṃ vā sarvamevākṣayaṃ bhavet //
2.19.d:
यो ददाति गुडोन्मिश्रतिलानि श्राद्धकर्मणि ।
मधु वामधुमिश्रं वा सर्वमेवाक्षयं भवेत् ॥
2.19.m:
He who gives sesame seeds mixed with jaggery in the śrāddha rite,
or honey, or [something] mixed with honey, all becomes truly inexhaustible.

2.19.s:
na brāhmaṇaṃ parikṣeta sadā deyaṃ hi mānavaiḥ /
daivekarmaṇi pitrye ca śrūyate vai parīkṣaṇam //
2.19.d:
न ब्राह्मणं परिक्षेत सदा देयं हि मानवैः ।
दैवेकर्मणि पित्र्ये च श्रूयते वै परीक्षणम् ॥
2.19.m:
A brāhmaṇa should not be examined [casually]; gifts should always be given by men.
Indeed, examination is prescribed only in rites for the gods and rites for the ancestors.

2.19.s:
sarvavedavratasnātāḥ paṅktīnāṃ pāvanā dvijāḥ /
ye ca bhāṣāvidaḥ kecidye ca vyākaraṇe ratāḥ //
2.19.d:
सर्ववेदव्रतस्नाताः पङ्क्तीनां पावना द्विजाः ।
ये च भाषाविदः केचिद्ये च व्याकरणे रताः ॥
2.19.m:
Twice-born men who have bathed at the completion of vows for all the Vedas, who purify rows [of diners],
and those who know languages, and those devoted to grammar;

2.19.s:
adhīyate purāṇaṃ vai dharmaśāstramathāpi ca /
triṇāciketaḥ pañcāgniḥ sa sauparṇaḥ ṣaḍaṅgavit //
2.19.d:
अधीयते पुराणं वै धर्मशास्त्रमथापि च ।
त्रिणाचिकेतः पञ्चाग्निः स सौपर्णः षडङ्गवित् ॥
2.19.m:
those who study the Purāṇa and the legal treatises;
one who knows the Triṇāciketa fire, one who maintains the five fires, one who knows the Sauparṇa hymn, one who knows the six Vedāṅgas;

2.19.s:
brahmadevasutaścaiva cchandogo jyeṣṭhasāmagaḥ /
puṇyeṣu yaśca tīrtheṣu kṛtasnānaḥ kṛtavrataḥ //
2.19.d:
ब्रह्मदेवसुतश्चैव च्छन्दोगो ज्येष्ठसामगः ।
पुण्येषु यश्च तीर्थेषु कृतस्नानः कृतव्रतः ॥
2.19.m:
the son of a Brahma-marriage, a chanter of the Chandoga, one who sings the Jyeṣṭhasāman,
and one who has bathed at holy pilgrimage-places and kept vows;

2.19.s:
makheṣu ye ca sarveṣu bhavantyavabhṛthāplutāḥ /
ye ca satyavratā nityaṃ svadharmaniratāśca ye //
2.19.d:
मखेषु ये च सर्वेषु भवन्त्यवभृथाप्लुताः ।
ये च सत्यव्रता नित्यं स्वधर्मनिरताश्च ये ॥
2.19.m:
and those who have bathed in final ablutions in all sacrifices,
and those who are ever devoted to the vow of truth and intent upon their own duty;

2.19.s:
akrodhanā lobhaparāstāñchrāddheṣu nimantrayet /
etebhyo dattamakṣayyamete vai paṅktipāvanāḥ //
2.19.d:
अक्रोधना लोभपरास्ताञ्छ्राद्धेषु निमन्त्रयेत् ।
एतेभ्यो दत्तमक्षय्यमेते वै पङ्क्तिपावनाः ॥
2.19.m:
those free from anger and intent on generous giving—these he should invite to śrāddhas.
What is given to them is inexhaustible; they indeed purify the row [of diners].

2.19.s:
śrāddhīyā brahmaṇā ye tu yogavratasuniṣṭhitāḥ /
trayo 'pi pūjitāstena brahmaviṣṇumaheśvarāḥ //
2.19.d:
श्राद्धीया ब्रह्मणा ये तु योगव्रतसुनिष्ठिताः ।
त्रयो ऽपि पूजितास्तेन ब्रह्मविष्णुमहेश्वराः ॥
2.19.m:
Those eligible for śrāddha who are steadfast in the vow of yoga by means of the Veda,
by him the three are worshipped: Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśvara.

2.19.s:
pitṛbhiḥ saha lokāśca yo hyetānpūjayennaraḥ /
pavitrāṇāṃ pavitraṃ ca maṅgalānāṃ ca maṅgalam //
2.19.d:
पितृभिः सह लोकाश्च यो ह्येतान्पूजयेन्नरः ।
पवित्राणां पवित्रं च मङ्गलानां च मङ्गलम् ॥
2.19.m:
And the worlds together with the ancestors [are worshipped] by whatever man honours them;
[this is] the purifier of purifiers and the auspiciousness of auspicious things.

2.19.s:
prathamaḥ sarvadharmāṇāṃ yogadharmo nigadyate /
apāṅkteyānpravakṣyami gadato me nibodhata //
2.19.d:
प्रथमः सर्वधर्माणां योगधर्मो निगद्यते ।
अपाङ्क्तेयान्प्रवक्ष्यमि गदतो मे निबोधत ॥
2.19.m:
The duty of yoga is declared to be foremost among all duties.
I shall declare those unfit to sit in the row; listen to me as I speak:

2.19.s:
kitavo madyapo yaśca paśupālo nirākṛtaḥ /
grāmapreṣyo vārdhuṣiko hyāpaṇo vaṇijastathā //
2.19.d:
कितवो मद्यपो यश्च पशुपालो निराकृतः ।
ग्रामप्रेष्यो वार्धुषिको ह्यापणो वणिजस्तथा ॥
2.19.m:
A gambler, a drinker of liquor, a herdsman, an outcast,
a village servant, a usurer, a shopkeeper, and likewise merchants;

2.19.s:
agāra dāhī garado vṛṣalo grāmayājakaḥ /
kāṇḍapṛṣṭho 'tha kuṇḍāśī madhupaḥ somavikrayī //
2.19.d:
अगार दाही गरदो वृषलो ग्रामयाजकः ।
काण्डपृष्ठो ऽथ कुण्डाशी मधुपः सोमविक्रयी ॥
2.19.m:
an arsonist, a poisoner, an outcaste, a village priest,
a mercenary who fights for pay, one who eats the food of an adulteress's son, a drunkard, a seller of soma;

2.19.s:
samudrāntarito bhṛtyaḥ piśunaḥ kūṭasākṣikaḥ /
pitrā vivadamānaśca yasya copapatirgṛhe //
2.19.d:
समुद्रान्तरितो भृत्यः पिशुनः कूटसाक्षिकः ।
पित्रा विवदमानश्च यस्य चोपपतिर्गृहे ॥
2.19.m:
one separated by the sea, a hired servant, an informer, a false witness,
one who disputes with his father, and one in whose house a paramour dwells;

2.19.s:
abhiśastastathā stenaḥ śilpaṃ yaścopajīvati /
stavakaḥ sūpakāraśca yaśca mitrāṇi nindati //
2.19.d:
अभिशस्तस्तथा स्तेनः शिल्पं यश्चोपजीवति ।
स्तवकः सूपकारश्च यश्च मित्राणि निन्दति ॥
2.19.m:
an accused person, a thief, and one who lives by a craft,
a flatterer, a cook, and one who reviles friends;

2.19.s:
kāṇaśca khañjakaścaiva nāstiko vedavarjitaḥ /
unmatto 'pyatha ṣaṇḍhaśca bhrūṇahā gurutalpagaḥ //
2.19.d:
काणश्च खञ्जकश्चैव नास्तिको वेदवर्जितः ।
उन्मत्तो ऽप्यथ षण्ढश्च भ्रूणहा गुरुतल्पगः ॥
2.19.m:
one-eyed, lame, an atheist, one destitute of the Veda,
a madman, an eunuch, an aborticide, one who violates the teacher’s bed;

2.19.s:
bhiṣagjīvī prāśanikaḥ parastrīṃ yaśca sevate /
vikrīṇāti ca yo brahmavratāni niyamāṃstathā //
2.19.d:
भिषग्जीवी प्राशनिकः परस्त्रीं यश्च सेवते ।
विक्रीणाति च यो ब्रह्मव्रतानि नियमांस्तथा ॥
2.19.m:
one who makes a living as a physician, a professional eater, one who attends on another’s wife,
and one who sells the sacred knowledge, vows, and observances;

2.19.s:
naṣṭaṃ syānnāstike dattaṃ vrataghne cāpavarjitam /
yaccavāṇijake dattaṃ neha nāmutra saṃbhavet //
2.19.d:
नष्टं स्यान्नास्तिके दत्तं व्रतघ्ने चापवर्जितम् ।
यच्चवाणिजके दत्तं नेह नामुत्र संभवेत् ॥
2.19.m:
What is given to an atheist is ruined, and [what is given] to a vow-breaker is discarded;
and that which is given to a trader does not bear fruit here or in the world beyond.

2.19.s:
nikṣepahārake caiva kṛtaghne vidavarjite /
tathā pāṇavike vai ca kāruke dharmavarjite //
2.19.d:
निक्षेपहारके चैव कृतघ्ने विदवर्जिते ।
तथा पाणविके वै च कारुके धर्मवर्जिते ॥
2.19.m:
Likewise regarding a stealer of deposits, an ungrateful person, one destitute of Vedic knowledge,
and a drummer, an artisan destitute of righteousness;

2.19.s:
krīṇāti yo hyapaṇyāni vikrīṇāti praśaṃsati /
anyatrāsya samādhānaṃ na vaṇikūchrāddhamarhati //
2.19.d:
क्रीणाति यो ह्यपण्यानि विक्रीणाति प्रशंसति ।
अन्यत्रास्य समाधानं न वणिकूछ्राद्धमर्हति ॥
2.19.m:
one who buys prohibited goods, sells them, or praises them—
his composure lies elsewhere; a trader does not deserve a śrāddha.

2.19.s:
bhasmanīva hutaṃ havyaṃ dattaṃ paunarbhave dvijaḥ /
ṣaṣṭiṃ kāṇaḥ śataṃ ṣaṇḍhaḥ śvitrī pañcaśatānyapi //
2.19.d:
भस्मनीव हुतं हव्यं दत्तं पौनर्भवे द्विजः ।
षष्टिं काणः शतं षण्ढः श्वित्री पञ्चशतान्यपि ॥
2.19.m:
The oblation given to a twice-born son of a remarried woman is like an offering in ashes:
a one-eyed man [destroys the fruit of] sixty [guests], an eunuch a hundred, and a leper five hundred;

2.19.s:
pāparogī sahasraṃ vai dāturnāśayate phalam /
bhraśyeddhi sa phalāttasmātpradātā yastu bāliśaḥ //
2.19.d:
पापरोगी सहस्रं वै दातुर्नाशयते फलम् ।
भ्रश्येद्धि स फलात्तस्मात्प्रदाता यस्तु बालिशः ॥
2.19.m:
a person afflicted with a vile disease destroys the fruit of a thousand for the giver.
Verily, from that fruit falls the donor who is foolish.

2.19.s:
yadviṣṭitaśirā bhuṅkte yadbhuṅkte dakṣiṇāmukhaḥ /
sopānatkaśca yadbhuṅkte yacca dattamasatkṛtam //
2.19.d:
यद्विष्टितशिरा भुङ्क्ते यद्भुङ्क्ते दक्षिणामुखः ।
सोपानत्कश्च यद्भुङ्क्ते यच्च दत्तमसत्कृतम् ॥
2.19.m:
What one eats with head wrapped, what one eats facing the south,
what one eats wearing shoes, and that which is given disrespectfully—

2.19.s:
sarvaṃ tadasuredrāya brahmā bhāgamakalpayat /
śvā caiva brahmahā caiva nāvekṣeta kathañcana //
2.19.d:
सर्वं तदसुरेद्राय ब्रह्मा भागमकल्पयत् ।
श्वा चैव ब्रह्महा चैव नावेक्षेत कथञ्चन ॥
2.19.m:
Brahmā assigned all that as the share for the king of Asuras.
A dog and a killer of a brāhmaṇa should by no means look on.

2.19.s:
tasmātparivṛtairdadyāttilaiścānnaṃ vikīrya ca /
rākṣasānāṃ tilāḥ proktāḥ śunāṃ parivṛtāstathā //
2.19.d:
तस्मात्परिवृतैर्दद्यात्तिलैश्चान्नं विकीर्य च ।
राक्षसानां तिलाः प्रोक्ताः शुनां परिवृतास्तथा ॥
2.19.m:
Therefore one should give in enclosed [places], having scattered food with sesame seeds;
sesame seeds are proclaimed [protective] against Rākṣasas, and enclosed spaces against dogs.

2.19.s:
darśanātsūkaro hanti pakṣavātena kukkuṭaḥ /
rajasvalāyāḥ sparśena kruddhoyaśca prayacchati //
2.19.d:
दर्शनात्सूकरो हन्ति पक्षवातेन कुक्कुटः ।
रजस्वलायाः स्पर्शेन क्रुद्धोयश्च प्रयच्छति ॥
2.19.m:
A pig spoils [the rite] by sight, a cock by the wind of its wings,
[a woman] in her menses by touch, and [one who is] angry when he gives.

2.19.s:
nadītīreṣu ramyeṣu saritsu ca sarassu ca /
vivikteṣu ca prīyante datteneha pitāmahāḥ //
2.19.d:
नदीतीरेषु रम्येषु सरित्सु च सरस्सु च ।
विविक्तेषु च प्रीयन्ते दत्तेनेह पितामहाः ॥
2.19.m:
On pleasant riverbanks, near streams and lakes,
and in solitary places, the ancestors are pleased with what is given here.

2.19.s:
nāsavyaṃpātayejjānu na yukto vācamīrayet /
tasmātparivṛteneha vidhivaddarbhapāṇinā //
2.19.d:
नासव्यंपातयेज्जानु न युक्तो वाचमीरयेत् ।
तस्मात्परिवृतेनेह विधिवद्दर्भपाणिना ॥
2.19.m:
One must not let down the left knee, nor utter a word when engaged [in the rite].
Therefore, here, by one who is screened, holding darbha-grass in hand according to rule,

2.19.s:
pitrorārādhanaṃ kāryamevaṃ prīṇayate pitṝn /
anumānya dvijānpūrvamargauṃ kuryādyathāvidhi //
2.19.d:
पित्रोराराधनं कार्यमेवं प्रीणयते पितॄन् ।
अनुमान्य द्विजान्पूर्वमर्गौं कुर्याद्यथाविधि ॥
2.19.m:
the propitiation of the parents is to be performed; in this way one pleases the ancestors.
Having first obtained the assent of the twice-born, one should offer the respectful water according to rule.

2.19.s:
pitṝṇāṃ nirvapedbhūmau sūrye vā darbhasaṃstare /
śuklapakṣe ca pūrvāṅṇe śrāddhaṃ kuryādyathāvidhi //
2.19.d:
पितॄणां निर्वपेद्भूमौ सूर्ये वा दर्भसंस्तरे ।
शुक्लपक्षे च पूर्वाङ्णे श्राद्धं कुर्याद्यथाविधि ॥
2.19.m:
One should offer to the ancestors on the ground, or before the sun, on a strewing of darbha-grass;
in the bright fortnight, one should perform the śrāddha in the morning according to rule.

2.19.s:
kṛṣṇapakṣe 'paraṅṇe tu rauhiṇaṃ vai na laṅghayet /
evamete mahātmāno mahāyogā mahaujasaḥ //
2.19.d:
कृष्णपक्षे ऽपरङ्णे तु रौहिणं वै न लङ्घयेत् ।
एवमेते महात्मानो महायोगा महौजसः ॥
2.19.m:
In the dark fortnight, however, [one should perform it] in the afternoon; one must not transgress the Rauhiṇa [muhūrta].
Thus these great-souled ones possess great yoga and great splendour.

2.19.s:
sadā vai pitaraḥ pūjyāḥ saṃ prāptau deśakālayoḥ /
pitṛbhaktyaiva tu naro yogaṃ prāpnoti durllabham //
2.19.d:
सदा वै पितरः पूज्याः सं प्राप्तौ देशकालयोः ।
पितृभक्त्यैव तु नरो योगं प्राप्नोति दुर्ल्लभम् ॥
2.19.m:
The ancestors are ever to be worshipped when the place and time have arrived;
verily, by devotion to the ancestors a man attains the yoga that is difficult to obtain.

2.19.s:
dhyānena mokṣaṃ gaccheddhi hitvā karma śubhāśubham /
yajñahetostaduddhṛtya mohayitvā jagattathā //
2.19.d:
ध्यानेन मोक्षं गच्छेद्धि हित्वा कर्म शुभाशुभम् ।
यज्ञहेतोस्तदुद्धृत्य मोहयित्वा जगत्तथा ॥
2.19.m:
By meditation he would attain liberation, abandoning auspicious and inauspicious karma.
Having extracted that for the sake of sacrifice, and having deluded the world,

2.19.s:
guhāyāṃ nihitaṃ brahma kaśyapena mahātmanā /
amṛtaṃ guhyamuddhṛtya yoge yogavidāṃ varāḥ //
2.19.d:
गुहायां निहितं ब्रह्म कश्यपेन महात्मना ।
अमृतं गुह्यमुद्धृत्य योगे योगविदां वराः ॥
2.19.m:
the sacred knowledge was placed in a secret cave by the great-souled Kaśyapa.
Having extracted the secret nectar in yoga, O best among those who know yoga,

2.19.s:
proktaḥ sanatkumāreṇa mahāto brahmaṇaḥ padam /
devānāṃ paramaṃ guhyamṛṣīṇāṃ ca parāyaṇam //
2.19.d:
प्रोक्तः सनत्कुमारेण महातो ब्रह्मणः पदम् ।
देवानां परमं गुह्यमृषीणां च परायणम् ॥
2.19.m:
the abode of the supreme Brahman was proclaimed by Sanatkumāra,
the ultimate secret of the gods and the supreme refuge of the sages.

2.19.s:
pitṛbhaktyā prayatnena prāpya te tanmanīṣibhiḥ /
pitṛbhaktaḥ samāsena pitṛpūrvaparaśca yaḥ //
2.19.d:
पितृभक्त्या प्रयत्नेन प्राप्य ते तन्मनीषिभिः ।
पितृभक्तः समासेन पितृपूर्वपरश्च यः ॥
2.19.m:
Attaining that with effort through devotion to the ancestors, by those wise men—
he who is devoted to the ancestors, in brief, and intent upon his ancestors before all else,

2.19.s: ayatnātprāpnuyādeva sarvametanna saṃśayaḥ //
2.19.d: अयत्नात्प्राप्नुयादेव सर्वमेतन्न संशयः ॥
2.19.m: verily attains all this without effort; there is no doubt.

2.19.s:
bṛhaspatiruvāca
yasmaiśrāddhāni deyāni yacca dattaṃ mahatphalam /
yeṣu cāpyakṣayaṃ śrāddhaṃ tīrtheṣu ca guhāsu ca //
2.19.d:
बृहस्पतिरुवाच
यस्मैश्राद्धानि देयानि यच्च दत्तं महत्फलम् ।
येषु चाप्यक्षयं श्राद्धं तीर्थेषु च गुहासु च ॥
2.19.m:
Bṛhaspati said:
To whom funeral offerings should be given, and what given yields great fruit, / and at which sacred water bodies and caves a funeral offering becomes inexhaustible,

2.19.s:
yeṣu svargamavāpnoti tatte proktaṃ sasaṃgraham /
śrutvemaṃ śrāddhakalpaṃ ca na kuryādyastu mānavaḥ //
2.19.d:
येषु स्वर्गमवाप्नोति तत्ते प्रोक्तं ससंग्रहम् ।
श्रुत्वेमं श्राद्धकल्पं च न कुर्याद्यस्तु मानवः ॥
2.19.m: and at which one attains heaven—that has been declared to you in summary. / But the mortal who, having heard this rite of funeral offerings, does not perform it,

2.19.s:
sa majjennarake ghore nāstikastamasāvṛte /
parivādo na karttavyo yogināṃ tu viśeṣataḥ //
2.19.d:
स मज्जेन्नरके घोरे नास्तिकस्तमसावृते ।
परिवादो न कर्त्तव्यो योगिनां तु विशेषतः ॥
2.19.m: that nihilist would sink into a terrible hell enveloped in darkness. / Moreover, censure must not be made, especially of yogins.

2.19.s:
parivādātkrimirbhūtvā tatraiva parivarttate /
yogānparivadedyastu dhyānino mokṣakāṅkṣiṇaḥ //
2.19.d:
परिवादात्क्रिमिर्भूत्वा तत्रैव परिवर्त्तते ।
योगान्परिवदेद्यस्तु ध्यानिनो मोक्षकाङ्क्षिणः ॥
2.19.m: From censure, having become a worm, one revolves in that very place. / The one who reviles the yogas, the meditators desirous of liberation,

2.19.s:
sa gacchennarakaṃ ghoraṃ śrotāpyasya na saṃśayaḥ /
āvṛtaṃ tamasaḥ sarvaṃ narakaṃ ghoradarśanam /
yogīśvaraparīvādānna svargaṃ yāti mānavaḥ //
2.19.d:
स गच्छेन्नरकं घोरं श्रोताप्यस्य न संशयः ।
आवृतं तमसः सर्वं नरकं घोरदर्शनम् ।
योगीश्वरपरीवादान्न स्वर्गं याति मानवः ॥
2.19.m: he would go to a terrible hell, and the hearer of it as well, no doubt. / All hell, terrible in appearance, is enveloped in darkness; / from censuring a lord of yogins, a mortal does not go to heaven.

2.19.s:
yogeśvarāṇāmā krośaṃ śṛṇuyādyo yatātmanām /
sahi kālaṃ ciraṃ majjennarake nātra saṃśayaḥ /
kuṃbhīpākeṣu pacyante jihvācchede punaḥ punaḥ //
2.19.d:
योगेश्वराणामा क्रोशं शृणुयाद्यो यतात्मनाम् ।
सहि कालं चिरं मज्जेन्नरके नात्र संशयः ।
कुंभीपाकेषु पच्यन्ते जिह्वाच्छेदे पुनः पुनः ॥
2.19.m: He who listens to abuse of the lords of yoga, of self-controlled souls, / will certainly sink into hell for a long time, there is no doubt here; / in the Kumbhīpāka hells they are cooked, their tongues being severed again and again.

2.19.s:
samudre ca yathā loṣaṭastadbatsīdanti te narāḥ /
manasā karmaṇā vācā dveṣaṃ yogeṣu varjayet /
protyānantaṃ phalaṃ bhuṅkta iha vāpi na saṃśayaḥ //
2.19.d:
समुद्रे च यथा लोषटस्तद्बत्सीदन्ति ते नराः ।
मनसा कर्मणा वाचा द्वेषं योगेषु वर्जयेत् ।
प्रोत्यानन्तं फलं भुङ्क्त इह वापि न संशयः ॥
2.19.m: And just like a clod of earth [dissolves] in the ocean, so those men sink. / One should avoid hatred toward yogas in mind, action, and speech; / having departed, he enjoys infinite fruit, or even here, without doubt.

2.19.s:
na pārago vindati paramātmanastrilokamadhye carati svakarmamiḥ /
ṛco yajuḥ sāma tadaṅgapārage 'vikārametaṃ hyanavāpya sīdati //
2.19.d:
न पारगो विन्दति परमात्मनस्त्रिलोकमध्ये चरति स्वकर्ममिः ।
ऋचो यजुः साम तदङ्गपारगे ऽविकारमेतं ह्यनवाप्य सीदति ॥
2.19.m: The one who has not crossed over does not find the Supreme Self, but roams within the three worlds through his own acts; / having crossed to the further shore of the Ṛg, Yajur, and Sāma Vedas and their auxiliary branches, not having attained this changeless [Self], he sinks.

2.19.s:
vikārapāraṃ prakṛteśca pāragastrayīguṇānā triguṇasya pāragaḥ /
yaḥ syāccaturviśatitattvapāragaḥ sa pārago nādhyayanasya pāragaḥ //
2.19.d:
विकारपारं प्रकृतेश्च पारगस्त्रयीगुणाना त्रिगुणस्य पारगः ।
यः स्याच्चतुर्विशतितत्त्वपारगः स पारगो नाध्ययनस्य पारगः ॥
2.19.m: He who has reached the end of modification and crossed beyond nature, crossed beyond the three qualities of the three Vedas— / he who has crossed beyond the twenty-four principles is the true master, not one who has merely mastered recitation.

2.19.s:
kṛtsnaṃ yathāvatsamupaiti tatparastathaiva bhūyaḥ pralayatvamātmanaḥ /
pratyāharedyogapathaṃ na yo dvijo na sarvapāra kramapāragocaraḥ //
2.19.d:
कृत्स्नं यथावत्समुपैति तत्परस्तथैव भूयः प्रलयत्वमात्मनः ।
प्रत्याहरेद्योगपथं न यो द्विजो न सर्वपार क्रमपारगोचरः ॥
2.19.m: The highest one attains all properly, and likewise the self's dissolution again. / The twice-born who does not withdraw onto the path of yoga is not a master of everything, nor within the range of mastery over the stages.

2.19.s:
vedasya veditavyaṃ ca vedyaṃ vindati yogavit /
taṃ vai vedavidaḥ prāhustamāhurvedapāragam //
2.19.d:
वेदस्य वेदितव्यं च वेद्यं विन्दति योगवित् ।
तं वै वेदविदः प्राहुस्तमाहुर्वेदपारगम् ॥
2.19.m: The knower of yoga finds the Veda, what is to be known, and the knowable; / him indeed the knowers of the Veda call, him they proclaim a master of the Veda.

2.19.s:
vedaṃ ca veditavyaṃ ca viditvā vai yathāsthitaḥ /
evaṃ vedavidaḥ prāhuranyaṃ vai vedapāragam //
2.19.d:
वेदं च वेदितव्यं च विदित्वा वै यथास्थितः ।
एवं वेदविदः प्राहुरन्यं वै वेदपारगम् ॥
2.19.m: Having known the Veda and what is to be known, abiding truly as it is— / thus the knowers of the Veda proclaim another to be a master of the Veda.

2.19.s:
yajñānvedāṃstathā kāmāṃstapāṃsi vividhāni ca /
prāpnotyāyuḥ prajāścaiva pitṛbhakto na saśayaḥ //
2.19.d:
यज्ञान्वेदांस्तथा कामांस्तपांसि विविधानि च ।
प्राप्नोत्यायुः प्रजाश्चैव पितृभक्तो न सशयः ॥
2.19.m: Sacrifices, Vedas, desires, and various austerities, / life and offspring indeed—the one devoted to the ancestors attains, no doubt.

2.19.s:
śraddhayā śrāddhakalpaṃ tu yastvimaṃ niyataḥ paṭhet /
sarvāṇyetāni vāpnoti tīrthadānaphalāni ca //
2.19.d:
श्रद्धया श्राद्धकल्पं तु यस्त्विमं नियतः पठेत् ।
सर्वाण्येतानि वाप्नोति तीर्थदानफलानि च ॥
2.19.m: Whoever, restrained, recites this rite of funeral offerings with faith / attains all these fruits and those of gifts at sacred water bodies.

2.19.s:
sa paṅktipāvanaścaiva dvijānāmagrabhugbhavet /
āśrāvya ca dvijānso 'tha sarvakāmānavāpnuyāt //
2.19.d:
स पङ्क्तिपावनश्चैव द्विजानामग्रभुग्भवेत् ।
आश्राव्य च द्विजान्सो ऽथ सर्वकामानवाप्नुयात् ॥
2.19.m: He purifies the row [of diners] and becomes the foremost eater among twice-borns; / and having recited it to the twice-born, he would then attain all desires.

2.19.s:
yaścaitacchṛṇuyānnityama nyāṃśca śrāvayeddvijaḥ /
anasūyurjitakrodho lobhamohavivarjitaḥ //
2.19.d:
यश्चैतच्छृणुयान्नित्यम न्यांश्च श्रावयेद्द्विजः ।
अनसूयुर्जितक्रोधो लोभमोहविवर्जितः ॥
2.19.m: And the twice-born who listens to this daily, and recites it to others, / ungrudging, having conquered anger, freed from greed and delusion,

2.19.s:
tīrthādīnāṃ phalaṃ prāpya dānādīnāṃ ca sarvaśaḥ /
mokṣopāyaṃ labhecchreṣṭhaṃ svargopāyaṃ na saṃśayaḥ /
iha cāpi parā puṣṭhistasmātkurvīta nityaśaḥ //
2.19.d:
तीर्थादीनां फलं प्राप्य दानादीनां च सर्वशः ।
मोक्षोपायं लभेच्छ्रेष्ठं स्वर्गोपायं न संशयः ।
इह चापि परा पुष्ठिस्तस्मात्कुर्वीत नित्यशः ॥
2.19.m: having attained the fruit of sacred water bodies and the like, and of gifts and the like completely, / would obtain the best means to liberation and the means to heaven, no doubt; / and supreme nourishment is here as well; therefore one should do it daily.

2.19.s:
imaṃ vidhiṃ yo hi paṭhedatandritaḥ samāhitaḥ saṃsadi parvasaṃdhiṣu /
apatyabhāgī ca pareṇa tejasā divaukasāṃ sa vrajate salokatām //
2.19.d:
इमं विधिं यो हि पठेदतन्द्रितः समाहितः संसदि पर्वसंधिषु ।
अपत्यभागी च परेण तेजसा दिवौकसां स व्रजते सलोकताम् ॥
2.19.m: Whoever, unwearied, collected in mind, recites this rule in an assembly on the conjunctions of festival days, / becomes a possessor of offspring and, through supreme splendor, goes to the same world as the heaven-dwellers.

2.19.s:
yena proktastvayaṃ kalpo namastasmai svayaṃbhuve /
mahāyogeśvarebhyaśca sadā ca praṇato 'smyaham //
iti śrībrahmāṇḍe mahāpurāṇe vāyuprokte madhyabhāge tṛtīya upoddhātapāde
śrāddhakalpe brahmaṇaparīkṣā nāma ekonaviṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ // 19//
2.19.d:
येन प्रोक्तस्त्वयं कल्पो नमस्तस्मै स्वयंभुवे ।
महायोगेश्वरेभ्यश्च सदा च प्रणतो ऽस्म्यहम् ॥
इति श्रीब्रह्माण्डे महापुराणे वायुप्रोक्ते मध्यभागे तृतीय उपोद्धातपादे
श्राद्धकल्पे ब्रह्मणपरीक्षा नाम एकोनविंशो ऽध्यायः ॥ 19॥
2.19.m:
Homage to that Svayambhū by whom this rite was declared, / and I am always bowed to the great lords of yoga.

Thus ends the nineteenth chapter, named 'Examination of Brahmins', in the rite of funeral offerings, in the third Upoddhātapāda, in the middle part of the glorious Brahmāṇḍa Mahāpurāṇa spoken by Vāyu.

2.20.s:
bṛhaspatiruvāca
ityete pitaro devā devānāmapi devatāḥ /
saptasvete sthitā nityaṃ sthāneṣu pitaro 'vyayāḥ //
2.20.d:
बृहस्पतिरुवाच
इत्येते पितरो देवा देवानामपि देवताः ।
सप्तस्वेते स्थिता नित्यं स्थानेषु पितरो ऽव्ययाः ॥
2.20.m:
Bṛhaspati said:
Thus these ancestors are gods, deities even of the gods; / established in these seven stations, the imperishable ancestors are eternal.

2.20.s:
prajāpatisutā hyete sarveṣāṃ tu mahātmanām /
ādyo gaṇastu yogānāmanuyogavivarddhanaḥ //
2.20.d:
प्रजापतिसुता ह्येते सर्वेषां तु महात्मनाम् ।
आद्यो गणस्तु योगानामनुयोगविवर्द्धनः ॥
2.20.m: They are sons of Prajāpati, of all the great-souled beings. / The first group belongs to yogas, promoting subsequent yoga;

2.20.s:
dvitīyo devatānāṃ tu tṛtīyo dānavādinām /
śeṣāstu varṇiṃnāṃ jñeyā iti sarve prakīrttitāḥ //
2.20.d:
द्वितीयो देवतानां तु तृतीयो दानवादिनाम् ।
शेषास्तु वर्णिंनां ज्ञेया इति सर्वे प्रकीर्त्तिताः ॥
2.20.m: the second belongs to deities; the third to Dānavas and others; / and the rest are to be known as belonging to the social classes: thus all have been proclaimed.

2.20.s:
devāschaitānyajante vai sarvajñāneṣvavasthitān /
āśramaśca yajantyenāṃścatvārastu yathākramam //
2.20.d:
देवास्छैतान्यजन्ते वै सर्वज्ञानेष्ववस्थितान् ।
आश्रमश्च यजन्त्येनांश्चत्वारस्तु यथाक्रमम् ॥
2.20.m: The gods sacrifice to these who are established in all knowledge; / and the four stages of life sacrifice to them in proper order.

2.20.s:
sarve varṇā yajantyenāṃścatvārastu yathāgamam /
tathā saṃkarajātyaśca mlecchāścāpi yajanti vai //
2.20.d:
सर्वे वर्णा यजन्त्येनांश्चत्वारस्तु यथागमम् ।
तथा संकरजात्यश्च म्लेच्छाश्चापि यजन्ति वै ॥
2.20.m: All four social classes sacrifice to them in accordance with scripture; / likewise, mixed castes and even foreigners sacrifice [to them].

2.20.s:
pitṛṃstu yo yajedbhaktyā pitaraḥ prīṇayanti te /
pitaraḥ puṣṭikāmasya prajākāmasya vā punaḥ //
2.20.d:
पितृंस्तु यो यजेद्भक्त्या पितरः प्रीणयन्ति ते ।
पितरः पुष्टिकामस्य प्रजाकामस्य वा पुनः ॥
2.20.m: The ancestors whom one sacrifices to with devotion, they gratify [him]; / the ancestors, for one desiring nourishment or one desiring offspring,

2.20.s:
puṣṭiṃ prajāṃ tu svargaṃ ca prayacchanti pitāmahāḥ /
devakāryādapi tathā pitṛkāryaṃ viśiṣyate //
2.20.d:
पुष्टिं प्रजां तु स्वर्गं च प्रयच्छन्ति पितामहाः ।
देवकार्यादपि तथा पितृकार्यं विशिष्यते ॥
2.20.m: the grandfathers grant nourishment, offspring, and heaven. / Likewise, the duty to ancestors is superior even to the duty to gods.

2.20.s:
devatānāṃ hi pitaraḥ pūrvamāpyāyanaṃ smṛtāḥ /
na hi yogagatiḥ sūkṣmā pitṝṇāṃ jñāyate naraiḥ //
2.20.d:
देवतानां हि पितरः पूर्वमाप्यायनं स्मृताः ।
न हि योगगतिः सूक्ष्मा पितॄणां ज्ञायते नरैः ॥
2.20.m: For the ancestors are traditionally remembered as the prior nourishment of deities. / Indeed, the subtle course of yoga of the ancestors is not known by men,

2.20.s:
tapasā hi prasiddhena kiṃ punarmāṃsacakṣuṣā /
sarveṣāṃ rājataṃ pātramatha vā rajatānvitam //
2.20.d:
तपसा हि प्रसिद्धेन किं पुनर्मांसचक्षुषा ।
सर्वेषां राजतं पात्रमथ वा रजतान्वितम् ॥
2.20.m: even by renowned austerity, much less by the eye of flesh. / For all, a silver vessel, or one provided with silver,

2.20.s:
pāvanaṃ hyuttamaṃ proktaṃ devānāṃ pitṛbhiḥ saha /
yeṣāṃ dāsyanti piṇḍāṃstrīnbāndhavā nāmagotrataḥ //
2.20.d:
पावनं ह्युत्तमं प्रोक्तं देवानां पितृभिः सह ।
येषां दास्यन्ति पिण्डांस्त्रीन्बान्धवा नामगोत्रतः ॥
2.20.m: is declared to be the highest purifier for gods together with ancestors. / To those for whom relatives offer three rice balls by name and lineage,

2.20.s:
bhūmau kuśottarāyāṃ ca apasavyavidhānataḥ /
sarvatra varttamānāste piṇḍāḥ prīṇanti vai pitṝn //
2.20.d:
भूमौ कुशोत्तरायां च अपसव्यविधानतः ।
सर्वत्र वर्त्तमानास्ते पिण्डाः प्रीणन्ति वै पितॄन् ॥
2.20.m: on the ground strewn with kuśa grass, according to the counter-clockwise ritual procedure, / those rice balls, existing everywhere, truly gratify the ancestors.

2.20.s:
yadāhāro bhavejjanturāhāraḥ so 'sya jāyate /
yathā goṣṭhe pranaṣṭāṃ vai vatso vindati mātaram //
2.20.d:
यदाहारो भवेज्जन्तुराहारः सो ऽस्य जायते ।
यथा गोष्ठे प्रनष्टां वै वत्सो विन्दति मातरम् ॥
2.20.m: Whatever food a creature eats, that becomes his food [there]. / Just as a calf finds its lost mother in a cattle pen,

2.20.s:
tathā taṃ nayate mantro janturyatrāvatiṣṭhati /
nāmagotraṃ ca mantraṃ ca dattamannaṃ nayanti tam //
2.20.d:
तथा तं नयते मन्त्रो जन्तुर्यत्रावतिष्ठति ।
नामगोत्रं च मन्त्रं च दत्तमन्नं नयन्ति तम् ॥
2.20.m: so the mantra leads it to where the creature stays; / name, lineage, and mantra convey that given food to him.

2.20.s:
api yoniśataṃ prāptāṃstṛptistānanugacchati /
evameṣā sthitā sattā brahmaṇaḥ parameṣṭhinaḥ //
2.20.d:
अपि योनिशतं प्राप्तांस्तृप्तिस्ताननुगच्छति ।
एवमेषा स्थिता सत्ता ब्रह्मणः परमेष्ठिनः ॥
2.20.m: Even if they have attained a hundred wombs, satisfaction follows them. / Thus this nature was established by Brahmā Parameṣṭhin

2.20.s:
pitṝṇamādisargetu lokānāmakṣayārthinām /
ityete pitaraścaiva lokā duhitarastathā //
2.20.d:
पितॄणमादिसर्गेतु लोकानामक्षयार्थिनाम् ।
इत्येते पितरश्चैव लोका दुहितरस्तथा ॥
2.20.m: at the primary creation of the ancestors, for the sake of worlds desiring imperishability. / Thus these ancestors, the worlds, and the daughters,

2.20.s:
dauhitrā yajamānaśca proktāścaiva mayānagha /
kīrttitāḥ pitaraste vai tava putra yathākramam //
2.20.d:
दौहित्रा यजमानश्च प्रोक्ताश्चैव मयानघ ।
कीर्त्तिताः पितरस्ते वै तव पुत्र यथाक्रमम् ॥
2.20.m: the daughters' sons, and the sacrificer have been declared by me, O sinless one; / your ancestors have been proclaimed to you, O son, in proper order.

2.20.s:
śaṃyuruvāca
aho divyastvayā tāta pitṛsargastu kīrtitaḥ /
lokā duhitaraścaiva dohitrāśca śrutāstathā //
2.20.d:
शंयुरुवाच
अहो दिव्यस्त्वया तात पितृसर्गस्तु कीर्तितः ।
लोका दुहितरश्चैव दोहित्राश्च श्रुतास्तथा ॥
2.20.m:
Śaṃyu said:
Oh, the divine creation of ancestors has been proclaimed by you, dear father; / the worlds, daughters, and daughters' sons have likewise been heard,

2.20.s:
dānāni saha śaucena kīrttitāni phalāni ca /
akṣayyatvaṃ dvijāṃścaiva sarvametadudāhṛtam /
adyaprabhṛti karttāsmi sarvametadyathātatham //
2.20.d:
दानानि सह शौचेन कीर्त्तितानि फलानि च ।
अक्षय्यत्वं द्विजांश्चैव सर्वमेतदुदाहृतम् ।
अद्यप्रभृति कर्त्तास्मि सर्वमेतद्यथातथम् ॥
2.20.m: and gifts along with purity have been proclaimed, and fruits, / imperishability, and twice-borns—all this has been set forth. / From this day forward, I will perform all this just as it is.

2.20.s:
bṛhaspatiruvāca
ityetadaṅgirāḥ pūrvamṛṣīṇāmuktavānprabhuḥ /
pṛṣṭaśca saṃśayānsarvānṛṣīnāha nṛsaṃsadi //
2.20.d:
बृहस्पतिरुवाच
इत्येतदङ्गिराः पूर्वमृषीणामुक्तवान्प्रभुः ।
पृष्टश्च संशयान्सर्वानृषीनाह नृसंसदि ॥
2.20.m:
Bṛhaspati said:
Thus Angiras, the lord, previously spoke this to the sages; / and questioned, he stated all doubts to the sages in an assembly of men,

2.20.s:
satre tu vitate pūrvaṃ tathā varṣasahasrake /
yasminsadaspatisnāto brahmā sīddevatāprabhuḥ //
2.20.d:
सत्रे तु वितते पूर्वं तथा वर्षसहस्रके ।
यस्मिन्सदस्पतिस्नातो ब्रह्मा सीद्देवताप्रभुः ॥
2.20.m: at the sacrificial session formerly extended for a thousand years, / in which Brahmā, the lord of deities, was the bathed president of the assembly.

2.20.s:
gatāni tatra varṣāṇāṃ pañcāśacca śatāni vai /
ślokāścātra purā gītā ṛṣibhirbrahmavādibhiḥ //
2.20.d:
गतानि तत्र वर्षाणां पञ्चाशच्च शतानि वै ।
श्लोकाश्चात्र पुरा गीता ऋषिभिर्ब्रह्मवादिभिः ॥
2.20.m: Fifty hundred years had passed there; / and verses were sung on this in ancient times by the sages who expounded Brahman,

2.20.s:
dīkṣitasya purā satre brahmamaḥ paramātmanaḥ /
tatraiva dattamannāgraṃ pitṝṇāmakṣayarthinām /
lokānāṃ ca hitārthāya brahmaṇā parameṣṭhinā //
2.20.d:
दीक्षितस्य पुरा सत्रे ब्रह्ममः परमात्मनः ।
तत्रैव दत्तमन्नाग्रं पितॄणामक्षयर्थिनाम् ।
लोकानां च हितार्थाय ब्रह्मणा परमेष्ठिना ॥
2.20.m: formerly at the sacrificial session of Brahmā, the Supreme Self, who had received consecration; / in that very place, the foremost portion of food was given by Brahmā Parameṣṭhin for the ancestors who desire imperishability, / and for the welfare of the worlds.

2.20.s:
sūta uvāca
evaṃ bṛhaspatiḥ pūrvaṃ pṛṣṭaḥ putreṇa dhīmatā /
provāca pitṛsargaṃ tu yaścaiva samudāhṛta //
iti śrībrahmāṇḍe mahāpurāṇe vāyuprokte madhyabhāge tṛtīya upoddhātapāde
śrāddhakalpo nāma viṃśatitamo 'dhyāyaḥ // 20//
2.20.d:
सूत उवाच
एवं बृहस्पतिः पूर्वं पृष्टः पुत्रेण धीमता ।
प्रोवाच पितृसर्गं तु यश्चैव समुदाहृत ॥
इति श्रीब्रह्माण्डे महापुराणे वायुप्रोक्ते मध्यभागे तृतीय उपोद्धातपादे
श्राद्धकल्पो नाम विंशतितमो ऽध्यायः ॥ 20॥
2.20.m:
The bard said: / Thus Bṛhaspati, previously questioned by his wise son, / declared the creation of the ancestors, just as has been related.

Thus ends the twentieth chapter, named "The Procedure for Śrāddha," in the third [section], the Upoddhātapāda, in the middle portion of the glorious Brahmāṇḍa Mahāpurāṇa spoken by Vāyu.

2.21.s:
samāptaścāyaṃ śrāddhakalpaḥ /
vasiṣṭha uvāca
itthaṃ pravarttamānasya jamadagnermahātmanaḥ /
varṣāṇi katicidrājanvyatīyuramitaujasaḥ //
2.21.d:
समाप्तश्चायं श्राद्धकल्पः ।
वसिष्ठ उवाच
इत्थं प्रवर्त्तमानस्य जमदग्नेर्महात्मनः ।
वर्षाणि कतिचिद्राजन्व्यतीयुरमितौजसः ॥
2.21.m: And this procedure for śrāddha is concluded. / Vasiṣṭha said: / As the great-souled Jamadagni of boundless splendour was living thus, / a few years passed by, O king.

2.21.s:
rāmo 'pi nṛpaśārdūla sarvadharmabhṛtāṃ varaḥ /
vedavedāṅgatattvajñaḥ sarvaśāstraviśāradaḥ //
2.21.d:
रामो ऽपि नृपशार्दूल सर्वधर्मभृतां वरः ।
वेदवेदाङ्गतत्त्वज्ञः सर्वशास्त्रविशारदः ॥
2.21.m: Rāma also, O tiger among kings, foremost of all maintainers of dharma, / knew the truth of the Vedas and Vedāṅgas and was proficient in all treatises.

2.21.s:
pitroścakāra śuśrūṣāṃ vinītātmā mahāmatiḥ /
prītiṃ ca nijaceṣṭābhiranvahaṃ paryavarttayat //
2.21.d:
पित्रोश्चकार शुश्रूषां विनीतात्मा महामतिः ।
प्रीतिं च निजचेष्टाभिरन्वहं पर्यवर्त्तयत् ॥
2.21.m: Humble in nature and highly intelligent, he attended upon his parents, / and daily increased their affection by his actions.

2.21.s:
itthaṃ pravarttamānasya varṣāṇi katicinnṛpa /
pitroḥ śuśrūṣayānaiṣīdrāmo matimatāṃ varaḥ //
2.21.d:
इत्थं प्रवर्त्तमानस्य वर्षाणि कतिचिन्नृप ।
पित्रोः शुश्रूषयानैषीद्रामो मतिमतां वरः ॥
2.21.m: As he lived in this manner, O king, Rāma, foremost of the wise, / spent some years serving his parents.

2.21.s:
sa kadācinmahātejāḥ pitāmaha guhaṃ prati /
gantuṃ vyavasito rājandaivena ca niyojitaḥ //
2.21.d:
स कदाचिन्महातेजाः पितामह गुहं प्रति ।
गन्तुं व्यवसितो राजन्दैवेन च नियोजितः ॥
2.21.m: Once, that one of great fiery energy resolved to go to his grandfather's house, / impelled, O king, by destiny.

2.21.s:
nipīḍya śirasā pitroścaraṇau bhṛgupuṅgavaḥ /
uvāca prāñjalirbhūtavā sapraśrayamidaṃ vacaḥ //
2.21.d:
निपीड्य शिरसा पित्रोश्चरणौ भृगुपुङ्गवः ।
उवाच प्राञ्जलिर्भूतवा सप्रश्रयमिदं वचः ॥
2.21.m: Touching his parents' feet with his head, that eminent Bhṛgu, / with folded hands, addressed these respectful words [to them]:

2.21.s:
kañcidarthamahaṃ tāta mātaraṃ tvāṃ ca sāmpratam /
vijñāpayitumicchāmi mama tacchrotumarhathaḥ //
2.21.d:
कञ्चिदर्थमहं तात मातरं त्वां च साम्प्रतम् ।
विज्ञापयितुमिच्छामि मम तच्छ्रोतुमर्हथः ॥
2.21.m: "Father, I wish now to make a certain request / to mother and to you; you ought to hear it from me.

2.21.s:
pitāmahamahaṃ draṣṭumutkaṇṭhitamanāściram /
tasmāttatpārśvamadhunā gamiṣye vāmanujñayā //
2.21.d:
पितामहमहं द्रष्टुमुत्कण्ठितमनाश्चिरम् ।
तस्मात्तत्पार्श्वमधुना गमिष्ये वामनुज्ञया ॥
2.21.m: My mind has long been longing to see my grandfather; / therefore, with your permission, I shall now go to his presence.

2.21.s:
āhūtaścāsakṛttāta sotkaṇṭhaṃ prīyamāṇayā /
pitāmahyā bahumukhairicchantyā mama darśanam //
2.21.d:
आहूतश्चासकृत्तात सोत्कण्ठं प्रीयमाणया ।
पितामह्या बहुमुखैरिच्छन्त्या मम दर्शनम् ॥
2.21.m: And I have been summoned repeatedly, father, through many messengers / by my grandmother, who loves me with longing and wishes to see me.

2.21.s:
pitṝnpitāmahasyāpi priyameva pradarśanam /
sadīyaṃ tena tatpārśvaṃ gantuṃ māmanujānata //
2.21.d:
पितॄन्पितामहस्यापि प्रियमेव प्रदर्शनम् ।
सदीयं तेन तत्पार्श्वं गन्तुं मामनुजानत ॥
2.21.m: The sight of one's own descendants is truly pleasing even to ancestors and grandfathers; / therefore, grant me leave to go to his presence."

2.21.s:
vasiṣṭha uvāca
iti tasya vacaḥ śrutvā saṃbhrāntaṃ samudīritam /
harṣeṇa mahatā yuktau sāśrunetrau babhūvatuḥ //
2.21.d:
वसिष्ठ उवाच
इति तस्य वचः श्रुत्वा संभ्रान्तं समुदीरितम् ।
हर्षेण महता युक्तौ साश्रुनेत्रौ बभूवतुः ॥
2.21.m: Vasiṣṭha said: / Hearing this eagerly uttered speech of his, / they were filled with great joy, and their eyes filled with tears.

2.21.s:
tamāliṅgya mahābhāgaṃ mūrdhnyupāghrāya sādaram /
abhinandyāśiṣā tāta hyubhau tāvidamāhatuḥ //
2.21.d:
तमालिङ्ग्य महाभागं मूर्ध्न्युपाघ्राय सादरम् ।
अभिनन्द्याशिषा तात ह्युभौ ताविदमाहतुः ॥
2.21.m: Embracing that fortunate one and smelling his head with affection, / blessing him with a benediction, father, the two spoke thus to him:

2.21.s:
pitāmahagṛhaṃ tāta prayāhi tvaṃ yathāsukham /
pitāmahapitāmahyoḥ prītaye darśanāya ca //
2.21.d:
पितामहगृहं तात प्रयाहि त्वं यथासुखम् ।
पितामहपितामह्योः प्रीतये दर्शनाय च ॥
2.21.m: "Go at your pleasure, child, to your grandfather's house, / for the delight and the sight of your grandfather and grandmother.

2.21.s:
tatra gatvā yathānyāyaṃ taṃ śuśrūṣā parāyaṇaḥ /
kañcitkālaṃ tayorvatsa prītaye vasa tadgṛhe //
2.21.d:
तत्र गत्वा यथान्यायं तं शुश्रूषा परायणः ।
कञ्चित्कालं तयोर्वत्स प्रीतये वस तद्गृहे ॥
2.21.m: Having gone there, devoted to serving him properly, / dwell in their house for a short time, child, for their joy.

2.21.s:
sthitvā nāticiraṃ kālaṃ tayorbhūyo 'pyanuśaya /
atrāgaccha mahābhāga kṣemeṇāsmaddidṛkṣayā //
2.21.d:
स्थित्वा नातिचिरं कालं तयोर्भूयो ऽप्यनुशय ।
अत्रागच्छ महाभाग क्षेमेणास्मद्दिदृक्षया ॥
2.21.m: Having stayed for not too long a time, taking leave of them once more, / return here in safety, O fortunate one, out of a desire to see us.

2.21.s:
kṣaṇārddhamapi śaktāḥ stho na vinā putradarśanam /
tasmātpitāmaha gṛhe na cirātsthātumarhasi //
2.21.d:
क्षणार्द्धमपि शक्ताः स्थो न विना पुत्रदर्शनम् ।
तस्मात्पितामह गृहे न चिरात्स्थातुमर्हसि ॥
2.21.m: We are not able to endure even half a moment without the sight of our son; / therefore, you should not remain in your grandfather's house for long.

2.21.s:
tadājñayātha vā putra prapitāmahasannidhim /
gato 'pi śīghramāgaccha krameṇa tadanujñayā //
2.21.d:
तदाज्ञयाथ वा पुत्र प्रपितामहसन्निधिम् ।
गतो ऽपि शीघ्रमागच्छ क्रमेण तदनुज्ञया ॥
2.21.m: Or, if by his command you go, O son, to the presence of your great-grandfather, / return quickly in due course with his permission."

2.21.s:
vasiṣṭha uvāca
ityuktastau parikramya praṇamya ca mahāmatiḥ /
pitarāvapyanujñāpya pitāmahagṛhaṃ tataḥ //
2.21.d:
वसिष्ठ उवाच
इत्युक्तस्तौ परिक्रम्य प्रणम्य च महामतिः ।
पितरावप्यनुज्ञाप्य पितामहगृहं ततः ॥
2.21.m: Vasiṣṭha said: / Thus addressed, circumambulating and bowing to the two of them, / that highly intelligent one took leave of his parents and then set out for his grandfather's house.

2.21.s:
sa gatvā bhṛguvaryasya ṛcīkasya mahātmanaḥ /
praviveśāśramaṃ rāmo muniśiṣyopaśobhitam //
2.21.d:
स गत्वा भृगुवर्यस्य ऋचीकस्य महात्मनः ।
प्रविवेशाश्रमं रामो मुनिशिष्योपशोभितम् ॥
2.21.m: Going forth, Rāma entered the hermitage of the great-souled Ṛcīka, best of the Bhṛgus, / adorned with the sage's disciples,

2.21.s:
svādhyāyaghoṣairvipulaiḥ sarvataḥ pratināditam /
praśāntavaira sattvāḍhyaṃ sarvasattvamanoharam //
2.21.d:
स्वाध्यायघोषैर्विपुलैः सर्वतः प्रतिनादितम् ।
प्रशान्तवैर सत्त्वाढ्यं सर्वसत्त्वमनोहरम् ॥
2.21.m: resounding on all sides with the loud chanting of Vedic recitation, / filled with creatures whose enmity was pacified, charming to all living beings.

2.21.s:
sa praviśyaśramaṃ ramyamṛcīkaṃ sthitamāsane /
dadarśa rāmo rājendra sa pitāmahamagrataḥ //
2.21.d:
स प्रविश्यश्रमं रम्यमृचीकं स्थितमासने ।
ददर्श रामो राजेन्द्र स पितामहमग्रतः ॥
2.21.m: Entering that delightful hermitage, Rāma, O best of kings, / saw his grandfather Ṛcīka seated on a seat before him,

2.21.s:
jājvalyamānaṃ tapasā dhiṣṇyasthamiva pāvakam /
upāsitaṃ satyavatyā yathā dakṣiṇāya'dhvaram //
2.21.d:
जाज्वल्यमानं तपसा धिष्ण्यस्थमिव पावकम् ।
उपासितं सत्यवत्या यथा दक्षिणायऽध्वरम् ॥
2.21.m: blazing with ascetic heat like fire upon its hearth, / attended by Satyavatī like a sacrifice accompanied by sacrificial fees.

2.21.s:
svasamīpamupāyāntaṃ rāmamālokya tau nṛpa /
