suciraṃ taṃ vimarśetāṃ samājñāpūrvadarśanau //
2.21.d:
स्वसमीपमुपायान्तं राममालोक्य तौ नृप ।
सुचिरं तं विमर्शेतां समाज्ञापूर्वदर्शनौ ॥
2.21.m: Beholding Rāma approaching their presence, O king, / the two, who had never seen him before, gazed at him thoughtfully for a long time:

2.21.s:
ko 'yameṣa taporāśiḥ sarvalatraṇapūjitaḥ /
bālo 'yaṃ balavānbhātigāṃbhīryātpraśrayeṇa ca //
2.21.d:
को ऽयमेष तपोराशिः सर्वलत्रणपूजितः ।
बालो ऽयं बलवान्भातिगांभीर्यात्प्रश्रयेण च ॥
2.21.m: "Who is this mass of ascetic power, graced with all auspicious marks? / This boy appears powerful because of his gravity and modesty."

2.21.s:
evaṃ tayościntayatoḥ saharṣaṃ hṛdi kautukāt /
āsasāda śanai rāmaḥ samīpe vinayānvitaḥ //
2.21.d:
एवं तयोश्चिन्तयतोः सहर्षं हृदि कौतुकात् ।
आससाद शनै रामः समीपे विनयान्वितः ॥
2.21.m: As the two were thus pondering in their hearts with joy and curiosity, / Rāma, filled with humility, slowly approached their presence.

2.21.s:
svanāmagotre matimānuktvā pitrormudānvitaḥ /
saṃspṛśaṃścaraṇau mūrdhnā hastābhyāṃ cābhyavādayat //
2.21.d:
स्वनामगोत्रे मतिमानुक्त्वा पित्रोर्मुदान्वितः ।
संस्पृशंश्चरणौ मूर्ध्ना हस्ताभ्यां चाभ्यवादयत् ॥
2.21.m: Joyfully declaring his name and the lineage of his parents, the wise youth, / touching their feet with his head and his hands, paid homage to them.

2.21.s:
tatastau prītamanasau samuthāpya ca sattamam /
āśīrbhirabhinandetāṃ pṛthak pṛthagubhāvapi //
2.21.d:
ततस्तौ प्रीतमनसौ समुथाप्य च सत्तमम् ।
आशीर्भिरभिनन्देतां पृथक् पृथगुभावपि ॥
2.21.m: Then, raising up the excellent youth with delighted minds, / both of them welcomed him, each with blessings.

2.21.s:
tamāśliṣyāṅkamāropya harṇāśruplutalocanau /
vīkṣantau tanmukhāṃbhojaṃ paraṃ harṣamavāpatuḥ //
2.21.d:
तमाश्लिष्याङ्कमारोप्य हर्णाश्रुप्लुतलोचनौ ।
वीक्षन्तौ तन्मुखांभोजं परं हर्षमवापतुः ॥
2.21.m: Embracing him and taking him upon their laps, their eyes flooded with tears of joy, / they experienced supreme delight gazing upon his lotus face.

2.21.s:
tataḥ sukhopaviṣṭaṃ tamātmavaṃśasamudvaham /
anāmayamapṛcchetāṃ tāvubhau daṃpatī tadā //
2.21.d:
ततः सुखोपविष्टं तमात्मवंशसमुद्वहम् ।
अनामयमपृच्छेतां तावुभौ दंपती तदा ॥
2.21.m: Then, as that perpetuator of their lineage was comfortably seated, / the couple asked him about his welfare:

2.21.s:
pitarau te kuśalino vatsa kiṃbhrātarastathā /
anāyāsena te vṛttirvartate cātha karhicit //
2.21.d:
पितरौ ते कुशलिनो वत्स किंभ्रातरस्तथा ।
अनायासेन ते वृत्तिर्वर्तते चाथ कर्हिचित् ॥
2.21.m: "Child, are your parents well, and likewise your brothers? / And does your livelihood proceed without hardship at all times?"

2.21.s:
samastābhyāṃ tato rājannācacakṣe yathoditaḥ /
tathā svānugataṃ pitrorbhrātṝṇāṃ caiva ceṣṭitam //
2.21.d:
समस्ताभ्यां ततो राजन्नाचचक्षे यथोदितः ।
तथा स्वानुगतं पित्रोर्भ्रातॄणां चैव चेष्टितम् ॥
2.21.m: Then, O king, as he was questioned, he reported fully to both of them / all the activities of his parents and brothers, and how he obeyed them.

2.21.s:
evaṃ tayormahārāja satprītijanitaiguṇaiḥ /
prīyamāṇo 'vasadrāmaḥ pituḥ pitrornniveśane //
2.21.d:
एवं तयोर्महाराज सत्प्रीतिजनितैगुणैः ।
प्रीयमाणो ऽवसद्रामः पितुः पित्रोर्न्निवेशने ॥
2.21.m: Thus, O great king, cherished by them with qualities born of true affection, / Rāma dwelt in the abode of his father's parents.

2.21.s:
sa tasminsarvabhūtānāṃ manonayananandanaḥ /
uvāsa katicinmāsāṃstacchuśrūṣāparāyaṇaḥ //
2.21.d:
स तस्मिन्सर्वभूतानां मनोनयननन्दनः ।
उवास कतिचिन्मासांस्तच्छुश्रूषापरायणः ॥
2.21.m: Gladdening the minds and eyes of all living beings, / he lived there for a few months, devoted to serving them.

2.21.s:
athānujñāpya tau rājanbhṛguvaryo mahāmanāḥ /
pitāmahagurorgantumiyeṣāśrayamāśramam //
2.21.d:
अथानुज्ञाप्य तौ राजन्भृगुवर्यो महामनाः ।
पितामहगुरोर्गन्तुमियेषाश्रयमाश्रमम् ॥
2.21.m: Then, having taken leave of the two, O king, that noble-minded best of the Bhṛgus / desired to go to the shelter, the hermitage of his grandfather's elder.

2.21.s:
sa tābhyāṃ prītiyuktābhyāmāśīrbhirabhinanditaḥ /
yathā cābhyāṃ pradiṣṭena yayā vaurvāśramaṃ prati //
2.21.d:
स ताभ्यां प्रीतियुक्ताभ्यामाशीर्भिरभिनन्दितः ।
यथा चाभ्यां प्रदिष्टेन यया वौर्वाश्रमं प्रति ॥
2.21.m: Congratulated with blessings by the two who were filled with love, / he set out toward the hermitage of Ūrva along the path indicated by them.

2.21.s:
taṃ namaskṛtya vidhivaccyavanaṃ ca mahātapāḥ /
sapraharṣaṃ tadājñātaḥ prayayāvāśramaṃ bhṛgoḥ //
2.21.d:
तं नमस्कृत्य विधिवच्च्यवनं च महातपाः ।
सप्रहर्षं तदाज्ञातः प्रययावाश्रमं भृगोः ॥
2.21.m: Having duly paid homage to him and to Cyavana of great austerities, / permitted by them, he joyfully went forth to the hermitage of Bhṛgu.

2.21.s:
sa gatvāmunimukhyasya bhṛgorāśramamaṇḍalam /
dadarśa śāntacetobhirmunibhiḥ sarvato vṛtam //
2.21.d:
स गत्वामुनिमुख्यस्य भृगोराश्रममण्डलम् ।
ददर्श शान्तचेतोभिर्मुनिभिः सर्वतो वृतम् ॥
2.21.m: Arriving at the precinct of the hermitage of Bhṛgu, foremost among sages, / he saw it surrounded on all sides by sages of tranquil mind,

2.21.s:
susnigdhaśītalacchāyaiḥ sarvartukaguṇānvitaiḥ /
tarubhiḥ saṃvṛtaṃ prītaḥ phalapuṣpottarānvitaiḥ //
2.21.d:
सुस्निग्धशीतलच्छायैः सर्वर्तुकगुणान्वितैः ।
तरुभिः संवृतं प्रीतः फलपुष्पोत्तरान्वितैः ॥
2.21.m: surrounded by trees with very glossy, cool shade, endowed with the virtues of all seasons, / bearing an abundance of fruit and flowers, delighting [the visitor],

2.21.s:
nānākhagakulārāvairmanaḥśrotrasukhāvahaiḥ /
brahmaghoṣaiśca vividhaiḥ sarvataḥ pratināditam //
2.21.d:
नानाखगकुलारावैर्मनःश्रोत्रसुखावहैः ।
ब्रह्मघोषैश्च विविधैः सर्वतः प्रतिनादितम् ॥
2.21.m: resounding on all sides with the cries of various flocks of birds bringing joy to mind and ear, / and with manifold recitations of the Veda,

2.21.s:
samantrāhutihomotthadhūmagandhena sarvataḥ /
nirastanikhilāghaughaṃ vanāntaravisarpiṇā //
2.21.d:
समन्त्राहुतिहोमोत्थधूमगन्धेन सर्वतः ।
निरस्तनिखिलाघौघं वनान्तरविसर्पिणा ॥
2.21.m: having the entire multitude of sins dispelled on every side / by the scent of smoke rising from the offering of oblations with mantras, wafting through the forest,

2.21.s:
samitkuśāharairdaṇḍamekhalājinamaṇḍitaiḥ /
abhitaḥ śobhitaṃ rājanramyairmunikumārakaiḥ //
2.21.d:
समित्कुशाहरैर्दण्डमेखलाजिनमण्डितैः ।
अभितः शोभितं राजन्रम्यैर्मुनिकुमारकैः ॥
2.21.m: adorned round about, O king, by charming young ascetic boys / carrying firewood and kuśa grass, adorned with staffs, girdles, and antelope skins,

2.21.s:
prasūnajalasaṃpūrmapātrahastābhirantarā /
śobhitaṃ munikalyābhiścarantībhiritastataḥ //
2.21.d:
प्रसूनजलसंपूर्मपात्रहस्ताभिरन्तरा ।
शोभितं मुनिकल्याभिश्चरन्तीभिरितस्ततः ॥
2.21.m: beautified by the daughters of sages walking here and there, / with vessels filled with flowers and water in their hands,

2.21.s:
sapotahariṇīyūthairvisraṃbhādaviśaṅkibhiḥ /
uṭajāṅgaṇaparyantatarucchāyāsvadhiṣṭhitam //
2.21.d:
सपोतहरिणीयूथैर्विस्रंभादविशङ्किभिः ।
उटजाङ्गणपर्यन्ततरुच्छायास्वधिष्ठितम् ॥
2.21.m: occupied in the shade of trees bordering the cottage courtyards / by herds of does with their fawns, fearless out of trust,

2.21.s:
romanthataḥ parāmṛṣṭiyūtha sākṣikamutpradaiḥ /
prārabdhatāṇḍavaṃ kekīmayūrairmadhurasvaraiḥ //
2.21.d:
रोमन्थतः परामृष्टियूथ साक्षिकमुत्प्रदैः ।
प्रारब्धताण्डवं केकीमयूरैर्मधुरस्वरैः ॥
2.21.m: where dance was begun with sweet cries by peacocks, / observed by herds of beasts peacefully chewing the cud and giving joy,

2.21.s:
pravikīrṇakaṇoddeśaṃ mṛgaśabdaiḥ samīpagaiḥ /
anālīḍhātapacchāyāśuṣyannīvārarāśibhiḥ //
2.21.d:
प्रविकीर्णकणोद्देशं मृगशब्दैः समीपगैः ।
अनालीढातपच्छायाशुष्यन्नीवारराशिभिः ॥
2.21.m: with areas where grains were scattered, nearby sounds of deer, / and heaps of wild nīvāra rice drying in the shaded heat untouched [by pests],

2.21.s:
hūyamānānalaṃ kāle pūjyamānātithivrajam /
abhyasyamānacchandaughaṃ cintyamānagamoditam //
2.21.d:
हूयमानानलं काले पूज्यमानातिथिव्रजम् ।
अभ्यस्यमानच्छन्दौघं चिन्त्यमानगमोदितम् ॥
2.21.m: where fires were fed with oblations at the proper time, crowds of guests were honoured, / the multitude of Vedic metres was recited, and the teachings of the sacred scriptures were contemplated.

2.21.s:
paṭhyamānākhilasmārttaṃ śrautārthapravicāraṇam /
prārabdhapitṛdevejyaṃ sarvabhūtamanoharam //
2.21.d:
पठ्यमानाखिलस्मार्त्तं श्रौतार्थप्रविचारणम् ।
प्रारब्धपितृदेवेज्यं सर्वभूतमनोहरम् ॥
2.21.m: where all the Smṛti texts were being recited, and the meaning of the Śruti was investigated, / where offerings to the ancestors and gods had commenced, captivating every creature,

2.21.s:
tapasvijanabhūyiṣṭhamākāpuruṣasevitam /
tapovṛddhikaraṃ puṇyaṃ sarvasattvasukhāspadam //
2.21.d:
तपस्विजनभूयिष्ठमाकापुरुषसेवितम् ।
तपोवृद्धिकरं पुण्यं सर्वसत्त्वसुखास्पदम् ॥
2.21.m: abounding in ascetics, frequented by foremost men, / fostering austerities, holy, the abode of happiness for all living beings,

2.21.s:
tapodhanānandakaraṃ brahmalokamivāparam /
prasūnasaurabhabhrāmyanmadhupārāvanāditam //
2.21.d:
तपोधनानन्दकरं ब्रह्मलोकमिवापरम् ।
प्रसूनसौरभभ्राम्यन्मधुपारावनादितम् ॥
2.21.m: giving joy to those whose wealth is penance, like a second world of Brahmā, / made resonant with the humming of bees hovering around the fragrance of flowers,

2.21.s:
sarvato vījyamānena vividhena nabhasvatā /
evaṃvidhaguṇopetaṃ paśyannāśramamuttamam //
2.21.d:
सर्वतो वीज्यमानेन विविधेन नभस्वता ।
एवंविधगुणोपेतं पश्यन्नाश्रममुत्तमम् ॥
2.21.m: fanned on all sides by varied breezes. / Beholding that excellent hermitage endowed with such virtues,

2.21.s:
praviveśa vinītātmā sukṛtīvāmarālayam /
saṃpraviśyaśramopāntaṃ rāmaḥ svaprapitāmaham //
2.21.d:
प्रविवेश विनीतात्मा सुकृतीवामरालयम् ।
संप्रविश्यश्रमोपान्तं रामः स्वप्रपितामहम् ॥
2.21.m: he entered with a humble mind, like a meritorious man entering the abode of the gods. / Having entered the precincts of the hermitage, Rāma [beheld] his great-grandfather;

2.21.s:
dadarśa parito rājanmuniśiṣyaśatāvṛtam /
vyākhyānavedikāmadhye niviṣṭaṃ kuśaviṣṭare /
sitaśmaśrujaṭākūrcabrahmasūtropaśobhitam //
2.21.d:
ददर्श परितो राजन्मुनिशिष्यशतावृतम् ।
व्याख्यानवेदिकामध्ये निविष्टं कुशविष्टरे ।
सितश्मश्रुजटाकूर्चब्रह्मसूत्रोपशोभितम् ॥
2.21.m: he saw him surrounded on all sides by hundreds of ascetic disciples, O king, / seated in the middle of a discourse platform upon a mat of kuśa grass, / adorned with a white beard, matted hair, a whisk, and the sacred thread,

2.21.s: vāmetarorumadhyāsta vāmajaṅghena jānunā //
2.21.d: वामेतरोरुमध्यास्त वामजङ्घेन जानुना ॥
2.21.m: with his left knee and shank resting upon the middle of his right thigh,

2.21.s:
yogapaṭṭena saṃvītasvadehamṛṣipuṅgavam /
vyākhyānamudrāvilasatsavyapāṇitalāṃbujam //
2.21.d:
योगपट्टेन संवीतस्वदेहमृषिपुङ्गवम् ।
व्याख्यानमुद्राविलसत्सव्यपाणितलांबुजम् ॥
2.21.m: that bull among sages, his body bound by a meditation band, / the lotus of his right palm radiant in the posture of exposition,

2.21.s:
yogapaṭṭoparinyastavibhrājadvāmapāṇikam /
samyagāraṇyavākyānāṃ sūkṣmatattvārthasaṃhatim //
2.21.d:
योगपट्टोपरिन्यस्तविभ्राजद्वामपाणिकम् ।
सम्यगारण्यवाक्यानां सूक्ष्मतत्त्वार्थसंहतिम् ॥
2.21.m: his left hand resting shining upon the meditation band, / who, fully explaining the aggregate of subtle and true meanings of the forest texts,

2.21.s:
vivṛtya munimukhyebhyaḥ śrāvayantaṃ taponidhim /
pituḥ pitāmahaṃ ddaṣṭvā rāmastasya mahātmanaḥ //
2.21.d:
विवृत्य मुनिमुख्येभ्यः श्रावयन्तं तपोनिधिम् ।
पितुः पितामहं द्दष्ट्वा रामस्तस्य महात्मनः ॥
2.21.m: was expounding them to the foremost sages, that treasury of penance. / Seeing the grandfather of his father, that great-souled one,

2.21.s:
śanairivamahārāja samīpaṃ samupāgamat /
tamāgatamupālakṣya tatprabhāvapradharṣitāḥ //
2.21.d:
शनैरिवमहाराज समीपं समुपागमत् ।
तमागतमुपालक्ष्य तत्प्रभावप्रधर्षिताः ॥
2.21.m: Rāma slowly approached near, O great king. / Perceiving him arrived, overwhelmed by his splendour,

2.21.s:
śaṅkāmavāpurmunayo dūrādevākhilā nṛpa /
tāvadūbhṛgurameyātmā tadāgamanatoṣitaḥ //
2.21.d:
शङ्कामवापुर्मुनयो दूरादेवाखिला नृप ।
तावदूभृगुरमेयात्मा तदागमनतोषितः ॥
2.21.m: all the sages felt apprehension from afar, O king. / Meanwhile, the immeasurable Bhṛgu, pleased with his arrival,

2.21.s:
nivṛttānyakathālāpastaṃ paśyannāsa pārthiva /
rāmo 'pi tamupāgamya vinayāvanatānanaḥ //
2.21.d:
निवृत्तान्यकथालापस्तं पश्यन्नास पार्थिव ।
रामो ऽपि तमुपागम्य विनयावनताननः ॥
2.21.m: ceased all other conversation and sat looking at him, O protector of the earth. / Rāma also approached him, his face bowed in humility,

2.21.s:
avandata yathānyayamupendra iva vedhasam /
abhivādya yathānyāyaṃ khyātiṃ ca vinayānvitaḥ //
2.21.d:
अवन्दत यथान्ययमुपेन्द्र इव वेधसम् ।
अभिवाद्य यथान्यायं ख्यातिं च विनयान्वितः ॥
2.21.m: and bowed down according to custom, like Upendra before the Creator. / Having properly saluted him and Khyāti with humility,

2.21.s:
tāṃśca saṃbhāvayāmāsa munīnrāmoyathāvayaḥ /
taiśca sarvairmudopetairāśīrbhirabhivarddhitaḥ //
2.21.d:
तांश्च संभावयामास मुनीन्रामोयथावयः ।
तैश्च सर्वैर्मुदोपेतैराशीर्भिरभिवर्द्धितः ॥
2.21.m: Rāma honoured those sages according to their age. / Augmented with blessings by all of them, who were filled with joy,

2.21.s:
upāviveśa medhāvī bhūmau teṣāmanujñayā /
upaviṣṭaṃ tato rāmamāśīrbhirabhinanditam //
2.21.d:
उपाविवेश मेधावी भूमौ तेषामनुज्ञया ।
उपविष्टं ततो राममाशीर्भिरभिनन्दितम् ॥
2.21.m: the wise one sat down on the ground with their permission. / Seeing Rāma thus seated and greeted with blessings,

2.21.s:
papracchakuśalapraśnaṃ tamālokya bhṛgustadā /
kuśalaṃ khalu te vatsa pitrośca kimanāmayam //
2.21.d:
पप्रच्छकुशलप्रश्नं तमालोक्य भृगुस्तदा ।
कुशलं खलु ते वत्स पित्रोश्च किमनामयम् ॥
2.21.m: Bhṛgu then asked him concerning his welfare: / “Is it well with you, dear child, and is there health for your parents,

2.21.s:
bhrātṝṇāṃ caiva bhavataḥpituḥ pitrostathaiva ca /
kimarthamāgato 'tra tvamadhunāmama sannidhim //
2.21.d:
भ्रातॄणां चैव भवतःपितुः पित्रोस्तथैव च ।
किमर्थमागतो ऽत्र त्वमधुनामम सन्निधिम् ॥
2.21.m: and for your brothers, as well as for your father's parents? / For what purpose have you now come here to my presence?

2.21.s:
kenāpi vā tvamādiṣṭaḥ svayamevāthavāgataḥ /
tatorāmo yathānyāyaṃ tasmai sarvamaśeṣataḥ //
2.21.d:
केनापि वा त्वमादिष्टः स्वयमेवाथवागतः ।
ततोरामो यथान्यायं तस्मै सर्वमशेषतः ॥
2.21.m: Were you sent by someone, or have you come of your own accord?” / Then Rāma properly and completely recounted to him

2.21.s:
kathayāmāsa yatpṛṣṭaṃ tadā tena mahātmanā /
piturmātuśca vṛttānta bhrātṝṇāṃ ca mahātmanām //
2.21.d:
कथयामास यत्पृष्टं तदा तेन महात्मना ।
पितुर्मातुश्च वृत्तान्त भ्रातॄणां च महात्मनाम् ॥
2.21.m: all that was asked then by that great soul: / the condition of his father, his mother, and his great-souled brothers,

2.21.s:
pituḥ pritroścakauśalya darśanaṃ ca tayornṛpa /
etadanyacca sakalaṃ bhṛgoḥ sapraśrayaṃ mudā //
2.21.d:
पितुः प्रित्रोश्चकौशल्य दर्शनं च तयोर्नृप ।
एतदन्यच्च सकलं भृगोः सप्रश्रयं मुदा ॥
2.21.m: the welfare of his father’s parents, and their seeing him, O king. / All this and everything else he humbly and joyfully reported to Bhṛgu,

2.21.s:
nyavedayadyathānyāyamātmanaśca samīhitam /
śrutvaitadakhilaṃ rājanrāmeṇa samudīritam //
2.21.d:
न्यवेदयद्यथान्यायमात्मनश्च समीहितम् ।
श्रुत्वैतदखिलं राजन्रामेण समुदीरितम् ॥
2.21.m: duly making known his own desire. / Having heard all this spoken by Rāma, O king,

2.21.s:
taṃ ca dṛṣṭvā viśeṣeṇa bhṛguḥ prīto 'bhyanandata /
evaṃ tasya priyaṃ kurvannutkṛṣṭairātmakarmabhiḥ //
2.21.d:
तं च दृष्ट्वा विशेषेण भृगुः प्रीतो ऽभ्यनन्दत ।
एवं तस्य प्रियं कुर्वन्नुत्कृष्टैरात्मकर्मभिः ॥
2.21.m: and seeing him especially, Bhṛgu was delighted and welcomed him. / Thus pleasing him through his own excellent deeds,

2.21.s:
tatrāśrame 'vasadrāmo dināni katicinnṛpa /
tataḥ kadācidekānte rāmaṃ munivarottamaḥ //
2.21.d:
तत्राश्रमे ऽवसद्रामो दिनानि कतिचिन्नृप ।
ततः कदाचिदेकान्ते रामं मुनिवरोत्तमः ॥
2.21.m: Rāma dwelt in that hermitage for some days, O king. / Then once, in a secluded spot, that best of eminent sages

2.21.s:
vatsāgaccheti taṃ rājannupāhvayadupahvare /
so 'bhigamya tamāsīnamabhivādya kṛtāñjaliḥ //
2.21.d:
वत्सागच्छेति तं राजन्नुपाह्वयदुपह्वरे ।
सो ऽभिगम्य तमासीनमभिवाद्य कृताञ्जलिः ॥
2.21.m: called him aside, saying: “Come, dear child!” / Approaching him as he sat, Rāma bowed with folded hands

2.21.s:
tasthau tatpurato rāmaḥ suprītenāntarātmanā /
āśīrbhirabhinandyātha bhṛgustaṃ prīta mānasaḥ //
2.21.d:
तस्थौ तत्पुरतो रामः सुप्रीतेनान्तरात्मना ।
आशीर्भिरभिनन्द्याथ भृगुस्तं प्रीत मानसः ॥
2.21.m: and stood before him with a joyful inner self. / Having greeted him with blessings, Bhṛgu, with a delighted mind,

2.21.s:
prāha nādhigatāśaṅkaṃ rāmamālokya sādaram /
śruṇu vatsa vaco mahya yattvāṃ vakṣyāmi sāṃpratam //
2.21.d:
प्राह नाधिगताशङ्कं राममालोक्य सादरम् ।
श्रुणु वत्स वचो मह्य यत्त्वां वक्ष्यामि सांप्रतम् ॥
2.21.m: spoke respectfully to Rāma, whose doubts were removed: / “Listen, dear child, to my word which I shall speak to you now,

2.21.s:
hitārthaṃ sarvalokānāṃ tava cāsmākameva ca /
gaccha putra mamādeśāddhimavantaṃ mahāgirim //
2.21.d:
हितार्थं सर्वलोकानां तव चास्माकमेव च ।
गच्छ पुत्र ममादेशाद्धिमवन्तं महागिरिम् ॥
2.21.m: for the benefit of all the worlds, of yourself, and of ourselves. / Go, son, by my command to the great mountain Himavat,

2.21.s:
adhunaivāśramādasmāttapase dhṛtamānasaḥ /
tatragatvā mahābhāga kṛtvāśramāpadaṃ śubham //
2.21.d:
अधुनैवाश्रमादस्मात्तपसे धृतमानसः ।
तत्रगत्वा महाभाग कृत्वाश्रमापदं शुभम् ॥
2.21.m: this very moment from this hermitage, with your mind resolved upon austerity. / Having gone there, O fortunate one, and made an auspicious hermitage,

2.21.s:
ārādhaya mahādevaṃ tapasā niyamena ca /
prītimutpādya tasya tvaṃ bhaktyānanyagayā cirāt //
2.21.d:
आराधय महादेवं तपसा नियमेन च ।
प्रीतिमुत्पाद्य तस्य त्वं भक्त्यानन्यगया चिरात् ॥
2.21.m: worship Mahādeva with austerity and self-restraint. / Producing his pleasure after a long time through undivided devotion,

2.21.s:
śreyo mahadavāpnoṣi nātra kāryā vijāraṇā /
tarasā tava bhaktyā ca prīto bhavati śaṅkaraḥ //
2.21.d:
श्रेयो महदवाप्नोषि नात्र कार्या विजारणा ।
तरसा तव भक्त्या च प्रीतो भवति शङ्करः ॥
2.21.m: you will attain great welfare; no doubt should be entertained in this matter. / Śaṅkara is swiftly pleased by your power and devotion,

2.21.s:
kariṣyati ca te sarvaṃ manasā yadyadicchasi /
tuṣṭe tasmiñjagannāthe śaṅkare bhaktavatsale //
2.21.d:
करिष्यति च ते सर्वं मनसा यद्यदिच्छसि ।
तुष्टे तस्मिञ्जगन्नाथे शङ्करे भक्तवत्सले ॥
2.21.m: and he will grant you everything, whatever you wish in your mind. / When that lord of the universe, Śaṅkara, affectionate to devotees, is satisfied,

2.21.s:
astragrāmamaśeṣaṃ tvaṃ vaṇu putra yathepsitam /
tvayā hitārthaṃ devānāṃ karaṇīyaṃ suduṣkaram //
2.21.d:
अस्त्रग्राममशेषं त्वं वणु पुत्र यथेप्सितम् ।
त्वया हितार्थं देवानां करणीयं सुदुष्करम् ॥
2.21.m: choose, my son, the entire host of divine weapons as you desire. / For the welfare of the gods, a most difficult task must be performed by you;

2.21.s:
vidyate 'bhyadhikaṃ karma śastrasādhyamanekaśaḥ /
tasmāttvaṃ devadeveśaṃ samārādhaya śaṅkaram //
2.21.d:
विद्यते ऽभ्यधिकं कर्म शस्त्रसाध्यमनेकशः ।
तस्मात्त्वं देवदेवेशं समाराधय शङ्करम् ॥
2.21.m: there is abundant work to be accomplished many times by weapons. / Therefore, propitiate Śaṅkara, the lord of the god of gods,

2.21.s:
bhaktyā paramayā yuktastato 'bhīṣṭamavāpsyasi //
iti śrībrahmāṇḍe mahāpurāṇe vāyuprokte madhyabhāge tṛtīya upoddhātapāde ekaviṃśati tamaudhyāyaḥ // 21//
2.21.d:
भक्त्या परमया युक्तस्ततो ऽभीष्टमवाप्स्यसि ॥
इति श्रीब्रह्माण्डे महापुराणे वायुप्रोक्ते मध्यभागे तृतीय उपोद्धातपादे एकविंशति तमौध्यायः ॥ 21॥
2.21.m:
endowed with supreme devotion; from that you will obtain what you desire.”

Thus ends the twenty-first chapter in the third Upoddhātapāda of the middle section of the glorious Brahmāṇḍa Mahāpurāṇa spoken by Vāyu. // 21

2.22.s:
vasiṣṭha uvāca
ityevamukto bhṛguṇā tathetyuktvā praṇamya ca /
rāmastenābhyanujñātaścakāra gamane manaḥ //
2.22.d:
वसिष्ठ उवाच
इत्येवमुक्तो भृगुणा तथेत्युक्त्वा प्रणम्य च ।
रामस्तेनाभ्यनुज्ञातश्चकार गमने मनः ॥
2.22.m: Vasiṣṭha said: / Thus addressed by Bhṛgu, saying “So be it” and bowing down, / Rāma, permitted by him, set his mind on departure.

2.22.s:
bhṛguṃ khyātiṃ ca vidhivatparikramya praṇamyaca /
pariṣvaktastathā tābhyāmāśīrbhirābhinanditaḥ //
2.22.d:
भृगुं ख्यातिं च विधिवत्परिक्रम्य प्रणम्यच ।
परिष्वक्तस्तथा ताभ्यामाशीर्भिराभिनन्दितः ॥
2.22.m: Having duly circumambulated and bowed down to Bhṛgu and Khyāti, / embraced by the two and greeted with blessings,

2.22.s:
munīṃśca tānnamaskṛtya taiḥ sarvairanumoditaḥ /
niścakramāśramāttasmāttapase kṛtaniścayaḥ //
2.22.d:
मुनींश्च तान्नमस्कृत्य तैः सर्वैरनुमोदितः ।
निश्चक्रमाश्रमात्तस्मात्तपसे कृतनिश्चयः ॥
2.22.m: and having bowed to those sages and received the approval of them all, / he departed from that hermitage, resolved upon austerity.

2.22.s:
tato guruniyogena taduktenaiva vartmanā /
himavantaṃ girivaraṃ yayau rāmo mahāmanāḥ //
2.22.d:
ततो गुरुनियोगेन तदुक्तेनैव वर्त्मना ।
हिमवन्तं गिरिवरं ययौ रामो महामनाः ॥
2.22.m: Then, by the master’s direction, along the very path indicated by him, / the high-minded Rāma went to Himavat, the foremost of mountains.
Passing through various lands, mountains, and rivers, / forests, and the dwellings of foremost sages, he proceeded slowly.

2.22.s:
tatratatra nivāseṣu munīnāṃ nivasanpathi /
tīrtheṣu kṣetramukhyeṣu nivasanvā yayau śanaiḥ //
2.22.d:
तत्रतत्र निवासेषु मुनीनां निवसन्पथि ।
तीर्थेषु क्षेत्रमुख्येषु निवसन्वा ययौ शनैः ॥
2.22.m: Dwelling here and there along the way in the residences of the sages, / and staying at holy bathing places and prominent sacred fields, he went slowly.

2.22.s:
atītya subahūndeśānpaśyannapi manoramān /
āsasādaca laśreṣṭhaṃ himavantamanuttamam //
2.22.d:
अतीत्य सुबहून्देशान्पश्यन्नपि मनोरमान् ।
आससादच लश्रेष्ठं हिमवन्तमनुत्तमम् ॥
2.22.m: Traversing very many lands and beholding delightful places, / he reached Himavat, the supreme, the foremost of mountains.

2.22.s:
sa gatvā parvatavaraṃ nānādrumalatāsthitam /
dadarśa vipulaiḥ śṛṅgairullikhantamivāṃbaram //
2.22.d:
स गत्वा पर्वतवरं नानाद्रुमलतास्थितम् ।
ददर्श विपुलैः शृङ्गैरुल्लिखन्तमिवांबरम् ॥
2.22.m: Having reached that best of mountains, covered with various trees and creepers, / he saw it as if scratching the sky with its vast peaks,
adorned with regions variegated by diverse minerals, / beautified all around by radiant gems and medicinal plants,
in some places burning anew with high wind-swept fire / born from dry trees rubbed together by the impact of the wind,
in some places with forest fires extinguished by water produced from melting snow-rocks / due to fires of sun-stones blazing when touched by the sun's rays,
in some places its forest lit up with rays of radiance from masses of crystal, antimony, silver, and gold / casting flashing reflections upon one another,
in some places its forest illuminated by hosts of Siddhas wet with snow / who resorted to the morning sun on the rock-surfaces of the foothills,
in some places its borders illuminated by hosts of Yakṣas / resting on gold rocks intersected by sunbeams, appearing as if entering fire.
In some places the caves were filled with the anguished cries of herds of deer, / agitated by the leaping out of hyenas emerging from cavern mouths;
in some places the slopes of trees and beautiful large rocks were violently struck / by the troop-leaders of boars and tigers fighting here and there;
in some places the slopes of the rocky plateaus were trampled by the hooves of wild oxen, / pursued by female elephants alarmed at the sight of their calves;
in some places the groves of large boulders were crushed by fighting bull-elephants / maddened by surging rut for the sake of females;
in some places the rocks were shattered by the claws and trampled by the paws of lions / charging at elephants in fury upon hearing their trumpeting;

2.22.s:
sahasā nipatatsiṃhanakhanirbhinnamastakaiḥ /
gajairākrandanādena pūryamāmaṃ vanaṃ kvacit //
2.22.d:
सहसा निपतत्सिंहनखनिर्भिन्नमस्तकैः ।
गजैराक्रन्दनादेन पूर्यमामं वनं क्वचित् ॥
2.22.m: in some places the forest was filled with the wailing roars / of elephants whose heads were torn open by the claws of suddenly pouncing lions;
in some places the deep recesses of all the rocks were split open by the fierce claws / of the eight-legged śarabhas forcefully tearing at lions;
in some places the stones were smashed in the mutual clash / of troop-leaders of bears confronted by numerous enraged hunters;
in some places the forest was occupied by bull-elephants sporting with cow-elephants in mountain bowers, / and by rutting elephants charging after female elephants;
hundreds of its caves were filled with the breath-winds of sleeping lions' mouths, / and deer roamed anxiously in the thickets out of great dread;
it was frequented by herds of yaks wandering very slowly, / fearful of their tail-hairs breaking when entangled in thorns;
the quarters of the sky were completely filled with soaring, rhythmic melodies / uttered by Kinnara women dwelling in the mountain caves;
the ground was imprinted with the feet wet with red lac-juice / of forest deities wandering here and there;

2.22.s:
mayūrakekirīvṛndaiḥ saṃgīta madhurasvaraiḥ /
pravṛttanṛttaṃ parito vitatodagrabarhibhiḥ //
2.22.d:
मयूरकेकिरीवृन्दैः संगीत मधुरस्वरैः ।
प्रवृत्तनृत्तं परितो विततोदग्रबर्हिभिः ॥
2.22.m: dances were begun all around by flocks of peacocks with outstretched upright tails, / accompanied by the sweet-voiced singing of peacocks;
it was gently fanned by forest breezes that brought delight to the body, / showering cascades of numerous water-grown and land-grown flowers;
the margins of the mango groves were thrown into excitement / by the calls of male cuckoos intoxicated by tasting the sweet juice of the spring season;
it was made to resound with the singing of bees intoxicated by the nectar of various flowers, / and the forest was deafened by the calls of countless birds;
the surface of the earth was adorned with continuous fresh showers of flowers / moist with streams of honey and scattered by the forest winds;
it was deafened all around by the great roar / of waterfalls cascading from above amid rugged stones;
it was shaded by spreading branches with dense leaves and tree-shadows, / filled with pāṭala trees growing along the forest outskirts,
and by kadaṃba, neem, hintāla, sarja, vedhūka, and tinduka trees, / kapittha, jackfruit, aśoka, mango, inguda, and aśana trees;
by nāgakeśara, campaka, punnāga, kovidāra, and priyaṅgu, / priyāla, nīpa, bakula, bandhūka, akṣa, and tamāla trees;
by grape, madhūka, āmalaka, rose-apple, kaṅkola, and jasmine, / as well as bilva, arjuna, karañja, mango, and citron trees;
by picula, ambaṣṭha, gold-flowered vaikaṅkata, śamī, and dhava trees, / putrajīva, abhayā, ariṣṭa, ironwood, udumbara, and pippala trees;
and adorned all around by other diverse trees, / whose unbroken tree-shadow kept far away
the rays of the sun all around, so that they never reached the forest floor; / it was teeming with monkeys nourished and strengthened by tasting various ripe fruits,
which crowded the frightened rows of hundreds of forests that they overran; / and it was graced here and there by very charming [streams] emerging from rocky caverns;
it was made resplendent, O king, by hundreds of rivers rushing over uneven cascades, / and by vast lakes adorned with white water-lilies and blue lotuses,

2.22.s:
nānāvihagasaṃghuṣṭaiḥ samantādupaśobhitam /
samāsādyatha śailendraṃ tuṣāraśiśiraṃ girim //
2.22.d:
नानाविहगसंघुष्टैः समन्तादुपशोभितम् ।
समासाद्यथ शैलेन्द्रं तुषारशिशिरं गिरिम् ॥
2.22.m: and adorned on all sides by the calls of various birds. / Having thus reached the lord of mountains, the mountain cold with frost,

2.22.s:
āruroha bhaguśreṣṭhastarasā taṃ mudānvitaḥ /
tasya praviśya gahanaṃ vanaṃ rāmo mahāmanāḥ //
2.22.d:
आरुरोह भगुश्रेष्ठस्तरसा तं मुदान्वितः ।
तस्य प्रविश्य गहनं वनं रामो महामनाः ॥
2.22.m: the best of the Bhṛgus climbed it swiftly and filled with joy. / Entering its dense forest, the noble-minded Rāma,

2.22.s:
vicacāra śanai rājannupaśalyamahīruham /
sa tatra vicarandikṣu hariṇībhiḥ samantataḥ //
2.22.d:
विचचार शनै राजन्नुपशल्यमहीरुहम् ।
स तत्र विचरन्दिक्षु हरिणीभिः समन्ततः ॥
2.22.m: O king, walked slowly among the trees at the outskirts of the mountain. / As he wandered about there, watched in all directions

2.22.s:
vikṣyamāṇo mudaṃ lebhe sāśaṅkaṃ mugdhadṛṣṭibhiḥ /
sa tatra kusumāmodagandhibhirvanavāyubhiḥ //
2.22.d:
विक्ष्यमाणो मुदं लेभे साशङ्कं मुग्धदृष्टिभिः ।
स तत्र कुसुमामोदगन्धिभिर्वनवायुभिः ॥
2.22.m: by does with shy, apprehensive glances, he experienced delight. / Fanned there by forest breezes

2.22.s:
vījyamāno jaharṣe sa vīkṣyodārāṃ vanaśriyam /
vividhāśca stharīḥ sūkṣmamuparikramya bhārgavaḥ //
2.22.d:
वीज्यमानो जहर्षे स वीक्ष्योदारां वनश्रियम् ।
विविधाश्च स्थरीः सूक्ष्ममुपरिक्रम्य भार्गवः ॥
2.22.m: fragrant with the scent of flowers, he rejoiced upon seeing the majestic beauty of the forest. / The Bhārgava, having ascended carefully to the various plateaus,

2.22.d:
द्वन्द्वांश्च धातून्विविधान्पश्यन्नेवमतर्कयत् ।
अहो ऽयं सर्वशैलानामाधिपत्ये ऽभिषेचितः ॥
2.22.m: and beholding pairs [of creatures] and various minerals, reflected thus: / 'Ah, this mountain was consecrated to sovereignty over all mountains

2.22.s:
brahmaṇā yajñabhākcaiva sthāne saṃpratipāditaḥ /
asya śailādhirājatvaṃ suvyaktamabhilakṣyate //
2.22.d:
ब्रह्मणा यज्ञभाक्चैव स्थाने संप्रतिपादितः ।
अस्य शैलाधिराजत्वं सुव्यक्तमभिलक्ष्यते ॥
2.22.m: by Brahmā and rightfully granted a share in sacrifices; / its supreme kingship over mountains is clearly evident!
Its forests are made melodious by the sounds of whistling bamboos; / with the dense mass of frost clinging to its slopes,
it shines as if wrapped all around in a pure, white upper garment; / and above, with its dense collection of fog and snow,
its body appears as though covered by a multi-coloured upper cloth; / with sandalwood, agallochum, camphor, musk, saffron, and other perfumes,

2.22.d:
अलङ्कृतागः सुव्यक्तं दृश्यते ऽही विलासिवत् ।
मृगेन्द्राहतदन्तीन्द्रकुंभस्थलपरिच्युतैः ॥
2.22.m: its body is adorned, clearly looking like a man of pleasure, O king; / with masses of large pearls fallen from the frontal globes of lordly elephants
struck down by the king of beasts, this mountain shines on every side; / having hair adorned with flowers of various trees, creepers, and climbing plants;
adorned with an unbroken, graceful canopy formed by masses of clouds; / its body variegated with various minerals and embellished with all kinds of gems;
resplendent with a white parasol appearing in the guise of Mount Kailāsa; / surrounded on all sides by herds of elephants and horse-faced Kinnaras;
having mansions in the form of stone caverns with great doors like gem-bearing islands; / seated upon a central throne in the secluded council-chamber of its caves;
having cane-bearers in the form of reed-trees standing closely all around, / unapproachable to common people upon sight, just like an emperor of great kings;
being fanned by the splendid chowries of roaming yaks; / with peacocks dancing before it and Kinnaras singing;
it shines, served by diverse kinds of living beings! / Clearly established in the position of supreme sovereign of mountain lords,

2.22.s:
bhunaktyākramya vasudhāṃ samagrāṃ śriyamojasā /
evaṃ saṃcintayānaḥ sa himādrivanagahvare //
2.22.d:
भुनक्त्याक्रम्य वसुधां समग्रां श्रियमोजसा ।
एवं संचिन्तयानः स हिमाद्रिवनगह्वरे ॥
2.22.m: it enjoys all the earth and complete splendour through its own might.' / Pondering thus in the forest caverns of the snowy mountain,

2.22.s:
vicacāra ciraṃ rāmo mudā paramayā yutaḥ /
āsasāda vane tasminvipule bhṛgupuṅgavaḥ //
2.22.d:
विचचार चिरं रामो मुदा परमया युतः ।
आससाद वने तस्मिन्विपुले भृगुपुङ्गवः ॥
2.22.m: Rāma wandered for a long time, endowed with supreme joy. / In that vast forest, the bull of the Bhṛgus reached
a large lake, O great king, containing pure water, / adorned with masses of white water-lilies, blue lotuses, and white kahlāra flowers,

2.22.s:
paṅkajairutpalaiścaiva raktapītaiḥ sitāsitaiḥ /
anyaiśca jalacairvakṣaiḥ sarvataḥ samalaṅkṛtam //
2.22.d:
पङ्कजैरुत्पलैश्चैव रक्तपीतैः सितासितैः ।
अन्यैश्च जलचैर्वक्षैः सर्वतः समलङ्कृतम् ॥
2.22.m: decorated on all sides with red, yellow, white, and dark / lotuses and water-lilies, and other water-growing plants,
and by hundreds of swans, cranes, water-hens, and kāraṇḍava ducks, / partridges, cakravāka birds, ospreys, and swarms of bees.

2.22.s:
saṃghuṣyamāṇaṃ paritaḥ sevitaṃ mandavāyunā /
śapharīmatsyasaṃghaiśca vicaradbhiritastataḥ //
2.22.d:
संघुष्यमाणं परितः सेवितं मन्दवायुना ।
शफरीमत्स्यसंघैश्च विचरद्भिरितस्ततः ॥
2.22.m: resounded on all sides, served by gentle breezes, / and by swarms of carp darting to and fro,
seeming to dance all around with waves generated within, / that excellent lake the best of the Bhṛgus approached.

2.22.s:
nānāpatatrrivirutairmadhurīkṛtadiktaṭam /
sa tasya tīre vipulaṃ kṛtvāśramapadaṃ śubham //
2.22.d:
नानापतत्र्रिविरुतैर्मधुरीकृतदिक्तटम् ।
स तस्य तीरे विपुलं कृत्वाश्रमपदं शुभम् ॥
2.22.m: Having made a spacious, auspicious hermitage upon its bank, / whose horizons were made sweet with the cries of diverse birds,

2.22.s:
rāmo matimatāṃ śreṣṭhastapase ca mano dadhe /
śākamūlaphalāhāro niyataṃ niyatendriyaḥ //
2.22.d:
रामो मतिमतां श्रेष्ठस्तपसे च मनो दधे ।
शाकमूलफलाहारो नियतं नियतेन्द्रियः ॥
2.22.m: Rāma, the foremost of the wise, set his mind on ascetic practice, / eating only vegetables, roots, and fruits, restrained and with senses subdued.

2.22.s:
tapaścacāra deveśaṃ viniveśyātmamānase /
bhṛgūpadiṣṭamārgeṇa bhaktyā paramayā yutaḥ //
2.22.d:
तपश्चचार देवेशं विनिवेश्यात्ममानसे ।
भृगूपदिष्टमार्गेण भक्त्या परमया युतः ॥
2.22.m: Placing the lord of the gods in his own mind, he performed austerity / according to the path taught by Bhṛgu, endowed with supreme devotion.

2.22.s:
pūjayāmāsa deveśamekāgramanasā nṛpa /
aniketaḥ sa varṣāsu śiśire jalasaṃśrayaḥ //
2.22.d:
पूजयामास देवेशमेकाग्रमनसा नृप ।
अनिकेतः स वर्षासु शिशिरे जलसंश्रयः ॥
2.22.m: With one-pointed mind he worshipped the lord of the gods, O king; / homeless in the rainy seasons, resorting to water in the cold season,

2.22.s:
grīṣme pañjāgnimadhyasthaścacāraivaṃ tapaściram /
ripūnnirjitya kāmādīnūrmiṣaṣaṭkaṃ vidhūya ca //
2.22.d:
ग्रीष्मे पञ्जाग्निमध्यस्थश्चचारैवं तपश्चिरम् ।
रिपून्निर्जित्य कामादीनूर्मिषषट्कं विधूय च ॥
2.22.m: and standing amidst five fires in summer, he thus performed long penance, / having conquered enemies such as desire and shaken off the six waves.
With intellect untroubled by pairs of opposites, unagitated by afflictive faults, / his body purified through restraints and observances, composed in mind,

2.22.s:
vaśī cakāra pavanaṃ prāṇāyāmena dehagam /
jitapadmāsano maunī sthiracitto mahāmuniḥ //
2.22.d:
वशी चकार पवनं प्राणायामेन देहगम् ।
जितपद्मासनो मौनी स्थिरचित्तो महामुनिः ॥
2.22.m: he brought under control the breath residing in the body through prāṇāyāma; / having mastered the lotus posture, silent, with steady mind, the great sage

2.22.s:
vaśī cakāra cākṣāṇi pratyāhāraparāyaṇaḥ /
dhāraṇābhiḥ sthirīcakre manaścañcalamātmavān //
2.22.d:
वशी चकार चाक्षाणि प्रत्याहारपरायणः ।
धारणाभिः स्थिरीचक्रे मनश्चञ्चलमात्मवान् ॥
2.22.m: subdued the senses, intent upon withdrawal; / with concentrations the self-possessed ascetic steadied the flickering mind.

2.22.s:
dhyānena devadeveśaṃ dadarśa parameśvaram /
svasthāntaḥ karaṇo maitraḥ sarvabādhāvivarjitaḥ //
2.22.d:
ध्यानेन देवदेवेशं ददर्श परमेश्वरम् ।
स्वस्थान्तः करणो मैत्रः सर्वबाधाविवर्जितः ॥
2.22.m: Through meditation he beheld the supreme Lord, the god of gods, / his inner organ tranquil, benevolent, free from all impediments.

2.22.s:
cintayāmāsa deveśaṃ dhyāne dṛṣṭvā jagadgurum /
dhyeyāvasthi tacittātmā niścaledriyadehavān //
2.22.d:
चिन्तयामास देवेशं ध्याने दृष्ट्वा जगद्गुरुम् ।
ध्येयावस्थि तचित्तात्मा निश्चलेद्रियदेहवान् ॥
2.22.m: Having seen the teacher of the world in meditation, he contemplated the lord of the gods, / his mind and self fixed upon the object of meditation, with motionless senses and body.

2.22.s:
ākālāvadhi so 'tiṣṭhannivātasthapradīpavat /
japaṃśca devadeveśaṃ dhyāyaṃśca svamanīṣayā //
2.22.d:
आकालावधि सो ऽतिष्ठन्निवातस्थप्रदीपवत् ।
जपंश्च देवदेवेशं ध्यायंश्च स्वमनीषया ॥
2.22.m: Until the appointed time he stood like a lamp in a windless place, / chanting the name of the god of gods and meditating through his own intellect.

2.22.s:
ārādhayadameyātmā sarvabhāvasthamīśvaram /
tataḥ sa niṣphalaṃ rūpamaiśvaraṃ yannirañjanam //
2.22.d:
आराधयदमेयात्मा सर्वभावस्थमीश्वरम् ।
ततः स निष्फलं रूपमैश्वरं यन्निरञ्जनम् ॥
2.22.m: The immeasurable-souled one propitiated the Lord dwelling in all states of being. / Then, upon that partless divine form which is immaculate,

2.22.s:
paraṃ jyotiracintyaṃ yadyogidhyeyamanutta mam /
nityaṃ śuddhaṃ sadā śāntamatīndriyamanaupamam /
ānandamātramacalaṃ vyāptāśeṣacarācaram //
2.22.d:
परं ज्योतिरचिन्त्यं यद्योगिध्येयमनुत्त मम् ।
नित्यं शुद्धं सदा शान्तमतीन्द्रियमनौपमम् ।
आनन्दमात्रमचलं व्याप्ताशेषचराचरम् ॥
2.22.m: the supreme, unthinkable light, unexcelled, to be meditated on by yogins, / eternal, pure, ever tranquil, beyond the senses, peerless, / consisting solely of bliss, immovable, pervading all that moves and is still—

2.22.s:
cintayāmāsa tadrūpaṃ devadevasya bhārgavaḥ /
nityaṃ śuddhaṃ sadā śāntamatīndriyamanaupamam //
iti śrībrahmāṇḍe mahāpurāṇe vāyuprokte madhyabhāge tṛtīye upoddhātapāde vasiṣṭhasagarasaṃvāde arcunopākhyāne jāmadagnyatapaścaraṇaṃ nāma dvāviṃśatitamo 'dhyāyaḥ // 22//
2.22.d:
चिन्तयामास तद्रूपं देवदेवस्य भार्गवः ।
नित्यं शुद्धं सदा शान्तमतीन्द्रियमनौपमम् ॥
इति श्रीब्रह्माण्डे महापुराणे वायुप्रोक्ते मध्यभागे तृतीये उपोद्धातपादे वसिष्ठसगरसंवादे अर्चुनोपाख्याने जामदग्न्यतपश्चरणं नाम द्वाविंशतितमो ऽध्यायः ॥ 22॥
2.22.m:
the Bhārgava contemplated that form of the god of gods: / eternal, pure, ever tranquil, beyond the senses, peerless.

Thus ends the twenty-second chapter, titled "The Performance of Austerity by the Son of Jamadagni," in the story of Arjuna, in the dialogue between Vasiṣṭha and Sagara, in the Upoddhātapāda, the third, middle section in the glorious and great Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa, spoken by Vāyu. // 22

2.23.s:
vasiṣṭha uvāca
tapasvinaṃ tadā rāmamekāgramanasaṃ bhave /
rahasyekāntanirataṃ niyataṃ śaṃsitavratam //
2.23.d:
वसिष्ठ उवाच
तपस्विनं तदा राममेकाग्रमनसं भवे ।
रहस्येकान्तनिरतं नियतं शंसितव्रतम् ॥
2.23.m: Vasiṣṭha said: / Hearing then that the ascetic Rāma was single-minded toward Bhava, / intent on secret solitude, self-restrained, his vows commended,

2.23.s:
śrutvā tamṛṣayaḥ sarve taponirdhūtakalmaṣāḥ /
jñānakarmavayovṛddhā mahāntaḥ śaṃsitavratāḥ //
2.23.d:
श्रुत्वा तमृषयः सर्वे तपोनिर्धूतकल्मषाः ।
ज्ञानकर्मवयोवृद्धा महान्तः शंसितव्रताः ॥
2.23.m: all the ṛṣis, whose impurities had been shaken off through austerity, / mature in knowledge, action, and age, great men of commended vows,

2.23.s:
didṛkṣavaḥ samājagmuḥ kutūhalasamanvitāḥ /
khyāpayantastapaḥ śreṣṭhaṃ tasya rājanmahātmanaḥ //
2.23.d:
दिदृक्षवः समाजग्मुः कुतूहलसमन्विताः ।
ख्यापयन्तस्तपः श्रेष्ठं तस्य राजन्महात्मनः ॥
2.23.m: came together desirous of seeing him, filled with curiosity, / proclaiming the excellent austerity of that great-souled one, O king.

2.23.s:
bhṛgvatrikratujābālivāmadevamṛkaṇḍavaḥ /
saṃbhāvayantaste rāmaṃ munayo vṛddhasaṃmatāḥ //
2.23.d:
भृग्वत्रिक्रतुजाबालिवामदेवमृकण्डवः ।
संभावयन्तस्ते रामं मुनयो वृद्धसंमताः ॥
2.23.m: Bhṛgu, Atri, Kratu, Jābāli, Vāmadeva, and Mṛkaṇḍu, / sages esteemed by the elders, honoring Rāma,

2.23.s:
ājagmurāśramaṃ tasya rāmasya tapasastapaḥ /
dūrādeva mahāntaste puṇyakṣetranivāsinaḥ //
2.23.d:
आजग्मुराश्रमं तस्य रामस्य तपसस्तपः ।
दूरादेव महान्तस्ते पुण्यक्षेत्रनिवासिनः ॥
2.23.m: came from afar to the hermitage of that Rāma, whose asceticism was penance itself, / those great men residing in holy sites.

2.23.s:
garīyaḥ sarvalokeṣu tapo 'gryaṃ jñānameva ca /
praśasya tasya te sarveprayayuḥ svaṃ svamāśramam //
2.23.d:
गरीयः सर्वलोकेषु तपो ऽग्र्यं ज्ञानमेव च ।
प्रशस्य तस्य ते सर्वेप्रययुः स्वं स्वमाश्रमम् ॥
2.23.m: Having praised his austerity, the weightiest in all the worlds, foremost, and his knowledge, / they all departed each to his own hermitage.

2.23.s:
evaṃ pravarttatastasya rāmasya bhagavāñchivaḥ /
prasannacetā nitarāṃ babhūva nṛpasattama //
2.23.d:
एवं प्रवर्त्ततस्तस्य रामस्य भगवाञ्छिवः ।
प्रसन्नचेता नितरां बभूव नृपसत्तम ॥
2.23.m: As that Rāma was proceeding thus, the blessed Śiva / became exceedingly pleased in mind, O best of kings.

2.23.s:
jijñāsustasya bhagavān bhaktimātmani śaṅkaraḥ /
mṛgavyādhavapurbhūtvā yayau rājaṃstadantikam //
2.23.d:
जिज्ञासुस्तस्य भगवान् भक्तिमात्मनि शङ्करः ।
मृगव्याधवपुर्भूत्वा ययौ राजंस्तदन्तिकम् ॥
2.23.m: Wishing to test his devotion to himself, the blessed Śaṅkara, / having assumed the form of a deer-hunter, went to his presence, O king.

2.23.s:
bhinnāñjanacayaprakhyo raktāntāyatalocanaḥ /
śaracāpadharaḥ prāṃśurvajrasaṃhanano yuvā //
2.23.d:
भिन्नाञ्जनचयप्रख्यो रक्तान्तायतलोचनः ।
शरचापधरः प्रांशुर्वज्रसंहननो युवा ॥
2.23.m: Resembling a heap of crushed collyrium, with long eyes reddish at the corners, / bearing bow and arrows, tall, a youth with limbs firm as a thunderbolt,

2.23.s:
uttuṅgahanubāhvaṃsaḥ piṅgalaśmaśrumūrddhajaḥ /
māṃsavisravasāgandhī sarvaprāṇivihiṃsakaḥ //
2.23.d:
उत्तुङ्गहनुबाह्वंसः पिङ्गलश्मश्रुमूर्द्धजः ।
मांसविस्रवसागन्धी सर्वप्राणिविहिंसकः ॥
2.23.m: with prominent jaw, arms, and shoulders, with tawny beard and hair, / smelling of raw meat, blood, and fat, a slayer of all living beings,

2.23.s:
sakaṇṭakulatāsparśakṣatārūṣitavigrahaḥ /
sāmaṭaksaṃcarvamāṇaśca māṃsakhaṇḍamanekaśaḥ //
2.23.d:
सकण्टकुलतास्पर्शक्षतारूषितविग्रहः ।
सामटक्संचर्वमाणश्च मांसखण्डमनेकशः ॥
2.23.m: his body covered with scratches from contact with thorny creepers, / chewing on raw and dry pieces of flesh again and again,

2.23.s:
māṃsabhāradvayālaṃbividhānānatakandharaḥ /
ārujaṃstarasā vṛkṣānūruvegena saṃghaśaḥ //
2.23.d:
मांसभारद्वयालंबिविधानानतकन्धरः ।
आरुजंस्तरसा वृक्षानूरुवेगेन संघशः ॥
2.23.m: his neck bent under the arrangement of carrying two loads of meat suspended [from a pole], / breaking down trees violently in masses with the force of his thighs,

2.23.s:
abhyavarttata taṃ deśaṃ pādacārīva parvataḥ /
āsādya sarasastasya tīraṃ kusumitadrumam //
2.23.d:
अभ्यवर्त्तत तं देशं पादचारीव पर्वतः ।
आसाद्य सरसस्तस्य तीरं कुसुमितद्रुमम् ॥
2.23.m: he strode toward that region like a walking mountain. / Having reached the bank of that lake, filled with flowering trees,

2.23.s:
nyadadhānmāsabhāraṃ ca sa mūle kasyacittaroḥ /
niṣasāda kṣaṇantatra tarucchāyāmupāśritaḥ //
2.23.d:
न्यदधान्मासभारं च स मूले कस्यचित्तरोः ।
निषसाद क्षणन्तत्र तरुच्छायामुपाश्रितः ॥
2.23.m: he placed the burden of meat down at the foot of a certain tree, / and sat down there for a moment, taking shelter in the shade of the tree.

2.23.s:
tiṣṭhantaṃ sarasastīre so 'paśyadbhṛgunandanam /
tataḥ sa śīghramutthāya samīpamupasṛtya ca //
2.23.d:
तिष्ठन्तं सरसस्तीरे सो ऽपश्यद्भृगुनन्दनम् ।
ततः स शीघ्रमुत्थाय समीपमुपसृत्य च ॥
2.23.m: He saw the descendant of Bhṛgu standing on the bank of the lake. / Then, rising quickly and approaching near,

2.23.s:
rāmāya seṣucāpābhyāṃ karābhyāṃ vidadheṃ'jalim /
sajalāṃbhodasannādagaṃbhīreṇa svareṇa ca //
2.23.d:
रामाय सेषुचापाभ्यां कराभ्यां विदधेंऽजलिम् ।
सजलांभोदसन्नादगंभीरेण स्वरेण च ॥
2.23.m: he made an añjali to Rāma with his hands holding bow and arrows; / and with a voice deep as the rumble of a rain-filled cloud,

2.23.s:
jagāda bhṛguśārdūlaṃ guhāntaravisarpiṇā /
toṣapravarṣavyādho 'haṃ vasāmyasminmahāvane //
2.23.d:
जगाद भृगुशार्दूलं गुहान्तरविसर्पिणा ।
तोषप्रवर्षव्याधो ऽहं वसाम्यस्मिन्महावने ॥
2.23.m: spreading like sound within a cave, he spoke to the tiger of the Bhṛgus: / "I am the hunter Toṣapravarṣa, dwelling in this great forest.

2.23.s:
īśo 'hamasya deśasya saprāṇitaruvīrudhaḥ /
carāmi samacittātmā nānāsattvā miṣāśanaḥ //
2.23.d:
ईशो ऽहमस्य देशस्य सप्राणितरुवीरुधः ।
चरामि समचित्तात्मा नानासत्त्वा मिषाशनः ॥
2.23.m: I am the lord of this land, along with its creatures, trees, and shrubs; / I wander with an equanimous mind, eating the flesh of various beings.

2.23.s:
samaśca sarvabhūteṣu na ca pitrādayo 'pi me /
abhakṣyāgamyapeyādicchandavastuṣu kutracit //
2.23.d:
समश्च सर्वभूतेषु न च पित्रादयो ऽपि मे ।
अभक्ष्यागम्यपेयादिच्छन्दवस्तुषु कुत्रचित् ॥
2.23.m: I am impartial toward all beings, nor do I have parents or others. / In whatever desired things—inedible, inaccessible, undrinkable, and the like—

2.23.s:
kṛtyākṛtyavidhaucaiva na viśeṣitadhīraham /
prapanno nābhigamanaṃ nivāsamapi kasyacit //
2.23.d:
कृत्याकृत्यविधौचैव न विशेषितधीरहम् ।
प्रपन्नो नाभिगमनं निवासमपि कस्यचित् ॥
2.23.m: and in rules of what should and should not be done, I have no discriminating mind. / I do not permit anyone's approach or residence,

2.23.s:
śakrasyāpi balenāhamanumanye na saṃśayaḥ /
jānate tadhyathā sarve deśo 'yaṃ madupāśrayaḥ //
2.23.d:
शक्रस्यापि बलेनाहमनुमन्ये न संशयः ।
जानते तध्यथा सर्वे देशो ऽयं मदुपाश्रयः ॥
2.23.m: not even of Śakra by force, of this there is no doubt. / For all know that this region is my resort.

2.23.s:
tasmānna kaścidāyāti mamātrānumatiṃ vinā /
ityeṣa mama vṛttāntaḥ kārtsnyena kathitastava //
2.23.d:
तस्मान्न कश्चिदायाति ममात्रानुमतिं विना ।
इत्येष मम वृत्तान्तः कार्त्स्न्येन कथितस्तव ॥
2.23.m: Therefore no one comes here without my permission. / Thus has my account been told to you in full.

2.23.s:
tvaṃ ca me brūhi tattvena nijavṛttamaśeṣataḥ /
kastvaṃ kasmādihāyātaḥ kimarthamiha dhiṣṭhitaḥ /
udyato 'nyatra vā gantuṃ kiṃ vā tava cikīrṣitam //
2.23.d:
त्वं च मे ब्रूहि तत्त्वेन निजवृत्तमशेषतः ।
कस्त्वं कस्मादिहायातः किमर्थमिह धिष्ठितः ।
उद्यतो ऽन्यत्र वा गन्तुं किं वा तव चिकीर्षितम् ॥
2.23.m: Tell me truly your own story completely: / Who are you? Whence have you come here? For what purpose are you stationed here? / Or are you preparing to go elsewhere, or what is it that you wish to do?"

2.23.s:
vasiṣṭha uvāca
ityevamuktaḥ prahasaṃstena rāmo mahādyutiḥ /
tūṣṇīṃ kṣaṇamiva sthitvā dadhyau kiñcidavāṅmukhaḥ //
2.23.d:
वसिष्ठ उवाच
इत्येवमुक्तः प्रहसंस्तेन रामो महाद्युतिः ।
तूष्णीं क्षणमिव स्थित्वा दध्यौ किञ्चिदवाङ्मुखः ॥
2.23.m: Vasiṣṭha said: / Thus addressed by him, smiling, Rāma of great splendor / stood as if silent for a moment, and contemplated with his face turned slightly downward:

2.23.s:
ko 'yameva durādharṣaḥ sajalāṃbhodanisvanaḥ /
bravīti ca giro 'tyarthaṃ vispaṣṭārthapadākṣarāḥ //
2.23.d:
को ऽयमेव दुराधर्षः सजलांभोदनिस्वनः ।
ब्रवीति च गिरो ऽत्यर्थं विस्पष्टार्थपदाक्षराः ॥
2.23.m: "Who is this unconquerable one, with the voice of a water-laden cloud, / who speaks words with such exceedingly clear meaning, terms, and syllables?

2.23.s:
kiṃ tu me mahatīṃ śaṅkāṃ tanurasya tanoti vai /
vijātisaṃśrayatvena ramaṇīyā tathā śarāḥ //
2.23.d:
किं तु मे महतीं शङ्कां तनुरस्य तनोति वै ।
विजातिसंश्रयत्वेन रमणीया तथा शराः ॥
2.23.m: Yet his form raises great suspicion in me: / though belonging to a low caste, it is handsome, and so are his arrows."

2.23.s:
evaṃ cintayatastasya nimittāni śubhāni vai /
babhūvurbhuvi dehe ca svābhipretārthadānyalam //
2.23.d:
एवं चिन्तयतस्तस्य निमित्तानि शुभानि वै ।
बभूवुर्भुवि देहे च स्वाभिप्रेतार्थदान्यलम् ॥
2.23.m: As he was thinking thus, auspicious omens / occurred on the earth and on his body, fully granting the desired object.

2.23.s:
tato vimṛśya bahuśo manasābhṛgupuṅgavaḥ /
uvāca śanakairvyādhaṃ vacanaṃ sūnṛtākṣaram //
2.23.d:
ततो विमृश्य बहुशो मनसाभृगुपुङ्गवः ।
उवाच शनकैर्व्याधं वचनं सूनृताक्षरम् ॥
2.23.m: Then, having reflected much in his mind, the bull of the Bhṛgus / spoke slowly to the hunter words of pleasing and true syllables:

2.23.s:
jāmadagnyo 'smi bhadraṃ te rāmo nāmnā tu bhārgavaḥ /
tapaścartumihāyātaḥ sāṃprataṃ guruśāsanāt //
2.23.d:
जामदग्न्यो ऽस्मि भद्रं ते रामो नाम्ना तु भार्गवः ।
तपश्चर्तुमिहायातः सांप्रतं गुरुशासनात् ॥
2.23.m: "I am the son of Jamadagni, hail to you, Rāma by name, a Bhārgava; / I have come here now to perform austerity by command of my guru.

2.23.s:
tapasā sarvalokeśaṃ bhaktyā ca niyamena ca /
ārādhayitumasmiṃstu cirāyāhaṃ samudyataḥ //
2.23.d:
तपसा सर्वलोकेशं भक्त्या च नियमेन च ।
आराधयितुमस्मिंस्तु चिरायाहं समुद्यतः ॥
2.23.m: Through austerity, devotion, and restraint, to propitiate / the lord of all worlds, I have undertaken [penance] here for a long time."

2.23.s:
tasmātmarveśvaraṃ sarvaśaraṇyamabhayapradam /
trinetraṃ pāpadamanaṃ śaṅkaraṃ bhaktavatsalam //
2.23.d:
तस्मात्मर्वेश्वरं सर्वशरण्यमभयप्रदम् ।
त्रिनेत्रं पापदमनं शङ्करं भक्तवत्सलम् ॥
2.23.m: Therefore, the Lord of all, refuge of all, bestower of fearlessness, / the three-eyed Śaṅkara, who suppresses sin and is affectionate to his devotees,

2.23.s:
tapasā toṣayiṣyāmi sarvajñaṃ tripurāntakam /
āśrame 'sminasarastīre niyamaṃ samupāśritaḥ //
2.23.d:
तपसा तोषयिष्यामि सर्वज्ञं त्रिपुरान्तकम् ।
आश्रमे ऽस्मिनसरस्तीरे नियमं समुपाश्रितः ॥
2.23.m: I shall satisfy by austerity, the omniscient destroyer of Tripura, / abiding by restraint in this hermitage on the shore of the lake.

2.23.s:
bhaktānukaṃpī bhagavānyāvatpratyakṣatāṃ haraḥ /
upaiti tāvadatraiva sthāsyāmīti matirmama //
2.23.d:
भक्तानुकंपी भगवान्यावत्प्रत्यक्षतां हरः ।
उपैति तावदत्रैव स्थास्यामीति मतिर्मम ॥
2.23.m: Until the blessed Hara, compassionate to devotees, / becomes visible, so long shall I remain right here: this is my resolve.

2.23.s:
tasmāditastvayādyaiva gantumanyatra yujyate /
na cedbhavati me hāniḥ svakṛterniyamasya ca //
2.23.d:
तस्मादितस्त्वयाद्यैव गन्तुमन्यत्र युज्यते ।
न चेद्भवति मे हानिः स्वकृतेर्नियमस्य च ॥
2.23.m: Therefore, it is proper for you to depart elsewhere from here this very day; / if not, harm will come to my own vow and duty.

2.23.s:
mānanīyo 'tha vāhaṃ te bhaktyā deśāntarātithiḥ /
svanivāsamupāyātastapasvī ca tathā muniḥ //
2.23.d:
माननीयो ऽथ वाहं ते भक्त्या देशान्तरातिथिः ।
स्वनिवासमुपायातस्तपस्वी च तथा मुनिः ॥
2.23.m: Or rather, I should be honoured by you with devotion as a guest from another land, / an ascetic and an ascetic sage who has arrived at his own dwelling.

2.23.s:
tvatasaṃnidhau nivāso me bhavetpāpāya kevalam /
tava cāpyasukhodarkaṃ matsamīpaniṣevaṇam //
2.23.d:
त्वतसंनिधौ निवासो मे भवेत्पापाय केवलम् ।
तव चाप्यसुखोदर्कं मत्समीपनिषेवणम् ॥
2.23.m: Living in your presence would lead solely to sin for me, / and resorting near me will result in misfortune for you as well.

2.23.s:
sa tvaṃmadāśramopānte paricaṅkramaṇādikam /
parityajya sukhībhūyā lokayorubhayorapi //
2.23.d:
स त्वंमदाश्रमोपान्ते परिचङ्क्रमणादिकम् ।
परित्यज्य सुखीभूया लोकयोरुभयोरपि ॥
2.23.m: So you, having abandoned wandering about and the like near my hermitage, / become happy in both worlds!

2.23.s:
vasiṣṭha uvāca
iti tasya vacaḥ śrutvā sa bhūyo bhṛgupuṅgavam /
uvāca roṣatāmrākṣastāmrākṣamidamuttaram //
2.23.d:
वसिष्ठ उवाच
इति तस्य वचः श्रुत्वा स भूयो भृगुपुङ्गवम् ।
उवाच रोषताम्राक्षस्ताम्राक्षमिदमुत्तरम् ॥
2.23.m: Vasiṣṭha said: / Having heard his words, he whose eyes were copper-red with anger / spoke this reply once more to that bull of the Bhṛgus whose eyes were red:

2.23.s:
brahman kimidamatyarthaṃ samīpe vasatiṃ mama /
parigarhayase yena kṛtaghnasyeva kāṃpratam //
2.23.d:
ब्रह्मन् किमिदमत्यर्थं समीपे वसतिं मम ।
परिगर्हयसे येन कृतघ्नस्येव कांप्रतम् ॥
2.23.m: "O brāhmaṇa, why do you so excessively censure my living nearby, / as if it were [the act] of an ungrateful person now?

2.23.s:
kiṃ mayāpakṛtaṃ loke bhavato 'nyasya vā kvacit /
anāgaskāriṇaṃ dāntaṃ ko 'vamanyeta nāmataḥ //
2.23.d:
किं मयापकृतं लोके भवतो ऽन्यस्य वा क्वचित् ।
अनागस्कारिणं दान्तं को ऽवमन्येत नामतः ॥
2.23.m: What harm have I done in the world to you or to anyone else anywhere? / Who, pray, would despise a self-controlled person who commits no offense?

2.23.s:
sannidhiḥ pariharttavyo yadi me viprapuṅgava /
darśanaṃ saha saṃvāsaḥ saṃbhāṣaṇamathāpi ca //
2.23.d:
सन्निधिः परिहर्त्तव्यो यदि मे विप्रपुङ्गव ।
दर्शनं सह संवासः संभाषणमथापि च ॥
2.23.m: If my presence is to be avoided, O best of brāhmaṇas, / along with seeing [me], living together, and speaking [with me],

2.23.s:
āyuṣmatādhunaivāsmādapasarttavyamāśramāt /
svasaṃśrayaṃ parityajya kvāhaṃ yāsye bubhukṣitaḥ //
2.23.d:
आयुष्मताधुनैवास्मादपसर्त्तव्यमाश्रमात् ।
स्वसंश्रयं परित्यज्य क्वाहं यास्ये बुभुक्षितः ॥
2.23.m: then you, long-lived one, should withdraw from this hermitage right now! / Having abandoned my own shelter, where shall I go, hungry [as I am]?

2.23.s:
svādhivāsaṃ parityajya bhavatā yoditaḥ katham /
ito 'nyasmin gāmiṣyāmi dūre nāhaṃ viśeṣataḥ //
2.23.d:
स्वाधिवासं परित्यज्य भवता योदितः कथम् ।
इतो ऽन्यस्मिन् गामिष्यामि दूरे नाहं विशेषतः ॥
2.23.m: How can I, having abandoned my own dwelling because of what you have said, / go elsewhere from here far away, especially not I?

2.23.s:
gamyatāṃ bhavatānyatra sthīyatāmatra vecchayā /
nāhaṃ cālayituṃ śakyaḥ sthānādasmātkathañcana //
2.23.d:
गम्यतां भवतान्यत्र स्थीयतामत्र वेच्छया ।
नाहं चालयितुं शक्यः स्थानादस्मात्कथञ्चन ॥
2.23.m: Let your honour go elsewhere, or remain here as you please; / I cannot be moved from this place by any means!"

2.23.s:
vasiṣṭha uvāca
tacchrutvā vacanaṃ tasya kiñcitkopasamanvitaḥ /
tamuvāca punarvākyamidaṃ rājanbhṛgūdvahaḥ //
2.23.d:
वसिष्ठ उवाच
तच्छ्रुत्वा वचनं तस्य किञ्चित्कोपसमन्वितः ।
तमुवाच पुनर्वाक्यमिदं राजन्भृगूद्वहः ॥
2.23.m: Vasiṣṭha said: / Having heard that statement of his, filled with a little anger, / that bearer of the Bhṛgu lineage spoke this word again to him, O king:

2.23.s:
vyādhajātiriyaṃ krūrā sarvasattvabhayāvahā /
khalakarmaratā nityaṃ dhikkṛtā sarvajantubhiḥ //
2.23.d:
व्याधजातिरियं क्रूरा सर्वसत्त्वभयावहा ।
खलकर्मरता नित्यं धिक्कृता सर्वजन्तुभिः ॥
2.23.m: "This hunter caste is cruel, bringing fear to all living beings, / constantly delighting in wicked deeds, reviled by all creatures.

2.23.s:
tasyāṃ jāto 'si pāpīyānsarvaprāṇivihiṃsakaḥ /
sa kathaṃ na parityājyaḥ sujanaiḥ syāttu durmate //
2.23.d:
तस्यां जातो ऽसि पापीयान्सर्वप्राणिविहिंसकः ।
स कथं न परित्याज्यः सुजनैः स्यात्तु दुर्मते ॥
2.23.m: You were born into it, very sinful, a slaughterer of all living beings; / how then should you not be avoided by good people, O evil-minded one?

2.23.s:
tasmādvihīnajātīyaṃ viditvātmānamabyatha /
śīghramasmādvrajānyatra nātra kāryā vicāraṇā //
2.23.d:
तस्माद्विहीनजातीयं विदित्वात्मानमब्यथ ।
शीघ्रमस्माद्व्रजान्यत्र नात्र कार्या विचारणा ॥
2.23.m: Therefore, knowing yourself to be of a base caste, without distress / go elsewhere from here quickly; no hesitation should be made here!

2.23.s:
śarīratrāṇakāruṇyātsamīpaṃ nopasarpasi /
yathā tvaṃ kaṇṭakādīnāmasahiṣṇutayā vyathām //
2.23.d:
शरीरत्राणकारुण्यात्समीपं नोपसर्पसि ।
यथा त्वं कण्टकादीनामसहिष्णुतया व्यथाम् ॥
2.23.m: Out of pity for the protection of [their] body, you do not come near [the truth]: / just as you feel pain out of intolerance of thorns and the like,

2.23.s:
tathāvehi samastānāṃ priyāḥ prāṇāḥ śarīriṇām /
vyathā cābhihatānāṃ tu vidyate bhavato 'nyathā //
2.23.d:
तथावेहि समस्तानां प्रियाः प्राणाः शरीरिणाम् ।
व्यथा चाभिहतानां तु विद्यते भवतो ऽन्यथा ॥
2.23.m: so know that life is dear to all embodied beings; / and pain exists for those who are struck down, not otherwise than for you.

2.23.s:
ahiṃsā sarvabhūtānāmiti dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ /
etadviruddhācaraṇānnityaṃ sadbhirvigarhitaḥ //
2.23.d:
अहिंसा सर्वभूतानामिति धर्मः सनातनः ।
एतद्विरुद्धाचरणान्नित्यं सद्भिर्विगर्हितः ॥
2.23.m: Non-violence toward all beings—this is the eternal dharma; / through conduct opposed to this, one is constantly censured by the virtuous.

2.23.s:
ātmaprāṇābhirakṣārthaṃ tvamaśeṣaśarīriṇaḥ /
haniṣyasi kathaṃ satsunāpnoṣi vacanīyatām //
2.23.d:
आत्मप्राणाभिरक्षार्थं त्वमशेषशरीरिणः ।
हनिष्यसि कथं सत्सुनाप्नोषि वचनीयताम् ॥
2.23.m: For the sake of preserving your own life, you / will kill all embodied beings; how will you not incur reproach among the virtuous?

2.23.s:
tasmācchīghraṃ tu bhogaccha tvameva puruṣādhama /
tvayā me kṛtyadoṣasya hāniśca na bhaviṣyati //
2.23.d:
तस्माच्छीघ्रं तु भोगच्छ त्वमेव पुरुषाधम ।
त्वया मे कृत्यदोषस्य हानिश्च न भविष्यति ॥
2.23.m: Therefore, go away quickly yourself, O vilest of men, / and on your account there will be no loss of my prescribed duty.

2.23.s:
na catsvayamito gaccheśtatastava balādapi /
apasarpaṇatābuddhimahamutpādaye sphuṭam //
2.23.d:
न चत्स्वयमितो गच्छेश्ततस्तव बलादपि ।
अपसर्पणताबुद्धिमहमुत्पादये स्फुटम् ॥
2.23.m: If you do not go from here of your own accord, then by force / I shall clearly produce in you the thought of retreating.

2.23.s:
kṣaṇārddhamapi te pāpa śreyasī neha saṃsthitiḥ /
viruddhācaraṇo nityaṃ dharmadriṣ ko labhecca śām //
2.23.d:
क्षणार्द्धमपि ते पाप श्रेयसी नेह संस्थितिः ।
विरुद्धाचरणो नित्यं धर्मद्रिष् को लभेच्च शाम् ॥
2.23.m: Even for half a moment, O sinner, your staying here is not auspicious; / how can an enemy of dharma, always behaving contrarily, obtain peace?"

2.23.s:
vasiṣṭha uvāca
rāmasya vacanaṃ śrutvā prīto 'pi tamidaṃ vacaḥ /
uvāca saṃkruddha iva vyādharūpī pinākadhṛk //
2.23.d:
वसिष्ठ उवाच
रामस्य वचनं श्रुत्वा प्रीतो ऽपि तमिदं वचः ।
उवाच संक्रुद्ध इव व्याधरूपी पिनाकधृक् ॥
2.23.m: Vasiṣṭha said: / Having heard Rāma's words, though pleased, the wielder of the Pināka / in the form of a hunter spoke this word to him as if enraged:

2.23.s:
sarvametadahaṃ manyaṃ vyarthaṃ vyavasitaṃ tava /
kutastvaṃ prathamo jñānī kutaḥ śaṃbhuḥ kutastapaḥ //
2.23.d:
सर्वमेतदहं मन्यं व्यर्थं व्यवसितं तव ।
कुतस्त्वं प्रथमो ज्ञानी कुतः शंभुः कुतस्तपः ॥
2.23.m: "I consider all this resolve of yours to be in vain: / where is your foremost knowledge, where is Śambhu, and where is austerity?

2.23.s:
kutastvaṃ kliśyase mūḍha tapasā tena te 'dhunā /
ghruvaṃ mithyāpravṛttasya na hi tuṣyati śaṅkaraḥ //
2.23.d:
कुतस्त्वं क्लिश्यसे मूढ तपसा तेन ते ऽधुना ।
घ्रुवं मिथ्याप्रवृत्तस्य न हि तुष्यति शङ्करः ॥
2.23.m: Why do you torment yourself with that austerity now, O fool? / Surely Śaṅkara is never pleased with one who has undertaken [it] falsely!

2.23.s:
viruddhalokācaraṇaḥ śaṃbhustasya vituṣṭaye /
pratapatyabudho marttyastvāṃ vinā kaḥ mudurmate //
2.23.d:
विरुद्धलोकाचरणः शंभुस्तस्य वितुष्टये ।
प्रतपत्यबुधो मर्त्त्यस्त्वां विना कः मुदुर्मते ॥
2.23.m: Śambhu's conduct is contrary to the world; for his gratification / what foolish mortal performs austerities except you, O very evil-minded one?

2.23.s:
atha vā ca gataṃ me 'dya yuktametadasaṃśayam /
saṃpūjya pūjakaviddhau śaṃbhostava ca saṃgamaḥ //
2.23.d:
अथ वा च गतं मे ऽद्य युक्तमेतदसंशयम् ।
संपूज्य पूजकविद्धौ शंभोस्तव च संगमः ॥
2.23.m: Or rather, it has occurred to me today: this is undoubtedly fitting— / the meeting between you and Śambhu in the manner of worshipper and worshipped!

2.23.s:
tvayā pūjayituṃ yuktaḥ sa eva bhuvane rataḥ /
saṃpūjako 'pi tasya tvaṃ yogyo nātra vicāraṇā //
2.23.d:
त्वया पूजयितुं युक्तः स एव भुवने रतः ।
संपूजको ऽपि तस्य त्वं योग्यो नात्र विचारणा ॥
2.23.m: He alone is fit to be worshipped by you, who delights in the [burning] ground; / and you are worthy to be his worshipper, there is no doubt about this.

2.23.s:
pitāmahasya lokānāṃ brahmaṇaḥ parameṣṭhinaḥ /
śiraśchittvā punaḥ śaṃbhurbrahmahatyāmavāptavān //
2.23.d:
पितामहस्य लोकानां ब्रह्मणः परमेष्ठिनः ।
शिरश्छित्त्वा पुनः शंभुर्ब्रह्महत्यामवाप्तवान् ॥
2.23.m: Having cut off the head of Brahmā the grandfather of the worlds, the supreme lord, / Śambhu in turn incurred the sin of slaying a brāhmaṇa.

2.23.s:
brahmahatyābhibhūtena prāyastvaṃ śaṃbhunā dvija /
upadiṣṭo 'si tatkartuṃ nocedevaṃ kathaṃ kṛthāḥ //
2.23.d:
ब्रह्महत्याभिभूतेन प्रायस्त्वं शंभुना द्विज ।
उपदिष्टो ऽसि तत्कर्तुं नोचेदेवं कथं कृथाः ॥
2.23.m: Most likely you have been instructed by Śambhu, who was overcome by the slaying of a brāhmaṇa, / to do that, O twice-born! If not, how would you have done so?

2.23.s:
tādātmyaguṇasaṃyogānmanyaṃ rudrasya te 'dhunā /
tapaḥ siddhiranuprāptā kolenālpīyasā mune //
2.23.d:
तादात्म्यगुणसंयोगान्मन्यं रुद्रस्य ते ऽधुना ।
तपः सिद्धिरनुप्राप्ता कोलेनाल्पीयसा मुने ॥
2.23.m: Due to the conjunction of essential qualities with Rudra, I think / the perfection of your austerity has now been attained in very little time, O sage!

2.23.s:
prāyo 'dya mātaraṃ hatvā sarvailoṅkairnirākṛtaḥ /
tapovyājena gahane nirjane saṃpravarttase //
2.23.d:
प्रायो ऽद्य मातरं हत्वा सर्वैलोङ्कैर्निराकृतः ।
तपोव्याजेन गहने निर्जने संप्रवर्त्तसे ॥
2.23.m: Most likely having killed your mother today, rejected by all the worlds, / under the guise of austerity you are wandering in an impassable, lonely forest.

2.23.s:
gurustrībrahmahatyotthapātakakṣapaṇāya ca /
tapaścarasi nānena tapasā tatpraṇaśyati //
2.23.d:
गुरुस्त्रीब्रह्महत्योत्थपातकक्षपणाय च ।
तपश्चरसि नानेन तपसा तत्प्रणश्यति ॥
2.23.m: And for the destruction of the sin arising from the slaying of a teacher's wife and a brāhmaṇa / you perform austerity; yet through this austerity that does not perish!

2.23.s:
pātakānāṃ kilānyeṣāṃ prāyaścittāni saṃtyapi /
mātṛdruhāmavehi tvaṃ na kvacitkila niṣkṛtiḥ //
2.23.d:
पातकानां किलान्येषां प्रायश्चित्तानि संत्यपि ।
मातृद्रुहामवेहि त्वं न क्वचित्किल निष्कृतिः ॥
2.23.m: For there are indeed expiations for other sins; / but know that there is no atonement anywhere for those who harm their mother!

2.23.s:
ahiṃsālakṣaṇo dharmo lokeṣu yadi te mataḥ /
svahastena kathaṃ rāma mātaraṃ kṛttavānasi //
2.23.d:
अहिंसालक्षणो धर्मो लोकेषु यदि ते मतः ।
स्वहस्तेन कथं राम मातरं कृत्तवानसि ॥
2.23.m: If the dharma whose characteristic is non-violence is approved by you in the worlds, / why, O Rāma, did you cut down your mother with your own hand?

2.23.s:
kṛtvā mātṛvadhaṃ ghoraṃ sarvalokavigarhitam /
tvaṃ punardhārmiko bhūtvā kāmato 'nyānvinindasi //
2.23.d:
कृत्वा मातृवधं घोरं सर्वलोकविगर्हितम् ।
त्वं पुनर्धार्मिको भूत्वा कामतो ऽन्यान्विनिन्दसि ॥
2.23.m: Having committed the terrible slaughter of your mother, reviled by all the worlds, / having become 'righteous' again, do you willfully blame others?

2.23.s:
paśyatā hasatāmoghaṃ ātmadoṣamajānatā /
aparyāptamahaṃ nanyaṃ paraṃ doṣavimarśanām //
2.23.d:
पश्यता हसतामोघं आत्मदोषमजानता ।
अपर्याप्तमहं नन्यं परं दोषविमर्शनाम् ॥
2.23.m: Seeing and laughing in vain, not knowing one's own fault, / I consider examining another's fault to be insufficient.

2.23.s:
svadharmaṃ yadyahaṃ tyaktvā vartteyamakulobhayam /
tarhi garhaya māṃ kāmaṃ nirupya manasā svayam //
2.23.d:
स्वधर्मं यद्यहं त्यक्त्वा वर्त्तेयमकुलोभयम् ।
तर्हि गर्हय मां कामं निरुप्य मनसा स्वयम् ॥
2.23.m: If, having abandoned my own duty, I were to live causing fear to families, / then censure me at will, having determined [it] yourself in your mind.

2.23.s:
mātāpitṛsutādīnāṃ bharaṇāyaiva kevalam /
kriyate prāṇihananaṃ nijadharmatayā mayā //
2.23.d:
मातापितृसुतादीनां भरणायैव केवलम् ।
क्रियते प्राणिहननं निजधर्मतया मया ॥
2.23.m: Solely for the maintenance of mother, father, sons, and others / the killing of living beings is done by me as my own inherent duty.

2.23.s:
svadharmādāmiṣeṇāhaṃ sakuṭumbo dinedine /
varttāmi sāpi me vṛttirvidhātrā vihitā purā //
2.23.d:
स्वधर्मादामिषेणाहं सकुटुम्बो दिनेदिने ।
वर्त्तामि सापि मे वृत्तिर्विधात्रा विहिता पुरा ॥
2.23.m: By meat from my own duty I subsist day by day with my family; / that livelihood of mine was also ordained by the Creator long ago.

2.23.s:
māṃsena yāvatā me syānnityaṃ pitrādi poṣaṇam /
haniṣye cettadadhikaṃ tarhi yujyeyamenasā //
2.23.d:
मांसेन यावता मे स्यान्नित्यं पित्रादि पोषणम् ।
हनिष्ये चेत्तदधिकं तर्हि युज्येयमेनसा ॥
2.23.m: With as much meat as would constantly suffice for the nourishment of my father and others, / if I were to kill more than that, then I would incur sin.

2.23.s:
yāvatpoṣaṇaghātena na vayaṃ syāma ninditāḥ /
tadetatsaṃpradhārya tvaṃ nindavā māṃ praśaṃsa vā //
2.23.d:
यावत्पोषणघातेन न वयं स्याम निन्दिताः ।
तदेतत्संप्रधार्य त्वं निन्दवा मां प्रशंस वा ॥
2.23.m: By killing only as much as is needed for nourishment, we are not blameworthy; / having reflected upon this, either blame me or praise me!

2.23.s:
sādhu vāsādhu vā karma yasya yadvihitaṃ purā /
tadeva tena karttavyamāpadyapi kathañcana //
2.23.d:
साधु वासाधु वा कर्म यस्य यद्विहितं पुरा ।
तदेव तेन कर्त्तव्यमापद्यपि कथञ्चन ॥
2.23.m: Good or bad, whatever deed was ordained for someone long ago, / that very deed should be performed by him even in adversity, by any means.

2.23.s:
nirūpaya svabhuddhyā tvamātmano mama cāntaram /
ahaṃ tu sarvabhāvena mitrādibharaṇe rataḥ //
2.23.d:
निरूपय स्वभुद्ध्या त्वमात्मनो मम चान्तरम् ।
अहं तु सर्वभावेन मित्रादिभरणे रतः ॥
2.23.m: Discern with your own intellect the difference between yourself and me: / I, indeed, am devoted with all my heart to maintaining friends and kin,

2.23.s:
saṃtyajya pitaraṃ vṛddhaṃ vinihatya ca mātaram /
bhūtvā tu dhārmikastvaṃ tu tapaścartumihāgataḥ //
2.23.d:
संत्यज्य पितरं वृद्धं विनिहत्य च मातरम् ।
भूत्वा तु धार्मिकस्त्वं तु तपश्चर्तुमिहागतः ॥
2.23.m: while you, having abandoned your aged father and having struck down your mother, / having become 'righteous', have come here to practice austerity!"

2.23.s:
ye tu mūlavidasteṣāṃ vispaṣṭaṃ yatra darśanam /
yathājihvaṃ bhavennātra vacasāpi samīhitum //
2.23.d:
ये तु मूलविदस्तेषां विस्पष्टं यत्र दर्शनम् ।
यथाजिह्वं भवेन्नात्र वचसापि समीहितुम् ॥
2.23.m: For those who know the root [facts], whose vision is clear, / it is not possible here even to wish [to speak] crookedly with words.

2.23.s:
ahaṃ tu samyagjānāmi tava vṛttamaśeṣataḥ /
tasmādalaṃ te tapasā niṣphalena bhṛgūdvaha //
2.23.d:
अहं तु सम्यग्जानामि तव वृत्तमशेषतः ।
तस्मादलं ते तपसा निष्फलेन भृगूद्वह ॥
2.23.m: I, however, know your conduct fully in its entirety; / therefore, have done with your fruitless austerities, O scion of Bhṛgu!

2.23.s:
sukhamicchasi cettyaktvā kāyakleśakaraṃ tapaḥ /
yāhi rāma tvamanyatra yatra vā na vidurjanāḥ //
iti śrībrahmāṇḍe mahāpurāṇe vāyuprokte madhyabhāge tṛtīya upoddhātapāde trayoviṃśatitamo 'dhyāyaḥ
2.23.d:
सुखमिच्छसि चेत्त्यक्त्वा कायक्लेशकरं तपः ।
याहि राम त्वमन्यत्र यत्र वा न विदुर्जनाः ॥
इति श्रीब्रह्माण्डे महापुराणे वायुप्रोक्ते मध्यभागे तृतीय उपोद्धातपादे त्रयोविंशतितमो ऽध्यायः
2.23.m:
If you desire happiness, abandon austerities that cause bodily affliction, / and go elsewhere, O Rāma, where people do not know [you].

Thus ends the twenty-third chapter in the Upoddhātapāda, the third [part], in the middle section of the glorious Brahmāṇḍa Mahāpurāṇa spoken by Vāyu.

2.24.s:
vasiṣṭha uvāca
ityuktastena bhūpāla rāmo matimatāṃ varaḥ /
nirūpya manasā bhūyastamuvācābhivismitam //
2.24.d:
वसिष्ठ उवाच
इत्युक्तस्तेन भूपाल रामो मतिमतां वरः ।
निरूप्य मनसा भूयस्तमुवाचाभिविस्मितम् ॥
2.24.m: Vasiṣṭha said: / Addressed thus by him, O king, Rāma, the best of the intelligent, / reflected in his mind and spoke back to him, filled with wonder:

2.24.s:
rāma uvāca
kastvaṃ brūhi mahābhāga na vai prākṛtapūruṣaḥ /
indrasyevānubhāvena vapurālakṣyate tava //
2.24.d:
राम उवाच
कस्त्वं ब्रूहि महाभाग न वै प्राकृतपूरुषः ।
इन्द्रस्येवानुभावेन वपुरालक्ष्यते तव ॥
2.24.m: Rāma said: / Tell me, who are you, O noble one? You are certainly no ordinary man. / Your body appears endowed with the majesty of Indra.

2.24.s:
vicitrārthapadaudāryaguṇagāṃbhīryajātibhiḥ /
sarvajñasyaiva te vāṇī śrūyate 'timanoharā //
2.24.d:
विचित्रार्थपदौदार्यगुणगांभीर्यजातिभिः ।
सर्वज्ञस्यैव ते वाणी श्रूयते ऽतिमनोहरा ॥
2.24.m: With its wonderful meanings, nobility of words, quality, depth, and refinement, / your voice is heard as if belonging to an all-knowing one, exceedingly captivating.

2.24.s:
indro vahniryamo dhātā varuṇo vā dhanādhipaḥ /
īśānastapano brahmā vāyuḥ somo gururguhaḥ //
2.24.d:
इन्द्रो वह्निर्यमो धाता वरुणो वा धनाधिपः ।
ईशानस्तपनो ब्रह्मा वायुः सोमो गुरुर्गुहः ॥
2.24.m: Indra, Agni, Yama, Dhātṛ, Varuṇa, or Kubera; / Īśāna, Sūrya, Brahmā, Vāyu, Soma, Bṛhaspati, or Guha—

2.24.s:
eṣāmanyatamaḥ prāyo bhavānbhavitumarhati /
anubhāvena jātiste hṛdiśaṅkāṃ tanoti me //
2.24.d:
एषामन्यतमः प्रायो भवान्भवितुमर्हति ।
अनुभावेन जातिस्ते हृदिशङ्कां तनोति मे ॥
2.24.m: you must probably be one among these. / Your noble nature spreads doubt in my heart.

2.24.s:
māyāvī bhagavānviṣṇuḥ śrūyate puruṣottamaḥ /
ko vā tvaṃ vapuṣānena brūhi māṃ samupāgataḥ //
2.24.d:
मायावी भगवान्विष्णुः श्रूयते पुरुषोत्तमः ।
को वा त्वं वपुषानेन ब्रूहि मां समुपागतः ॥
2.24.m: The lord Viṣṇu, Puruṣottama, is known as a master of illusion; / or who are you who have approached me with this body? Speak!

2.24.s:
atha vā jagatāṃ nāthaḥ sarvajñaḥ parameśvaraḥ /
paramātmātmasaṃbhūtirātmārāmaḥ sanātanaḥ //
2.24.d:
अथ वा जगतां नाथः सर्वज्ञः परमेश्वरः ।
परमात्मात्मसंभूतिरात्मारामः सनातनः ॥
2.24.m: Or else, the Lord of the worlds, the omniscient Supreme Lord, / the Supreme Self, self-born, delighting in the Self, eternal,

2.24.s:
svacchandacārī bhagavāñchivaḥ sarvajaganmayaḥ /
vapuṣānena saṃyukte bhavānbhavitumarhati //
2.24.d:
स्वच्छन्दचारी भगवाञ्छिवः सर्वजगन्मयः ।
वपुषानेन संयुक्ते भवान्भवितुमर्हति ॥
2.24.m: acting according to his own free will, the lord Śiva, consisting of the whole universe— / endowed with this body, you must be him.

2.24.s:
nānyasyedṛgbhavelloke prabhāvānugataṃ vapuḥ /
jātyarthasauṣṭhavopetā vāṇī caudāryaśālinī //
2.24.d:
नान्यस्येदृग्भवेल्लोके प्रभावानुगतं वपुः ।
जात्यर्थसौष्ठवोपेता वाणी चौदार्यशालिनी ॥
2.24.m: No one else in the world could have such a body attendant upon majesty, / and speech endowed with refinement of words and sense, abounding in grandeur.

2.24.s:
manye 'haṃ bhaktavātsalyādvānena vapuṣāharaḥ /
pratyakṣatāmupagato saṃdeho 'smatparīkṣayā //
2.24.d:
मन्ये ऽहं भक्तवात्सल्याद्वानेन वपुषाहरः ।
प्रत्यक्षतामुपगतो संदेहो ऽस्मत्परीक्षया ॥
2.24.m: I think that out of affection for your devotees, Hara, / you have become visible in this body to test me; there is no doubt.

2.24.s:
na kevalaṃ bhavān vyādhasteṣāṃ nedṛgvidhākṛtiḥ /
tasmāttubhyaṃ namastasmai surupaṃ saṃpradarśaya //
2.24.d:
न केवलं भवान् व्याधस्तेषां नेदृग्विधाकृतिः ।
तस्मात्तुभ्यं नमस्तस्मै सुरुपं संप्रदर्शय ॥
2.24.m: You are not merely a hunter; their appearance is not like this. / Therefore, obeisance to you, to him! Reveal your beautiful form.

2.24.s:
āviṣkurvanprasīdātmamahimānuguṇaṃ vapuḥ /
mamānekavidhā śaṅkāmucyeta yena mānasī //
2.24.d:
आविष्कुर्वन्प्रसीदात्ममहिमानुगुणं वपुः ।
ममानेकविधा शङ्कामुच्येत येन मानसी ॥
2.24.m: Be gracious, manifesting a body suited to your own greatness, / whereby my manifold mental doubt may be dispelled.

2.24.s:
prasīda sarvabhāvena buddhimohau mamādhunā /
praṇāśaya svarūpasya grahaṇādeva kevalam //
2.24.d:
प्रसीद सर्वभावेन बुद्धिमोहौ ममाधुना ।
प्रणाशय स्वरूपस्य ग्रहणादेव केवलम् ॥
2.24.m: Be gracious in every way! Dispel my confusion of mind right now / merely by perceiving your true nature.

2.24.s:
prārthayetvāṃ mahābhāga praṇamya śirasāsakṛt /
kastvaṃ me darśayātmānaṃ baddho 'yaṃ te mayāñjaliḥ //
2.24.d:
प्रार्थयेत्वां महाभाग प्रणम्य शिरसासकृत् ।
कस्त्वं मे दर्शयात्मानं बद्धो ऽयं ते मयाञ्जलिः ॥
2.24.m: I entreat you, O noble one, bowing repeatedly with my head: / reveal to me who you are; I have joined my palms before you.

2.24.s:
ityuktvā taṃ mahābhāga jñātumicchanbhṛgūdvahaḥ /
upaviśya tato bhūmau dhyānamāste samāhitaḥ //
2.24.d:
इत्युक्त्वा तं महाभाग ज्ञातुमिच्छन्भृगूद्वहः ।
उपविश्य ततो भूमौ ध्यानमास्ते समाहितः ॥
2.24.m: Having spoken thus, O noble one, wishing to know him, the scion of Bhṛgu / sat down upon the ground and remained absorbed in meditation, concentrated.

2.24.s:
baddhapadmāsano maunī yatavākkāyamānasaḥ /
niruddhaprāṇasaṃcāro dadhyau ciramudāradhīḥ //
2.24.d:
बद्धपद्मासनो मौनी यतवाक्कायमानसः ।
निरुद्धप्राणसंचारो दध्यौ चिरमुदारधीः ॥
2.24.m: Assuming the lotus posture, maintaining silence, subduing voice, body, and mind, / holding back the movement of his breath, the noble-minded one meditated for a long time.

2.24.s:
sanniyamyendriyagrāmaṃ mano hṛdi nirudhya ca /
cintayāmāsa deveśaṃ dhyānadṛṣṭyā jagadgurum //
2.24.d:
सन्नियम्येन्द्रियग्रामं मनो हृदि निरुध्य च ।
चिन्तयामास देवेशं ध्यानदृष्ट्या जगद्गुरुम् ॥
2.24.m: Restraining the host of senses and confining his mind in the heart, / he meditated on the Lord of the gods, the teacher of the universe, with the eye of meditation.

2.24.s:
apaśyacca jagannāthamātmasaṃdhānacakṣuṣā /
svabhaktānugrahakaraṃ mṛgavyādhasvarūpiṇam //
2.24.d:
अपश्यच्च जगन्नाथमात्मसंधानचक्षुषा ।
स्वभक्तानुग्रहकरं मृगव्याधस्वरूपिणम् ॥
2.24.m: And he saw the Lord of the universe with the eye of self-concentration, / bestowing grace upon his devotee, bearing the form of a deer-hunter.

2.24.s:
tata unmīlya nayane śīghramutthāya bhārgavaḥ /
dadarśa devaṃ tenaiva vapuṣā purataḥ sthitam //
2.24.d:
तत उन्मील्य नयने शीघ्रमुत्थाय भार्गवः ।
ददर्श देवं तेनैव वपुषा पुरतः स्थितम् ॥
2.24.m: Then, opening his eyes and rising swiftly, the Bhārgava / saw the god standing before him in that very body.

2.24.s:
ātmano 'nugrahārthāya śaraṇyaṃ bhaktavatsalam /
āvirbhūtaṃ mahārāja dṛṣṭvā rāmaḥ sasaṃbhramam //
2.24.d:
आत्मनो ऽनुग्रहार्थाय शरण्यं भक्तवत्सलम् ।
आविर्भूतं महाराज दृष्ट्वा रामः ससंभ्रमम् ॥
2.24.m: Seeing the refuge [of all], who is affectionate to his devotees, manifested / for the sake of bestowing grace upon him, O great king, Rāma, agitated with awe,

2.24.s:
romāñchodbhinnasarvāṅgo harṣāśruplutalocanaḥ /
papāta pādayorbhūmau bhaktyā tasya mahāmatiḥ //
2.24.d:
रोमाञ्छोद्भिन्नसर्वाङ्गो हर्षाश्रुप्लुतलोचनः ।
पपात पादयोर्भूमौ भक्त्या तस्य महामतिः ॥
2.24.m: his whole body bristling with horripilation, his eyes flooded with tears of joy, / fell at his feet on the ground with devotion, he of great intellect.

2.24.s:
sa gadgadamuvācainaṃ saṃbhramākulayā girā /
śaraṇaṃ bhava śarveti śaṅkaretyasakṛnnṛpa //
2.24.d:
स गद्गदमुवाचैनं संभ्रमाकुलया गिरा ।
शरणं भव शर्वेति शङ्करेत्यसकृन्नृप ॥
2.24.m: He spoke to him falteringly with words agitated by awe: / “Be my refuge, O Śarva! O Śaṅkara!” repeatedly, O king.

2.24.s:
tataḥ svarupadhṛk śaṃbhustadbhaktiparitoṣitaḥ /
rāmamutthāpayāmāsa praṇā māvanataṃ bhuvi //
2.24.d:
ततः स्वरुपधृक् शंभुस्तद्भक्तिपरितोषितः ।
राममुत्थापयामास प्रणा मावनतं भुवि ॥
2.24.m: Then Śambhu, assuming his own form and pleased with his devotion, / lifted Rāma up as he bowed in salutation to the ground.

2.24.s:
utthāpito jagaddhātrā svahastābhyāṃ bhṛgūdvahaḥ /
tuṣṭāva devadeveśaṃ puraḥ sthitvā kṛtājaliḥ //
2.24.d:
उत्थापितो जगद्धात्रा स्वहस्ताभ्यां भृगूद्वहः ।
तुष्टाव देवदेवेशं पुरः स्थित्वा कृताजलिः ॥
2.24.m: Raised up with both hands by the creator of the world, the scion of Bhṛgu / stood before him with joined palms and praised the god of gods.

2.24.s:
rāma uvāca
namaste devadevāya śaṅkarāyādimūrttaye /
namaḥ śarvāya śāntāya śāśvatāya namonamaḥ //
2.24.d:
राम उवाच
नमस्ते देवदेवाय शङ्करायादिमूर्त्तये ।
नमः शर्वाय शान्ताय शाश्वताय नमोनमः ॥
2.24.m: Rāma said: / Salutations to you, god of gods, Śaṅkara, primordial form! / Obeisance to Śarva, peaceful, eternal; salutations, salutations!

2.24.s:
namaste nīlakaṇṭhāya nīlalohitamūrttaye /
namaste bhūtanāthāya bhūtavāsāya te namaḥ //
2.24.d:
नमस्ते नीलकण्ठाय नीललोहितमूर्त्तये ।
नमस्ते भूतनाथाय भूतवासाय ते नमः ॥
2.24.m: Salutations to you, blue-throated one, whose form is dark blue and red! / Salutations to you, lord of beings, abode of creatures, obeisance to you!

2.24.s:
vyaktāvyaktasvarūpāya mahādevāya mīḍhuṣe /
śivāya bahurūpāya trinetrāya namonamaḥ //
2.24.d:
व्यक्ताव्यक्तस्वरूपाय महादेवाय मीढुषे ।
शिवाय बहुरूपाय त्रिनेत्राय नमोनमः ॥
2.24.m: To the one whose form is manifest and unmanifest, to the Great God, the bountiful, / to Śiva of manifold forms, the three-eyed one, salutations, salutations!

2.24.s:
śaraṇaṃ bhava me śarva tvadbhaktasya jagatpate /
bhūyo 'nanyāśrayāṇāṃ tu tvameva hi parāyaṇam //
2.24.d:
शरणं भव मे शर्व त्वद्भक्तस्य जगत्पते ।
भूयो ऽनन्याश्रयाणां तु त्वमेव हि परायणम् ॥
2.24.m: Be my refuge, O Śarva, to me your devotee, O Lord of the world! / For you alone are the supreme resort of those with no other refuge.

2.24.s:
yanmayāpakṛtaṃ deva duruktaṃ vāpi śaṅkara /
ajānatā tvāṃ bhagavanmama tatkṣantumarhasi //
2.24.d:
यन्मयापकृतं देव दुरुक्तं वापि शङ्कर ।
अजानता त्वां भगवन्मम तत्क्षन्तुमर्हसि ॥
2.24.m: Whatever wrong I may have committed, O god, or harsh words [spoken], O Śaṅkara, / not knowing you, O Lord, you ought to forgive me for that.

2.24.s:
ananyavedyarupasya sadbhāvamihakaḥ pumān /
tvāmṛte tava sarveśa samyak śakroti veditum //
2.24.d:
अनन्यवेद्यरुपस्य सद्भावमिहकः पुमान् ।
त्वामृते तव सर्वेश सम्यक् शक्रोति वेदितुम् ॥
2.24.m: Who in this world, other than you yourself, O Lord of all, / is able to properly know the true nature of your form, which cannot be known by another?

2.24.s:
tasmāttvaṃ sarvabhāvena prasīda mama śaṅkara /
nānyāsti me gatistubhyaṃ namo bhūyo namo namaḥ //
2.24.d:
तस्मात्त्वं सर्वभावेन प्रसीद मम शङ्कर ।
नान्यास्ति मे गतिस्तुभ्यं नमो भूयो नमो नमः ॥
2.24.m: Therefore, be gracious to me with all your heart, O Śaṅkara! / I have no other recourse; obeisance to you, repeatedly salutations, salutations!

2.24.s:
vasiṣṭha uvāca
iti saṃstūyamānastu kṛtāñjalipuṭaṃ puraḥ /
tiṣṭhantamāha bhagavānprasannātmā jaganmayaḥ //
2.24.d:
वसिष्ठ उवाच
इति संस्तूयमानस्तु कृताञ्जलिपुटं पुरः ।
तिष्ठन्तमाह भगवान्प्रसन्नात्मा जगन्मयः ॥
2.24.m: Vasiṣṭha said: / Being thus praised, the Lord, the soul of serenity, consisting of the universe, / spoke to him who stood before him with hands folded in reverent supplication:

2.24.s:
bhagavānuvāca
prīto 'smi bhavate tāta tapasānena sāṃpratam /
bhaktyā caivānapāyinyā hyapi bhārgavasattama //
2.24.d:
भगवानुवाच
प्रीतो ऽस्मि भवते तात तपसानेन सांप्रतम् ।
भक्त्या चैवानपायिन्या ह्यपि भार्गवसत्तम ॥
2.24.m: The Lord said: / I am pleased with you now, dear child, on account of this austerity, / and also because of your unfailing devotion, O best of the Bhārgavas!

2.24.s:
dāsye cābhi mataṃ save bhavate 'haṃ tvayā vṛtam /
bhakto hi me tvamatyarthaṃ nātra kāryā vicāraṇā //
2.24.d:
दास्ये चाभि मतं सवे भवते ऽहं त्वया वृतम् ।
भक्तो हि मे त्वमत्यर्थं नात्र कार्या विचारणा ॥
2.24.m: And I will grant all that is desired, chosen by you; / for you are exceedingly devoted to me, there is no deliberation to be made in this regard.

2.24.s:
mayaivāvagataṃ sarvaṃ tdṛdi vatte 'dyavarttate /
tasmādbravīmi yattvāhaṃ tatkuruṣvāviśaṅkitam //
2.24.d:
मयैवावगतं सर्वं त्दृदि वत्ते ऽद्यवर्त्तते ।
तस्माद्ब्रवीमि यत्त्वाहं तत्कुरुष्वाविशङ्कितम् ॥
2.24.m: All that is in your heart has been understood by me today; / therefore, do what I tell you without any hesitation.

2.24.s:
nāstrāṇāṃ dhāraṇe vatsa vidyate śaktiradya te /
raudrāṇāṃ tena bhūyo 'pi tapo ghoraṃ samācara //
2.24.d:
नास्त्राणां धारणे वत्स विद्यते शक्तिरद्य ते ।
रौद्राणां तेन भूयो ऽपि तपो घोरं समाचर ॥
2.24.m: You do not yet have the power to bear the dread missiles today, my child; / therefore, perform once again fierce austerities.

2.24.s:
parītya pṛthivīṃ sarvāṃ sarvatīrtheṣu ca kramāt /
srātvā pavitradehasttavaṃ sarvāṇyastrāṇyavāpsyasi //
2.24.d:
परीत्य पृथिवीं सर्वां सर्वतीर्थेषु च क्रमात् ।
स्रात्वा पवित्रदेहस्त्तवं सर्वाण्यस्त्राण्यवाप्स्यसि ॥
2.24.m: Circumambulate the whole earth, and bathing in sequence / at all the sacred bathing places, with your body purified, you will obtain all the missiles.

2.24.s:
ityuktvāntardadhe devastenaiva vapuṣā vibhuḥ /
rāmasya paśyato rājankṣaṇena bhavabhāgakṛt //
2.24.d:
इत्युक्त्वान्तर्दधे देवस्तेनैव वपुषा विभुः ।
रामस्य पश्यतो राजन्क्षणेन भवभागकृत् ॥
2.24.m: Having spoken thus, the all-pervading god, who grants the rewards of worldly existence, / disappeared in an instant in that very body before Rāma’s eyes, O king.

2.24.s:
antarhite jagannāthe rāmo natvā tu śaṅkaram /
parītyavasudhāṃ sarvāṃ tīrthasnāne 'karonmanaḥ //
2.24.d:
अन्तर्हिते जगन्नाथे रामो नत्वा तु शङ्करम् ।
परीत्यवसुधां सर्वां तीर्थस्नाने ऽकरोन्मनः ॥
2.24.m: When the Lord of the world had vanished, Rāma bowed to Śaṅkara / and set his mind on circumambulating the whole earth to bathe at sacred places.

2.24.s:
tataḥ sa pṛthivīṃ sarvāṃ parikramya yathākramam /
cakāra sarvatīrtheṣu snānaṃ vidhivadātmavān //
2.24.d:
ततः स पृथिवीं सर्वां परिक्रम्य यथाक्रमम् ।
चकार सर्वतीर्थेषु स्नानं विधिवदात्मवान् ॥
2.24.m: Then, having traversed the whole earth in proper sequence, / the self-controlled one performed ritual ablutions at all sacred places according to rule.

2.24.s:
tīrtheṣu kṣetramukhyeṣu tathā devālayeṣu ca /
pitṝndevāṃśca vidhivadatarpayadatandritaḥ //
2.24.d:
तीर्थेषु क्षेत्रमुख्येषु तथा देवालयेषु च ।
पितॄन्देवांश्च विधिवदतर्पयदतन्द्रितः ॥
2.24.m: At sacred bathing places, prominent sacred grounds, and temples of the gods, / unwearied, he duly gratified the ancestors and the gods.

2.24.s:
upavāsatapohomajapasnānādisukriyāḥ /
tīrtheṣu vidhivatkurvanparicakrāma medinīm //
2.24.d:
उपवासतपोहोमजपस्नानादिसुक्रियाः ।
