तीर्थेषु विधिवत्कुर्वन्परिचक्राम मेदिनीम् ॥
2.24.m: Duly performing auspicious rites such as fasts, austerities, oblations, recitations, and ablutions / at sacred bathing places, he traversed the earth.

2.24.s:
evaṃ krameṇa tīrtheṣu snātvā caiva vasuṃdharām /
pradakṣiṇīkṛtya śanaiḥ śuddhadeho 'bhavannṛpa //
2.24.d:
एवं क्रमेण तीर्थेषु स्नात्वा चैव वसुंधराम् ।
प्रदक्षिणीकृत्य शनैः शुद्धदेहो ऽभवन्नृप ॥
2.24.m: Having thus bathed at the sacred bathing places in succession, / and having slowly circumambulated the earth, he became purified in body, O king.

2.24.s:
parītyaivaṃ vasumatīṃ bhārgavaḥ śaṃbhuśāsanāt /
jagām bhūyastaṃ deśaṃ yatra pūrvamuvāsa saḥ //
2.24.d:
परीत्यैवं वसुमतीं भार्गवः शंभुशासनात् ।
जगाम् भूयस्तं देशं यत्र पूर्वमुवास सः ॥
2.24.m: Having thus traversed the earth by the command of Śambhu, the Bhārgava / went once again to that region where he had previously dwelt.

2.24.s:
gatvā rājansatatraiva sthitvā devamumāpatim /
bhaktyā saṃpūjayāmāsa tapobhirnniyamairapi //
2.24.d:
गत्वा राजन्सतत्रैव स्थित्वा देवमुमापतिम् ।
भक्त्या संपूजयामास तपोभिर्न्नियमैरपि ॥
2.24.m: Having gone there, O king, staying right there, he worshipped the god, the lord of Umā, / with devotion, through austerities and observances.

2.24.s:
etasminneva kāle tu devānāmasuraiḥ saha /
babhūva suciraṃ rājansaṃgrāmo romaharṣaṇaḥ //
2.24.d:
एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु देवानामसुरैः सह ।
बभूव सुचिरं राजन्संग्रामो रोमहर्षणः ॥
2.24.m: At that very time, O king, there occurred between the gods and the asuras / a very long war that made the hair stand on end.

2.24.s:
tato devānparājitya yuddhe 'tibalino 'surāḥ /
avāpuramaraiśvaryamaśeṣamakutobhayāḥ //
2.24.d:
ततो देवान्पराजित्य युद्धे ऽतिबलिनो ऽसुराः ।
अवापुरमरैश्वर्यमशेषमकुतोभयाः ॥
2.24.m: Then, having defeated the gods in battle, the extremely powerful asuras, / free from all fear, attained the entire sovereignty of the immortals.

2.24.s:
yuddhe parājitā devāḥ sakalā vāsavādayaḥ /
śaṅkaraṃ śaraṇaṃ cagmurhataiśvaryā hyarātibhiḥ //
2.24.d:
युद्धे पराजिता देवाः सकला वासवादयः ।
शङ्करं शरणं चग्मुर्हतैश्वर्या ह्यरातिभिः ॥
2.24.m: Defeated in battle, their sovereignty destroyed by their enemies, / all the gods, headed by Vāsava, went to Śaṅkara for refuge.

2.24.s:
toṣayitvā jagannāthaṃ praṇāmajaya saṃstavaiḥ /
prārthayāmāsurasurānhantuṃ devāḥ pinākinam //
2.24.d:
तोषयित्वा जगन्नाथं प्रणामजय संस्तवैः ।
प्रार्थयामासुरसुरान्हन्तुं देवाः पिनाकिनम् ॥
2.24.m: Having pleased the lord of the universe with prostrations and hymns of victory, / the gods implored the wielder of the Pināka bow to slay the asuras.

2.24.s:
tatasteṣāṃ pratiśrutya dānavānāṃ vadhaṃ nṛpa /
devānāṃ varadaḥ śaṃbhurmaho daramuvāca ha //
2.24.d:
ततस्तेषां प्रतिश्रुत्य दानवानां वधं नृप ।
देवानां वरदः शंभुर्महो दरमुवाच ह ॥
2.24.m: Then, having promised them the destruction of the Dānavas, O king, / Śambhu, the granter of boons to the gods, spoke to Mahodara:

2.24.s:
himadrerdakṣiṇe bhāge rāmo nāma mahātapāḥ /
muniputro 'titejasvī māmuddiśya tapasyati //
2.24.d:
हिमद्रेर्दक्षिणे भागे रामो नाम महातपाः ।
मुनिपुत्रो ऽतितेजस्वी मामुद्दिश्य तपस्यति ॥
2.24.m: "On the southern part of the Himalaya, a sage's son of great radiance, / named Rāma, of great ascetic fervor, performs austerities directed toward me.

2.24.s:
tatra gatvātvamadyaiva nivedya mama śāsanam /
mahodara tapasyantaṃ tamihānaya māciram //
2.24.d:
तत्र गत्वात्वमद्यैव निवेद्य मम शासनम् ।
महोदर तपस्यन्तं तमिहानय माचिरम् ॥
2.24.m: Going there this very day, Mahodara, having delivered my command, / bring him here without delay while he is performing austerities."

2.24.s:
ityājñaprastathetyuktvā praṇabhyeśaṃ mahodaraḥ /
jagāma vāyuvegena yatra rāmo vyavasthitaḥ //
2.24.d:
इत्याज्ञप्रस्तथेत्युक्त्वा प्रणभ्येशं महोदरः ।
जगाम वायुवेगेन यत्र रामो व्यवस्थितः ॥
2.24.m: Thus commanded, saying 'So be it,' and bowing to the Lord, Mahodara / went with the speed of the wind to where Rāma was abiding.

2.24.s:
samāsādya sa taṃ deśaṃ dṛṣṭvā rāmaṃ mahāmunim /
tapasyantamidaṃ vākyamuvāca vinayānvitaḥ //
2.24.d:
समासाद्य स तं देशं दृष्ट्वा रामं महामुनिम् ।
तपस्यन्तमिदं वाक्यमुवाच विनयान्वितः ॥
2.24.m: Having reached that place and seen Rāma, the great sage, / engaged in austerity, he spoke these words with humility:

2.24.s:
draṣṭumicchati śambhustvāṃ bhṛguvaryaṃ tadājñayā /
āgato 'haṃ tadāgaccha tatpādāṃbujasannidhim //
2.24.d:
द्रष्टुमिच्छति शम्भुस्त्वां भृगुवर्यं तदाज्ञया ।
आगतो ऽहं तदागच्छ तत्पादांबुजसन्निधिम् ॥
2.24.m: "Śambhu desires to see you, O best of the Bhṛgus; by his command / I have come. Therefore, come into the presence of his lotus feet."

2.24.s:
tacchrutvā vacanaṃ tasya śīghramutthāya bhārgavaḥ /
tadājñāṃ śirasānandya tatheti pratyabhāṣata //
2.24.d:
तच्छ्रुत्वा वचनं तस्य शीघ्रमुत्थाय भार्गवः ।
तदाज्ञां शिरसानन्द्य तथेति प्रत्यभाषत ॥
2.24.m: Hearing his speech, Bhārgava rose up quickly, / respectfully placed his command on his head, and answered, 'So be it.'

2.24.s:
tato rāmaṃ tvaropetaḥ śaṃbhupārśvaṃ mahodaraḥ /
prāpayāmāsa sahasā kailāse nāgasattame //
2.24.d:
ततो रामं त्वरोपेतः शंभुपार्श्वं महोदरः ।
प्रापयामास सहसा कैलासे नागसत्तमे ॥
2.24.m: Then, with haste, Mahodara quickly brought Rāma / to Śambhu's side on Kailāsa, the best of mountains.

2.24.s:
sahitaṃ sakalairbhūtairindrādyaiśca sahāmaraiḥ /
dadarśa bhārgavaśreṣṭhaḥ śaṅkaraṃ bhaktavatsalam //
2.24.d:
सहितं सकलैर्भूतैरिन्द्राद्यैश्च सहामरैः ।
ददर्श भार्गवश्रेष्ठः शङ्करं भक्तवत्सलम् ॥
2.24.m: Accompanied by all the beings, and together with the immortals headed by Indra, / the best of the Bhārgavas beheld Śaṅkara, who is affectionate to his devotees,

2.24.s:
saṃstūyamānaṃ munibhirnāradādyaistapodhanaiḥ /
gandharvairupagāyadbhirnṛtyadbhiścāpsarogaṇaiḥ //
2.24.d:
संस्तूयमानं मुनिभिर्नारदाद्यैस्तपोधनैः ।
गन्धर्वैरुपगायद्भिर्नृत्यद्भिश्चाप्सरोगणैः ॥
2.24.m: praised by sages rich in austerity headed by Nārada, / sung to by Gandharvas, and with troops of Apsarases dancing;

2.24.s:
upāsyamānaṃ deveśaṃ gajacarmadhṛtāmbaram /
bhasmoddhūlitasarvāṅgaṃ trinetraṃ candraśekharam //
2.24.d:
उपास्यमानं देवेशं गजचर्मधृताम्बरम् ।
भस्मोद्धूलितसर्वाङ्गं त्रिनेत्रं चन्द्रशेखरम् ॥
2.24.m: attracted upon, the lord of gods, clad in an elephant hide, / with all his limbs smeared with ashes, three-eyed, bearing the crescent moon on his crest;

2.24.s:
dhṛtapiṅgajaṭābhāraṃ nāgābharamabhūṣitam /
pralamboṣṭhabhujaṃ saumyaṃ prasannamukhapaṅkajam //
2.24.d:
धृतपिङ्गजटाभारं नागाभरमभूषितम् ।
प्रलम्बोष्ठभुजं सौम्यं प्रसन्नमुखपङ्कजम् ॥
2.24.m: bearing a mass of tawny matted hair, adorned with serpent ornaments, / with long lip and arms, gentle, his lotus face serene;

2.24.s:
āsthitaṃ kāñcane paṭṭe gīrvāṇasamitau nṛpa /
upāsarpattu deveśaṃ bhṛguvaryaḥ kṛtāñjaliḥ //
2.24.d:
आस्थितं काञ्चने पट्टे गीर्वाणसमितौ नृप ।
उपासर्पत्तु देवेशं भृगुवर्यः कृताञ्जलिः ॥
2.24.m: seated on a golden seat in the assembly of the gods, O king. / The best of the Bhṛgus approached the lord of gods with folded hands.

2.24.s:
śrīkaṇṭhadarśanodvattaromāñcāñcitavigrahaḥ /
bāṣpattu siktakāyena sa tu gatvā harāntikam //
2.24.d:
श्रीकण्ठदर्शनोद्वत्तरोमाञ्चाञ्चितविग्रहः ।
बाष्पत्तु सिक्तकायेन स तु गत्वा हरान्तिकम् ॥
2.24.m: His body bristling with horripilation at the sight of Śrīkaṇṭha, / his body bathed in tears, he went near Hara,

2.24.s:
bhaktyā sasaṃbhramaṃ vācā harṣagadgadayāsakṛt /
namaste devadeveti vyālapannākulākṣaram //
2.24.d:
भक्त्या ससंभ्रमं वाचा हर्षगद्गदयासकृत् ।
नमस्ते देवदेवेति व्यालपन्नाकुलाक्षरम् ॥
2.24.m: and, repeatedly murmuring with faltering syllables in devotion and agitation, / with a voice choked with joy, 'Homage to you, O god of gods!',

2.24.s:
papāta saṃspṛśanmūrdhnā caraṇau puravidviṣaḥ /
paśyatāṃ devavṛndānāṃ madhye bhṛgukulodvaham //
2.24.d:
पपात संस्पृशन्मूर्ध्ना चरणौ पुरविद्विषः ।
पश्यतां देववृन्दानां मध्ये भृगुकुलोद्वहम् ॥
2.24.m: the descendant of the Bhṛgu race fell down touching the feet of the foe of Tripura with his head, / in the midst of the hosts of gods who were looking on.

2.24.s:
tamutthāpya śivaḥ prītaḥ prasannamukhapaṅkajam /
rāmaṃ madhurayā vācā prahasannāha sādaram //
2.24.d:
तमुत्थाप्य शिवः प्रीतः प्रसन्नमुखपङ्कजम् ।
रामं मधुरया वाचा प्रहसन्नाह सादरम् ॥
2.24.m: Raising him up, Śiva, pleased, with a serene lotus face, / spoke to Rāma with a sweet voice, smiling respectfully:

2.24.s:
ime daityagaṇaiḥ krāntāḥ svādhiṣṭhānātparicyutāḥ /
aśakruvantastānhantuṃ gīrvāṇā māmupāgatāḥ //
2.24.d:
इमे दैत्यगणैः क्रान्ताः स्वाधिष्ठानात्परिच्युताः ।
अशक्रुवन्तस्तान्हन्तुं गीर्वाणा मामुपागताः ॥
2.24.m: "Overwhelmed by the hosts of Daityas and fallen from their rightful realm, / the gods, unable to slay them, have come to me.

2.24.s:
tasmānmamājñayā rāma devānāṃ ca priyepsayā /
jahi daityagaṇānsarvānsamarthastvaṃ hi me mataḥ //
2.24.d:
तस्मान्ममाज्ञया राम देवानां च प्रियेप्सया ।
जहि दैत्यगणान्सर्वान्समर्थस्त्वं हि मे मतः ॥
2.24.m: Therefore, by my command, O Rāma, and out of a desire to please the gods, / slay all the hosts of Daityas; for in my view you are capable."

2.24.s:
tato rāmo 'bravīccharvaṃ praṇipatya kṛtāñjaliḥ /
śṛṇvatāṃ sarvadevānāṃ sapraśrayamidaṃ vacaḥ //
2.24.d:
ततो रामो ऽब्रवीच्छर्वं प्रणिपत्य कृताञ्जलिः ।
शृण्वतां सर्वदेवानां सप्रश्रयमिदं वचः ॥
2.24.m: Then Rāma, having bowed down with folded hands, / addressed these modest words to Śarva while all the gods listened:

2.24.s:
svāminna viditaṃ kiṃ te sarvajñasyākhilātmanaḥ /
tathāpi vijñāpayato vacanaṃ me 'vadhāraya //
2.24.d:
स्वामिन्न विदितं किं ते सर्वज्ञस्याखिलात्मनः ।
तथापि विज्ञापयतो वचनं मे ऽवधारय ॥
2.24.m: "O Lord, what is not known to you, the omniscient soul of all? / Yet, heed my words as I make my petition.

2.24.s:
yadi śakrādibhirdevairakhilairamarārayaḥ /
na śakyā hantumekasya śakyāḥ syaste kathaṃ mama //
2.24.d:
यदि शक्रादिभिर्देवैरखिलैरमरारयः ।
न शक्या हन्तुमेकस्य शक्याः स्यस्ते कथं मम ॥
2.24.m: If the enemies of the immortals cannot be slain by all the gods headed by Śakra, / how could they possibly be slain by me alone?

2.24.s:
anastrajño 'smi deveśa yuddhānāmapyakovidaḥ /
kathaṃ haniṣye sakalānsuraśatrūnanāyudhaḥ //
2.24.d:
अनस्त्रज्ञो ऽस्मि देवेश युद्धानामप्यकोविदः ।
कथं हनिष्ये सकलान्सुरशत्रूननायुधः ॥
2.24.m: I know no divine weapons, O lord of gods, nor am I skilled in battles. / Weaponless, how will I slay all the foes of the suras?"

2.24.s:
ityuktastena deveśaḥ sitaṃ kālāgnisaprabham /
śaivamastramayaṃ tejo dadau tasmai mahātmane //
2.24.d:
इत्युक्तस्तेन देवेशः सितं कालाग्निसप्रभम् ।
शैवमस्त्रमयं तेजो ददौ तस्मै महात्मने ॥
2.24.m: Thus addressed by him, the lord of gods gave to that great soul / the white, fiery energy of Śiva's weapon, radiant like the fire of universal destruction.

2.24.s:
ātmīyaṃ paraśuṃ datvā sarvaśastrābhibhāvakam /
rāmapāha prasannātmā gīrvāṇānāṃ tu śṛṇvatam //
2.24.d:
आत्मीयं परशुं दत्वा सर्वशस्त्राभिभावकम् ।
रामपाह प्रसन्नात्मा गीर्वाणानां तु शृण्वतम् ॥
2.24.m: Having bestowed his own battle-axe, which overcomes all weapons, / he spoke to Rāma with a gracious heart, as the gods listened:

2.24.s:
matprasādena sakalānsuraśatrūnvinighnataḥ /
śaktirbhavatu te saumya samastāridurāsadā //
2.24.d:
मत्प्रसादेन सकलान्सुरशत्रून्विनिघ्नतः ।
शक्तिर्भवतु ते सौम्य समस्तारिदुरासदा ॥
2.24.m: "By my grace, as you strike down all the foes of the suras, / may you possess power unassailable by any enemy, O gentle one.

2.24.s:
anenaivāyudhena tvaṃ gaccha yudhyasva śatrubhiḥ /
svayameva ca vetsi tvaṃ yathāvadyuddhakauśalam //
2.24.d:
अनेनैवायुधेन त्वं गच्छ युध्यस्व शत्रुभिः ।
स्वयमेव च वेत्सि त्वं यथावद्युद्धकौशलम् ॥
2.24.m: With this very weapon, go and fight with the enemies; / you will know battle skills properly of your own accord."

2.24.s:
vasiṣṭha uvāca
evamuktastato rāmaḥ śaṃbhunā taṃ praṇamya ca /
jagrāha paraśuṃ śaiva vibudhārivadhodyataḥ //
2.24.d:
वसिष्ठ उवाच
एवमुक्तस्ततो रामः शंभुना तं प्रणम्य च ।
जग्राह परशुं शैव विबुधारिवधोद्यतः ॥
2.24.m: Vasiṣṭha said: / Thus addressed by Śambhu, Rāma bowed to him / and took up the battle-axe of Śiva, eager to slay the enemies of the gods.

2.24.s:
tataḥ sa śuśubhe rāmo viṣṇuterñjo 'śasaṃbhavaḥ /
rudrabhaktyā samāyukto dyutyeva saviturmahaḥ //
2.24.d:
ततः स शुशुभे रामो विष्णुतेर्ञ्जो ऽशसंभवः ।
रुद्रभक्त्या समायुक्तो द्युत्येव सवितुर्महः ॥
2.24.m: Then Rāma, born of a portion of the energy of Viṣṇu, / endowed with devotion to Rudra, shone like the brilliance of the sun with its radiance.

2.24.s:
so 'nujñātastrinetreṇa devaiḥ sarvaiḥ samanvitaḥ /
jagāma hantumasurānyuddhāya kṛtaniścayaḥ //
2.24.d:
सो ऽनुज्ञातस्त्रिनेत्रेण देवैः सर्वैः समन्वितः ।
जगाम हन्तुमसुरान्युद्धाय कृतनिश्चयः ॥
2.24.m: Permitted by the three-eyed god, accompanied by all the gods, / he set out, resolved on battle, to slay the asuras.

2.24.s:
tato 'bhavatpunaryuddhaṃ devānāmasuraiḥ saha /
trailokyavijayodyuktai rājannatibhayaṅkaram //
2.24.d:
ततो ऽभवत्पुनर्युद्धं देवानामसुरैः सह ।
त्रैलोक्यविजयोद्युक्तै राजन्नतिभयङ्करम् ॥
2.24.m: Then there took place once again a most terrifying war, O king, / between the gods and the asuras who were striving to conquer the three worlds.

2.24.s:
atha rāmo mahābāhustasminyuddhe sudāruṇe /
kuddhaḥ paraśunā tena nijaghāna mahāsurān //
2.24.d:
अथ रामो महाबाहुस्तस्मिन्युद्धे सुदारुणे ।
कुद्धः परशुना तेन निजघान महासुरान् ॥
2.24.m: Then the mighty-armed Rāma, enraged in that dreadful battle, / struck down the great asuras with that battle-axe.

2.24.s:
prahārairaśaniprakhyairnighnandaityānsahasraśaḥ /
cacāra samare rāmaḥ kruddhaḥ kāla ivāparaḥ //
2.24.d:
प्रहारैरशनिप्रख्यैर्निघ्नन्दैत्यान्सहस्रशः ।
चचार समरे रामः क्रुद्धः काल इवापरः ॥
2.24.m: Striking down the Daityas by the thousands with blows resembling thunderbolts, / Rāma moved across the battlefield, enraged like another Death.

2.24.s:
hatvā tu sakalāndaityāndevānsarvānaharṣayat /
kṣaṇena nāśayāmāsa rāmaḥ praharatāṃ varaḥ //
2.24.d:
हत्वा तु सकलान्दैत्यान्देवान्सर्वानहर्षयत् ।
क्षणेन नाशयामास रामः प्रहरतां वरः ॥
2.24.m: Having slain all the Daityas, Rāma, the best of warriors, / gladdened all the gods and destroyed [the enemy] in an instant.

2.24.s:
rāmeṇa hanyamā nāstu samastā daityadānavāḥ /
dadṛśuḥ sarvato rāmaṃ hataśeṣā bhayānvitāḥ //
2.24.d:
रामेण हन्यमा नास्तु समस्ता दैत्यदानवाः ।
ददृशुः सर्वतो रामं हतशेषा भयान्विताः ॥
2.24.m: Being slaughtered by Rāma, all the Daityas and Dānavas / who survived the slaughter saw Rāma everywhere, filled with terror.

2.24.s:
hateṣvasurasaṃgheṣu vidruteṣu ca kṛtsnaśaḥ /
rāmamāmantrya vibudhāḥ prayayustridivaṃ punaḥ //
2.24.d:
हतेष्वसुरसंघेषु विद्रुतेषु च कृत्स्नशः ।
राममामन्त्र्य विबुधाः प्रययुस्त्रिदिवं पुनः ॥
2.24.m: When the hosts of asuras had been slain and completely routed, / the gods took leave of Rāma and returned to heaven.

2.24.s:
rāmo 'pi hatvā ditijānabhyanujñāpya cāmarān /
svamāśramaṃ samāpede tapasyāsaktamānasaḥ //
2.24.d:
रामो ऽपि हत्वा दितिजानभ्यनुज्ञाप्य चामरान् ।
स्वमाश्रमं समापेदे तपस्यासक्तमानसः ॥
2.24.m: Rāma also, having slain the sons of Diti and taken leave of the immortals, / returned to his hermitage, his mind intent on austerities.

2.24.s:
mṛgavyādhapratikṛtiṃ kṛtvā śambhormahāmatiḥ /
bhaktyā saṃpūjayāmāsa sa tasminnāśramevaśī //
2.24.d:
मृगव्याधप्रतिकृतिं कृत्वा शम्भोर्महामतिः ।
भक्त्या संपूजयामास स तस्मिन्नाश्रमेवशी ॥
2.24.m: Having made an image of Śambhu in the form of a deer-hunter, / that self-controlled, wise one worshipped him with devotion in that hermitage.

2.24.s:
gandhaiḥ puṣpaistathā hṛdyairnaivedyairabhivandanaiḥ /
stotraiśca vidhivadbhaktyā parāṃ prītimupānayat //
iti śrībrahmāṇḍe mahāpurāṇe vāyuprokte madhyabhāge tṛtīya upoddhātapāder'junopākhyāne caturviṃśatitamo 'dhyāyaḥ // 24//
2.24.d:
गन्धैः पुष्पैस्तथा हृद्यैर्नैवेद्यैरभिवन्दनैः ।
स्तोत्रैश्च विधिवद्भक्त्या परां प्रीतिमुपानयत् ॥
इति श्रीब्रह्माण्डे महापुराणे वायुप्रोक्ते मध्यभागे तृतीय उपोद्धातपादेर्ऽजुनोपाख्याने चतुर्विंशतितमो ऽध्यायः ॥ 24॥
2.24.m:
With perfumes, flowers, delightful food-offerings, prostrations, / and hymns according to rule, he brought about supreme delight with devotion.

Thus ends the twenty-fourth chapter in the Story of Arjuna in the third Upoddhātapāda of the middle section in the glorious and great Brahmāṇḍapurāṇa proclaimed by Vāyu.

2.25.s:
vasiṣṭha uvāca
tatasta draktiyogena sa prītātmā jagatpatiḥ /
pratyakṣamagamattasya sarvaiḥ saha marudgaṇaiḥ //
2.25.d:
वसिष्ठ उवाच
ततस्त द्रक्तियोगेन स प्रीतात्मा जगत्पतिः ।
प्रत्यक्षमगमत्तस्य सर्वैः सह मरुद्गणैः ॥
2.25.m: Vasiṣṭha said: / Then, through the practice of that devotion, the pleased Lord of the Universe / appeared visible before him together with all the hosts of the Maruts.

2.25.s:
taṃ dṛṣṭvā devadeveśaṃ trinetraṃ candraśekharam /
vṛṣendravāhanaṃ śaṃbhuṃ bhūtakoṭisamanvitam //
2.25.d:
तं दृष्ट्वा देवदेवेशं त्रिनेत्रं चन्द्रशेखरम् ।
वृषेन्द्रवाहनं शंभुं भूतकोटिसमन्वितम् ॥
2.25.m: Beholding the lord of the gods of gods, three-eyed, bearing the crescent moon on his crest, / having the lord of bulls for his mount, Śambhu accompanied by millions of spirits,

2.25.s:
sasaṃbhramaṃ samutthāya harṣeṇākulalocanaḥ /
praṇāmamakarodbhaktyā śarvāya bhuvi bhārgavaḥ //
2.25.d:
ससंभ्रमं समुत्थाय हर्षेणाकुललोचनः ।
प्रणाममकरोद्भक्त्या शर्वाय भुवि भार्गवः ॥
2.25.m: Rising up in haste, his eyes overflowing with joy, / the Bhārgava bowed down in devotion to Śarva on the earth.

2.25.s:
utthāyotthāya deveśaṃ praṇamya śirasāsakṛt /
kṛtāñjalipuṭo rāmastuṣṭāva ca jagatpatim //
2.25.d:
उत्थायोत्थाय देवेशं प्रणम्य शिरसासकृत् ।
कृताञ्जलिपुटो रामस्तुष्टाव च जगत्पतिम् ॥
2.25.m: Rising again and again and bowing his head repeatedly before the lord of gods, / his hands joined in reverence, Rāma praised the lord of the universe.

2.25.s:
rāma uvāca
namaste devadeveśa namaste parameśvara /
namaste jagato nātha namaste tripurāntaka //
2.25.d:
राम उवाच
नमस्ते देवदेवेश नमस्ते परमेश्वर ।
नमस्ते जगतो नाथ नमस्ते त्रिपुरान्तक ॥
2.25.m: Rāma said: / "Homage to you, lord of the gods of gods! Homage to you, supreme lord! / Homage to you, lord of the universe! Homage to you, destroyer of Tripura!

2.25.s:
namaste sakalādhyakṣa namaste bhaktavatsala /
namaste sarvabhūteśa namaste vṛṣabhadhvaja //
2.25.d:
नमस्ते सकलाध्यक्ष नमस्ते भक्तवत्सल ।
नमस्ते सर्वभूतेश नमस्ते वृषभध्वज ॥
2.25.m: Homage to you, witness of all! Homage to you, compassionate to devotees! / Homage to you, lord of all beings! Homage to you whose banner bears a bull!

2.25.s:
namaste sakalādhīśa namaste karuṇākara /
namaste sakalāvāsa namaste nīlalohita //
2.25.d:
नमस्ते सकलाधीश नमस्ते करुणाकर ।
नमस्ते सकलावास नमस्ते नीललोहित ॥
2.25.m: Homage to you, master of everything! Homage to you, mine of compassion! / Homage to you, abode of all! Homage to you, dark blue and red!

2.25.s:
namaḥ sakaladevārigaṇanāśāya śūline /
kapāline namastubhyaṃ sarvalokaikapāline //
2.25.d:
नमः सकलदेवारिगणनाशाय शूलिने ।
कपालिने नमस्तुभ्यं सर्वलोकैकपालिने ॥
2.25.m: Homage to the trident-bearer, destroyer of the hosts of all enemies of the gods! / Homage to you who bear a skull, sole protector of all the worlds!

2.25.s:
śmaśānavāsine nityaṃ namaḥ kailāsavāsine /
namo 'stu pāśine tubhyaṃ kālakūṭaviṣāśine //
2.25.d:
श्मशानवासिने नित्यं नमः कैलासवासिने ।
नमो ऽस्तु पाशिने तुभ्यं कालकूटविषाशिने ॥
2.25.m: Homage forever to the dweller in cremation grounds, to the dweller on Kailāsa! / Homage be to you who wield the noose, devourer of the kālakūṭa poison!

2.25.s:
vibhave 'maravandyāya prabhave te svayaṃbhuve /
namo 'khilajagatkarmasākṣibhūtāya śaṃbhave //
2.25.d:
विभवे ऽमरवन्द्याय प्रभवे ते स्वयंभुवे ।
नमो ऽखिलजगत्कर्मसाक्षिभूताय शंभवे ॥
2.25.m: To the all-pervading lord worthy of praise by immortals, the source, the self-existent! / Homage to Śambhu, who stands as witness to the deeds of the entire universe!

2.25.s:
namastripatha gāphenabhāsigārddhandumauline /
mahābhogīndrahārāya śivāya paramātmane //
2.25.d:
नमस्त्रिपथ गाफेनभासिगार्द्धन्दुमौलिने ।
महाभोगीन्द्रहाराय शिवाय परमात्मने ॥
2.25.m: Homage to him whose crest bears the half-moon shining with the foam of the three-streamed [Gaṅgā], / who wears the great king of serpents as a necklace, to Śiva, the supreme self!

2.25.s:
bhasmasaṃcchannadehāya namor'kāgnīnducakṣuṣe /
kapardine namastubhyamandhakāsuramarddine //
2.25.d:
भस्मसंच्छन्नदेहाय नमोर्ऽकाग्नीन्दुचक्षुषे ।
कपर्दिने नमस्तुभ्यमन्धकासुरमर्द्दिने ॥
2.25.m: To him whose body is covered in ash, homage to him whose eyes are the sun, fire, and moon! / Homage to you with matted hair, smiter of the demon Andhaka!

2.25.s:
tripuradhvaṃsine dakṣayajñavidhvaṃsine namaḥ /
girijākucakāśmīravirañjitamahorase //
2.25.d:
त्रिपुरध्वंसिने दक्षयज्ञविध्वंसिने नमः ।
गिरिजाकुचकाश्मीरविरञ्जितमहोरसे ॥
2.25.m: Homage to the destroyer of Tripura, the destroyer of Dakṣa's sacrifice, / whose broad chest is reddened by the saffron from the breasts of the Mountain's daughter!

2.25.s:
mahādevāya maha te namaste kṛttivāsase /
yogidhyeyasvarūpāya śivāyācintyatejase //
2.25.d:
महादेवाय मह ते नमस्ते कृत्तिवाससे ।
योगिध्येयस्वरूपाय शिवायाचिन्त्यतेजसे ॥
2.25.m: To Mahādeva, the great one, homage to you clad in an animal skin! / Whose nature is the object of meditation for yogins, to Śiva of inconceivable splendor!

2.25.s:
svabhaktahṛdayāṃbhojakarṇikāmadhyavarttine /
sakalāgamasiddhāntasārarūpāya te namaḥ //
2.25.d:
स्वभक्तहृदयांभोजकर्णिकामध्यवर्त्तिने ।
सकलागमसिद्धान्तसाररूपाय ते नमः ॥
2.25.m: To him who abides within the pericarp of the heart-lotus of his devotees, / to you whose form is the essence of the conclusions of all Āgamas, homage!

2.25.s:
namo nikhilayogendrabodhanāyāmṛtātmane /
śaṅkarāyākhilavyāptamahimne paramātmane //
2.25.d:
नमो निखिलयोगेन्द्रबोधनायामृतात्मने ।
शङ्करायाखिलव्याप्तमहिम्ने परमात्मने ॥
2.25.m: Homage to him who awakens all lords of yoga, whose nature is nectar, / to Śaṅkara, whose greatness pervades all things, the supreme self!

2.25.s:
namaḥ śarvāya śāntāya brahmaṇe viśvarupiṇe /
ādimadhyāntahīnāya nityāyāvyaktamūrttaye //
2.25.d:
नमः शर्वाय शान्ताय ब्रह्मणे विश्वरुपिणे ।
आदिमध्यान्तहीनाय नित्यायाव्यक्तमूर्त्तये ॥
2.25.m: Homage to Śarva, the peaceful, to Brahman who takes the form of the universe, / devoid of beginning, middle, and end, eternal, whose form is unmanifest!

2.25.s:
vyaktāvyaktasvarūpāya sthūlasūkṣmātmane namaḥ /
namo vedāntavedyāya viśvavijñānarūpiṇe //
2.25.d:
व्यक्ताव्यक्तस्वरूपाय स्थूलसूक्ष्मात्मने नमः ।
नमो वेदान्तवेद्याय विश्वविज्ञानरूपिणे ॥
2.25.m: Homage to him whose nature is manifest and unmanifest, whose self is gross and subtle! / Homage to him who is known through the Vedānta, whose form is universal knowledge!

2.25.s:
namaḥ surāsuraśreṇimaulipuṣpārcitāṅghraye /
śrīkaṇṭhāya jagaddhātre lokakartre namonamaḥ //
2.25.d:
नमः सुरासुरश्रेणिमौलिपुष्पार्चिताङ्घ्रये ।
श्रीकण्ठाय जगद्धात्रे लोककर्त्रे नमोनमः ॥
2.25.m: Homage to him whose feet are worshiped with flowers from the diadems of rows of gods and asuras, / to Śrīkaṇṭha, supporter of the universe, creator of the world, homage, homage!

2.25.s:
rajoguṇātmane tubhyaṃ viśvasṛṣṭividhāyine /
hiraṇyagarbharūpāya harāya jagadādaye //
2.25.d:
रजोगुणात्मने तुभ्यं विश्वसृष्टिविधायिने ।
हिरण्यगर्भरूपाय हराय जगदादये ॥
2.25.m: To you whose nature is the quality of rajas, who bring about the creation of the universe, / whose form is the Golden Germ, to Hara, the origin of the world!

2.25.s:
namo viśvātmane lokasthitivyā pārakāriṇe /
sattvavijñānarupāya parāya pratyagātmane //
2.25.d:
नमो विश्वात्मने लोकस्थितिव्या पारकारिणे ।
सत्त्वविज्ञानरुपाय पराय प्रत्यगात्मने ॥
2.25.m: Homage to the universal self who conducts the operation of sustaining the world, / whose form is knowledge consisting of sattva, the supreme, innermost self!

2.25.s:
tamoguṇavikārāya jagatsaṃhārakāriṇe /
klpānte rudrarūpāya parāpara vide namaḥ //
2.25.d:
तमोगुणविकाराय जगत्संहारकारिणे ।
क्ल्पान्ते रुद्ररूपाय परापर विदे नमः ॥
2.25.m: To him who transforms into the quality of tamas, who causes the destruction of the universe, / whose form is Rudra at the end of an eon, knower of the higher and lower, homage!

2.25.s:
avikārāya nityāya namaḥ sadasadātmane /
buddhibuddhiprabodhāya buddhīndriyavikāriṇe //
2.25.d:
अविकाराय नित्याय नमः सदसदात्मने ।
बुद्धिबुद्धिप्रबोधाय बुद्धीन्द्रियविकारिणे ॥
2.25.m: Homage to the changeless, the eternal, whose self is both the real and the unreal, / the illuminator of the intellect's understanding, who undergoes transformation as the sense organs of cognition!

2.25.s:
vasvādityamarudbhiśca sādhyarudrāśvibhedataḥ /
yanmāyābhinnamatayo devāstasmai namonamaḥ //
2.25.d:
वस्वादित्यमरुद्भिश्च साध्यरुद्राश्विभेदतः ।
यन्मायाभिन्नमतयो देवास्तस्मै नमोनमः ॥
2.25.m: Homage, homage to him by whose māyā the minds of the gods are differentiated / into the divisions of Vasus, Ādityas, Maruts, Sādhyas, Rudras, and Aśvins!

2.25.s:
avikāramajaṃ nityaṃ sūkṣmarūpamanaupamam /
tava yattanna jānanti yogino 'pi sadāmalāḥ //
2.25.d:
अविकारमजं नित्यं सूक्ष्मरूपमनौपमम् ।
तव यत्तन्न जानन्ति योगिनो ऽपि सदामलाः ॥
2.25.m: That changeless, unborn, eternal, subtle, incomparable form of yours, / even the ever-pure yogins do not comprehend.

2.25.s:
tvāmavijñāya durjñeyaṃ samyagbrahmādayo 'pi hi /
saṃsaranti bhave nūnaṃ na tatkarmātmakāściram //
2.25.d:
त्वामविज्ञाय दुर्ज्ञेयं सम्यग्ब्रह्मादयो ऽपि हि ।
संसरन्ति भवे नूनं न तत्कर्मात्मकाश्चिरम् ॥
2.25.m: Not knowing you, who are so hard to know, even Brahmā and the others indeed / wander for long in cyclic existence, consisting of action and not of that [knowledge].

2.25.s:
yāvannopaiti caraṇau tavājñānavighātinaḥ /
tāvadbhramati saṃsāre paṇḍito 'cetano 'pi vā //
2.25.d:
यावन्नोपैति चरणौ तवाज्ञानविघातिनः ।
तावद्भ्रमति संसारे पण्डितो ऽचेतनो ऽपि वा ॥
2.25.m: As long as one does not approach your feet, which destroy ignorance, / so long does one wander in saṃsāra, whether a learned man or an unintelligent one.

2.25.s:
sa eva dakṣaḥ sa kṛtī sa muniḥ sa ca paṇḍitaḥ /
bhavataścaraṇāṃbhoje yena buddhiḥ sthirīkṛtā //
2.25.d:
स एव दक्षः स कृती स मुनिः स च पण्डितः ।
भवतश्चरणांभोजे येन बुद्धिः स्थिरीकृता ॥
2.25.m: He alone is capable, he has achieved his purpose, he is a sage and a scholar, / by whom the intellect has been steadied upon your lotus feet.

2.25.s:
susūkṣmatvena gahanaḥ sadbhāvaste trayīmayaḥ /
viduṣāmapi mūḍhena sa mayā jñāyate katham //
2.25.d:
सुसूक्ष्मत्वेन गहनः सद्भावस्ते त्रयीमयः ।
विदुषामपि मूढेन स मया ज्ञायते कथम् ॥
2.25.m: Deep and difficult to fathom due to its extreme subtlety, your true nature consists of the three Vedas; / how can it be known by me, a fool, when it is so even for the wise?

2.25.s:
aśabdagojaratvena mahimnastava sāṃpratam /
stotumapyanalaṃ samyaktvā mahaṃ jaḍadhīryataḥ //
2.25.d:
अशब्दगोजरत्वेन महिम्नस्तव सांप्रतम् ।
स्तोतुमप्यनलं सम्यक्त्वा महं जडधीर्यतः ॥
2.25.m: Because your greatness is beyond the reach of words, / I, whose intellect is dull, am completely incapable now of even praising you properly.

2.25.s:
tasmādajñānato vāpi mayā bhaktyaiva saṃstutaḥ /
prītaśca bhava deveśa nanu tvaṃ bhaktavatsalaḥ //
2.25.d:
तस्मादज्ञानतो वापि मया भक्त्यैव संस्तुतः ।
प्रीतश्च भव देवेश ननु त्वं भक्तवत्सलः ॥
2.25.m: Therefore, whether through ignorance or otherwise, you have been praised by me solely with devotion; / be pleased, O lord of gods, for surely you are affectionate to devotees!"

2.25.s:
vasiṣṭha uvāca
iti stutastadā tena bhaktyā rāmeṇa śaṅkaraḥ /
meghagaṃbhīrayā vācā tamuvāca hasanniva //
2.25.d:
वसिष्ठ उवाच
इति स्तुतस्तदा तेन भक्त्या रामेण शङ्करः ।
मेघगंभीरया वाचा तमुवाच हसन्निव ॥
2.25.m: Vasiṣṭha said: / Thus praised at that time by Rāma with devotion, Śaṅkara, / with a voice deep as a thundercloud, spoke to him as if smiling:

2.25.s:
bhagavānuvāca
rāmāhaṃ suprasanno 'smi śorṃyaśālitayā tava /
tapasā mayi bhaktyā ca stotreṇa ca viśeṣataḥ //
2.25.d:
भगवानुवाच
रामाहं सुप्रसन्नो ऽस्मि शोर्ंयशालितया तव ।
तपसा मयि भक्त्या च स्तोत्रेण च विशेषतः ॥
2.25.m: The Blessed Lord said: / "O Rāma, I am exceedingly pleased with your courage, / your asceticism, your devotion to me, and especially your hymn of praise.

2.25.s:
varaṃ varaya tasmāttvaṃ yadyadicchasi cetasā /
tubhyaṃ tattadaśeṣeṇa dāsyāmyahamaśeṣataḥ //
2.25.d:
वरं वरय तस्मात्त्वं यद्यदिच्छसि चेतसा ।
तुभ्यं तत्तदशेषेण दास्याम्यहमशेषतः ॥
2.25.m: Therefore choose a boon, whatever you desire in your heart; / I will grant all of it to you without remainder."

2.25.s:
vasiṣṭha uvāca
ityukto devadevena taṃ praṇamya bhṛgūdvahaḥ /
kṛtāñjalipuṭo bhūtvā rājannidamuvāca ha //
2.25.d:
वसिष्ठ उवाच
इत्युक्तो देवदेवेन तं प्रणम्य भृगूद्वहः ।
कृताञ्जलिपुटो भूत्वा राजन्निदमुवाच ह ॥
2.25.m: Vasiṣṭha said: / Thus addressed by the god of gods, bowing to him, that descendant of Bhṛgu, / with his hands joined in reverence, said this, O king:

2.25.s:
yadi deva prasannastvaṃ vārarhe 'smi ca yadyaham /
bhavatastadabhīpsāmi hetumastrāṇyaśeṣataḥ //
2.25.d:
यदि देव प्रसन्नस्त्वं वारर्हे ऽस्मि च यद्यहम् ।
भवतस्तदभीप्सामि हेतुमस्त्राण्यशेषतः ॥
2.25.m: "If you are pleased, O god, and if I am worthy of a boon, / then from you I desire to obtain all divine weapons without exception.

2.25.s:
astre śastre ca śāstre ca na matto 'bhyadhiko bhavet /
lokeṣu māṃraṇejetā na bhavettvatprasādataḥ //
2.25.d:
अस्त्रे शस्त्रे च शास्त्रे च न मत्तो ऽभ्यधिको भवेत् ।
लोकेषु मांरणेजेता न भवेत्त्वत्प्रसादतः ॥
2.25.m: In missiles, hand-weapons, and sacred treatises, let no one be superior to me; / in all the worlds, let there be no conqueror of me in battle, through your grace!"

2.25.s:
vasiṣṭha uvāca
tathetyuktvā tataḥ śaṃbhurastraśastrāṇyaśeṣataḥ /
dadau rāmāya suprītaḥ samantrāṇi kramānnṛpa //
2.25.d:
वसिष्ठ उवाच
तथेत्युक्त्वा ततः शंभुरस्त्रशस्त्राण्यशेषतः ।
ददौ रामाय सुप्रीतः समन्त्राणि क्रमान्नृप ॥
2.25.m: Vasiṣṭha said: / Saying ‘So be it,’ Śambhu, highly pleased, then gave to Rāma / all missiles and hand-weapons along with their mantras in proper order, O king.

2.25.s:
saprayogaṃ sasaṃhāramastragrāmaṃ caturvidham /
prasādābhimukho rāmaṃ grāhayāmāsa śaṅkaraḥ //
2.25.d:
सप्रयोगं ससंहारमस्त्रग्रामं चतुर्विधम् ।
प्रसादाभिमुखो रामं ग्राहयामास शङ्करः ॥
2.25.m: Inclined toward grace, Śaṅkara made Rāma master / the fourfold collection of divine weapons together with the methods of discharge and withdrawal.

2.25.s:
asaṃgavegaṃ śubhrāśvaṃ sudhvajaṃ ca rathottamam /
iṣudhī cākṣayaśarau dadau rāmāya śaṅkaraḥ //
2.25.d:
असंगवेगं शुभ्राश्वं सुध्वजं च रथोत्तमम् ।
इषुधी चाक्षयशरौ ददौ रामाय शङ्करः ॥
2.25.m: An excellent chariot with unimpeded speed, white horses, and a splendid banner, / and two quivers of inexhaustible arrows, Śaṅkara gave to Rāma;

2.25.s:
abhedyamajaraṃ divyaṃ dṛḍhajyaṃ vijayaṃ dhanuḥ /
sarvaśastrasahaṃ citraṃ kavacaṃ ca mahādhanam //
2.25.d:
अभेद्यमजरं दिव्यं दृढज्यं विजयं धनुः ।
सर्वशस्त्रसहं चित्रं कवचं च महाधनम् ॥
2.25.m: an unpierceable, ageless, divine bow named Vijaya with a sturdy bowstring, / and an extraordinary, priceless armor capable of withstanding all weapons;

2.25.s:
ajeyatvaṃ ca yuddheṣu śauryaṃ cāpratimaṃ bhuvi /
svecchayā dhāraṇe śāktiṃ prāṇānāṃ ca narādhipa //
2.25.d:
अजेयत्वं च युद्धेषु शौर्यं चाप्रतिमं भुवि ।
स्वेच्छया धारणे शाक्तिं प्राणानां च नराधिप ॥
2.25.m: and invincibility in battles, and peerless valour on the earth, / and the power to sustain his vital breaths at his own will, O ruler of men;

2.25.s:
khyātiṃ ca bījametreṇa tannāmnā sarvalaukikīm /
tapaḥ prabhāvaṃ ca mahatpradadau bhārgavāya saḥ //
2.25.d:
ख्यातिं च बीजमेत्रेण तन्नाम्ना सर्वलौकिकीम् ।
तपः प्रभावं च महत्प्रददौ भार्गवाय सः ॥
2.25.m: and universal renown in the worlds merely by the seed syllable of his name, / and great power of asceticism he bestowed upon that Bhārgava.

2.25.s:
bhakti cātmani rāmāya dattvā rājanyathocitām /
sahitaḥ sakalairbhūtaiścāmaraiścandraśekharaḥ //
2.25.d:
भक्ति चात्मनि रामाय दत्त्वा राजन्यथोचिताम् ।
सहितः सकलैर्भूतैश्चामरैश्चन्द्रशेखरः ॥
2.25.m: Having granted Rāma proper devotion to himself, O king, / the moon-crested god, accompanied by all the spirits and the immortals—

2.25.s:
tenaiva vapuṣā śaṃbhuḥ kṣipramantaradhāddharaḥ /
kṛtakṛtyastato rāmo labdhvā sarvamabhīpsitam //
2.25.d:
तेनैव वपुषा शंभुः क्षिप्रमन्तरधाद्धरः ।
कृतकृत्यस्ततो रामो लब्ध्वा सर्वमभीप्सितम् ॥
2.25.m: Śambhu, Hara, quickly vanished in that very form. / Then Rāma, having attained all that he desired and accomplished his goal,

2.25.s:
adṛśyatāṃ gate śarve mahodaramuvāca ha /
mahodara madarthe tvamidaṃ sarvamaśeṣataḥ //
2.25.d:
अदृश्यतां गते शर्वे महोदरमुवाच ह ।
महोदर मदर्थे त्वमिदं सर्वमशेषतः ॥
2.25.m: when Śarva had vanished from sight, spoke to Mahodara: / ‘O Mahodara, for my sake, you must guard all of this—

2.25.s:
rathacāpādikaṃ tāvatparirakṣitumarhasi /
yadā kṛtyaṃ mamaitena tadānīṃ tvaṃ mayā smṛtaḥ /
rathacāpādikaṃ sarvaṃ prahiṇu tvaṃ madantikam //
2.25.d:
रथचापादिकं तावत्परिरक्षितुमर्हसि ।
यदा कृत्यं ममैतेन तदानीं त्वं मया स्मृतः ।
रथचापादिकं सर्वं प्रहिणु त्वं मदन्तिकम् ॥
2.25.m: the chariot, the bow, and the rest—without omission for the time being. / When I have need of this, then, remembered by me, / send the chariot, bow, and everything to my presence.’

2.25.s:
vasiṣṭha uvāca
tathetyuktvā gate tasminbhṛguvaryo mahodare /
kṛtakṛtyo gurujanaṃ draṣṭuṃ gantumiyeṣa saḥ //
2.25.d:
वसिष्ठ उवाच
तथेत्युक्त्वा गते तस्मिन्भृगुवर्यो महोदरे ।
कृतकृत्यो गुरुजनं द्रष्टुं गन्तुमियेष सः ॥
2.25.m: Vasiṣṭha said: / When Mahodara had departed after saying ‘So be it,’ that best of Bhṛgus, / having accomplished his purpose, desired to go and see his elders.

2.25.s:
gacchannatha tadāsau tu himādrivanagahvare /
viveśa kandaraṃ rāmo bhāvikarmapracoditaḥ //
2.25.d:
गच्छन्नथ तदासौ तु हिमाद्रिवनगह्वरे ।
विवेश कन्दरं रामो भाविकर्मप्रचोदितः ॥
2.25.m: Proceeding then into a mountain forest retreat of the Himālaya, / Rāma entered a cave, impelled by his future destiny.

2.25.s:
sa tatra dadṛśe bālaṃ dhṛtaprāṇamanudrutam /
vyāghreṇa vipratanayaṃ rudantaṃ bhītabhītavat //
2.25.d:
स तत्र ददृशे बालं धृतप्राणमनुद्रुतम् ।
व्याघ्रेण विप्रतनयं रुदन्तं भीतभीतवत् ॥
2.25.m: There he saw a boy, a brāhmaṇa’s son, clinging to life, pursued / by a tiger, crying out in great terror.

2.25.s:
dṛṣṭvānukaṃpahṛdayastatparitrāṇakātaraḥ /
tiṣṭhatiṣṭheti taṃ vyāghraṃ vadannuccairathānvayāt //
2.25.d:
दृष्ट्वानुकंपहृदयस्तत्परित्राणकातरः ।
तिष्ठतिष्ठेति तं व्याघ्रं वदन्नुच्चैरथान्वयात् ॥
2.25.m: Seeing [this], his heart filled with compassion and anxious to rescue him, / he pursued [the beast], shouting loudly at the tiger: 'Stop! Stop!'

2.25.s:
tamanudrutya vegena cirādiva bhṛgūdvahaḥ /
āsasāda vane ghoraṃ śārdūlamatibhīṣaṇam //
2.25.d:
तमनुद्रुत्य वेगेन चिरादिव भृगूद्वहः ।
आससाद वने घोरं शार्दूलमतिभीषणम् ॥
2.25.m: Pursuing it swiftly, as if taking a long time, the upholder of the Bhṛgu race / reached the terrifying, dreadful tiger in the forest.

2.25.s:
vyāghreṇānudrutaḥ so 'pi palāyanvanagahvare /
nipapāta dvijasutastrastaḥ prāṇabhayāturaḥ //
2.25.d:
व्याघ्रेणानुद्रुतः सो ऽपि पलायन्वनगह्वरे ।
निपपात द्विजसुतस्त्रस्तः प्राणभयातुरः ॥
2.25.m: Pursued by the tiger, fleeing in the forest thicket, / the son of the twice-born fell, terrified and overcome with fear for his life.

2.25.s:
rāmo 'pi krodharaktākṣo vipraputraparīpsayā /
tṛṇamūlaṃ samādāya kuśāstreṇābhyamantrayat //
2.25.d:
रामो ऽपि क्रोधरक्ताक्षो विप्रपुत्रपरीप्सया ।
तृणमूलं समादाय कुशास्त्रेणाभ्यमन्त्रयत् ॥
2.25.m: Rāma too, his eyes red with anger, wishing to rescue the son of the brahmin, / took up the root of a blade of grass and consecrated it with a missile mantra over a kuśa grass.

2.25.s:
tāvattarakṣurbalavānādravatpatitaṃ dvijam /
dṛṣṭvā nanādasubhṛśaṃ rodasī kampayanniva //
2.25.d:
तावत्तरक्षुर्बलवानाद्रवत्पतितं द्विजम् ।
दृष्ट्वा ननादसुभृशं रोदसी कम्पयन्निव ॥
2.25.m: Meanwhile the powerful hyena ran toward the fallen twice-born; / seeing him, it roared intensely, as if shaking heaven and earth.

2.25.s:
dagdhvā tvastrāgninā vyāghraṃ praharantaṃ nakhāṅkuraiḥ /
akṛtavraṇamevāśu mokṣayāmāsa taṃ dvijam //
2.25.d:
दग्ध्वा त्वस्त्राग्निना व्याघ्रं प्रहरन्तं नखाङ्कुरैः ।
अकृतव्रणमेवाशु मोक्षयामास तं द्विजम् ॥
2.25.m: Having burned with the fire of the missile the tiger as it struck with its claw-tips, / he quickly rescued the twice-born without a single wound.

2.25.s:
so 'pi brahmāgninirdagdhadehaḥ pāpmā nabhastale /
gāndharvaṃ vapurāsthāya rāmamāheti sādaram //
2.25.d:
सो ऽपि ब्रह्माग्निनिर्दग्धदेहः पाप्मा नभस्तले ।
गान्धर्वं वपुरास्थाय राममाहेति सादरम् ॥
2.25.m: With his body consumed by the fire of the missile, that evil [creature] in the sky / assumed a Gandharva form and respectfully said to Rāma:

2.25.s:
vipraśāpena bhopūrvamahaṃ prāptastarakṣutām /
gacchāmi mocitaḥ śāpāttvayāhamadhunā divam //
2.25.d:
विप्रशापेन भोपूर्वमहं प्राप्तस्तरक्षुताम् ।
गच्छामि मोचितः शापात्त्वयाहमधुना दिवम् ॥
2.25.m: 'O hero, formerly through a brahmin's curse I fell into being a hyena; / freed from the curse by you, I now depart for heaven.'

2.25.s:
ityuktvā tu gate tasminrāmo vegena vismitaḥ /
patitaṃ dvijaputraṃ taṃ kṛpayā vyavapadyata //
2.25.d:
इत्युक्त्वा तु गते तस्मिन्रामो वेगेन विस्मितः ।
पतितं द्विजपुत्रं तं कृपया व्यवपद्यत ॥
2.25.m: Having spoken thus, when he had departed swiftly, Rāma, filled with wonder, / approached the fallen son of the twice-born with pity.

2.25.s:
mābhairevaṃ vadanvāṇīmārādeva dvijātmajam /
paramṛśattadaṅgāni śanairujjīvayannṛpa //
2.25.d:
माभैरेवं वदन्वाणीमारादेव द्विजात्मजम् ।
परमृशत्तदङ्गानि शनैरुज्जीवयन्नृप ॥
2.25.m: Saying 'Do not fear!' with words from close by, O king, / he touched the limbs of the son of the twice-born, slowly reviving him.

2.25.s:
rāmeṇotthāpitaścaivaṃ sa tadonmīlya locane /
vilokayandadarśāgre bhṛguśreṣṭhamavasthitam //
2.25.d:
रामेणोत्थापितश्चैवं स तदोन्मील्य लोचने ।
विलोकयन्ददर्शाग्रे भृगुश्रेष्ठमवस्थितम् ॥
2.25.m: Raised up thus by Rāma, he opened his eyes then; / looking around, he saw the best of the Bhṛgus standing before him.

2.25.s:
bhasmīkṛtaṃ ca śārdūlaṃ dṛṣṭavā vismayamāgataḥ /
gatabhīrāha kastvaṃ bhoḥ kathaṃ veha samāgataḥ //
2.25.d:
भस्मीकृतं च शार्दूलं दृष्टवा विस्मयमागतः ।
गतभीराह कस्त्वं भोः कथं वेह समागतः ॥
2.25.m: And seeing the tiger turned to ashes, he was filled with wonder; / his fear dispelled, he said: 'Who are you, sir, and how did you come here?

2.25.s:
kena vāyaṃ nihantuṃ māmudyato bhasmasātkṛtaḥ /
tarakṣurbhīṣaṇākāraḥ sākṣānmṛtyurivāparaḥ //
2.25.d:
केन वायं निहन्तुं मामुद्यतो भस्मसात्कृतः ।
तरक्षुर्भीषणाकारः साक्षान्मृत्युरिवापरः ॥
2.25.m: Or by whom was this [beast], who was intent on killing me, reduced to ashes— / this hyena of dreadful appearance, like Death himself incarnate?

2.25.s:
bhayasaṃmūḍhamanamo mamādyāpi mahāmate /
hate 'pi tasminnakhilā bhānti vai tanmayā diśaḥ //
2.25.d:
भयसंमूढमनमो ममाद्यापि महामते ।
हते ऽपि तस्मिन्नखिला भान्ति वै तन्मया दिशः ॥
2.25.m: Even now my mind is confounded with fear, O great-minded one; / even though it is slain, all directions seem to me full of it.

2.25.s:
tvāmeva manye sakalaṃ pitā mātā sutdṛdgurū /
paramāpadamāpannaṃ tvaṃ māṃ samupajīvayan //
2.25.d:
त्वामेव मन्ये सकलं पिता माता सुत्दृद्गुरू ।
परमापदमापन्नं त्वं मां समुपजीवयन् ॥
2.25.m: I consider you my all—father, mother, friend, and guru— / since you brought me back to life when I had fallen into the greatest calamity.

2.25.s:
āsīnmunivaraḥ kaścicchānto nāma mahātapāḥ /
putrastasyāsmi tīrthārthī śālagrāmamayāsiṣam //
2.25.d:
आसीन्मुनिवरः कश्चिच्छान्तो नाम महातपाः ।
पुत्रस्तस्यास्मि तीर्थार्थी शालग्राममयासिषम् ॥
2.25.m: There was a certain excellent sage named Śānta of great asceticism; / I am his son; seeking holy sites, I traveled to Śālagrāma.

2.25.s:
tasmātsaṃprasthitaśśailaṃ didṛkṣurgandhamādanam /
nānāmunigaṇairjuṣṭaṃ puṇyaṃ badarikāśramam //
2.25.d:
तस्मात्संप्रस्थितश्शैलं दिदृक्षुर्गन्धमादनम् ।
नानामुनिगणैर्जुष्टं पुण्यं बदरिकाश्रमम् ॥
2.25.m: Having set out from there, desiring to see Mount Gandhamādana / and the sacred hermitage of Badarī, frequented by hosts of various sages,

2.25.s:
gantukāmo 'pahāyāhaṃ panthānaṃ tu himācale /
praviśangahanaṃ ramyaṃ pradeśālokanākulam //
2.25.d:
गन्तुकामो ऽपहायाहं पन्थानं तु हिमाचले ।
प्रविशन्गहनं रम्यं प्रदेशालोकनाकुलम् ॥
2.25.m: wishing to go, I left the path in the Himālayas / and entered a lovely thicket, eager to behold the region.

2.25.s:
diśaṃprācīṃ samuddiśya krośamātramayāsiṣam /
tato diṣṭavaśenāhaṃ prādravaṃ bhayapīḍitaḥ //
2.25.d:
दिशंप्राचीं समुद्दिश्य क्रोशमात्रमयासिषम् ।
ततो दिष्टवशेनाहं प्राद्रवं भयपीडितः ॥
2.25.m: Directing myself toward the eastern direction, I went just a krośa; / then, by the power of destiny, I ran, afflicted with fear,

2.25.s:
patitaśca tvayā bhūyobhūmerutthāpito 'dhunā /
pitreva nitarāṃ putraḥ premṇātyarthaṃ dayālunā /
ityeṣa mama vṛttāntaḥ sākalyenoditastava //
2.25.d:
पतितश्च त्वया भूयोभूमेरुत्थापितो ऽधुना ।
पित्रेव नितरां पुत्रः प्रेम्णात्यर्थं दयालुना ।
इत्येष मम वृत्तान्तः साकल्येनोदितस्तव ॥
2.25.m: and having fallen, I was just now lifted up from the ground by you / like a son by an exceedingly compassionate father out of great affection. / Thus my entire story has been told to you.'

2.25.s:
vasiṣṭha uvāca
iti pṛṣṭastadā tena svavṛttāntamaśeṣataḥ /
kathayāmāsa rājendra rāmastasmai yathākramam //
2.25.d:
वसिष्ठ उवाच
इति पृष्टस्तदा तेन स्ववृत्तान्तमशेषतः ।
कथयामास राजेन्द्र रामस्तस्मै यथाक्रमम् ॥
2.25.m: Vasiṣṭha said: / Asked thus by him at that time, O best of kings, Rāma / related to him in due order his own entire story.

2.25.s:
tatastau prītisaṃyuktau kathayantau parasparam /
sthitvā nāticiraṃ kālamatha gantumiyeṣa saḥ //
2.25.d:
ततस्तौ प्रीतिसंयुक्तौ कथयन्तौ परस्परम् ।
स्थित्वा नातिचिरं कालमथ गन्तुमियेष सः ॥
2.25.m: Then the two of them, filled with affection, conversing with one another / after remaining for a short time, then he wished to depart.

2.25.s:
anvīyamānastenātha rāmastasmādguhāmukhāt /
niṣkramyāvasathaṃ pitroḥ saṃpratasthe mudānvitaḥ //
2.25.d:
अन्वीयमानस्तेनाथ रामस्तस्माद्गुहामुखात् ।
निष्क्रम्यावसथं पित्रोः संप्रतस्थे मुदान्वितः ॥
2.25.m: Followed by him, Rāma then emerged from the mouth of that cave / and set out with joy for the dwelling of his parents.

2.25.s:
akṛtavraṇa evāsau vyāghreṇa bhuvi pātitaḥ /
rāmeṇa rakṣitaścābhudyasmāddhyāghraṃ vinighnatā //
2.25.d:
अकृतव्रण एवासौ व्याघ्रेण भुवि पातितः ।
रामेण रक्षितश्चाभुद्यस्माद्ध्याघ्रं विनिघ्नता ॥
2.25.m: Because he was cast down on the ground by the tiger entirely without a wound (akṛtavraṇa), / and was protected by Rāma who slew the tiger,

2.25.s:
tasmāttadeva nāmāsya babhūva prathitaṃ bhuvi /
vipraputrasya rājendra tadetatso 'kṛtavraṇaḥ //
2.25.d:
तस्मात्तदेव नामास्य बभूव प्रथितं भुवि ।
विप्रपुत्रस्य राजेन्द्र तदेतत्सो ऽकृतव्रणः ॥
2.25.m: therefore that very name became renowned on earth / for that son of the brahmin, O best of kings—namely Akṛtavraṇa.

2.25.s:
tadā prabhṛti rāmasya cchāyevātapagā bhuvi /
babhūva mitramatyarthaṃ sarvāvasthāsu pārthiva //
2.25.d:
तदा प्रभृति रामस्य च्छायेवातपगा भुवि ।
बभूव मित्रमत्यर्थं सर्वावस्थासु पार्थिव ॥
2.25.m: From that time forward, on earth like a shadow fleeing the heat, / he became his extraordinary friend in all circumstances, O king.

2.25.s:
sa tenānugato rājanbhṛgorāsādya sannidhim /
dṛṣṭvā khyātiṃ ca so 'bhyetya vinayenābhyavādayat //
2.25.d:
स तेनानुगतो राजन्भृगोरासाद्य सन्निधिम् ।
दृष्ट्वा ख्यातिं च सो ऽभ्येत्य विनयेनाभ्यवादयत् ॥
2.25.m: Accompanied by him, O king, having reached the presence of Bhṛgu / and seeing Khyāti, he approached and saluted with humility.

2.25.s:
sa tābhyāṃ priyamāṇābhyāmāśīrbhirabhinanditaḥ /
dināni katicittatra nyavasattatpriyepsayā //
2.25.d:
स ताभ्यां प्रियमाणाभ्यामाशीर्भिरभिनन्दितः ।
दिनानि कतिचित्तत्र न्यवसत्तत्प्रियेप्सया ॥
2.25.m: Welcomed with blessings by the two who loved him, / he dwelt there for some days, seeking their pleasure.

2.25.s:
tatastayoranumate cyavanasya mahāmuneḥ /
āśramaṃ praticakrāma śiṣyasaṃghaiḥ samāvṛtam //
2.25.d:
ततस्तयोरनुमते च्यवनस्य महामुनेः ।
आश्रमं प्रतिचक्राम शिष्यसंघैः समावृतम् ॥
2.25.m: Then, with the permission of both, he proceeded toward the hermitage / of the great sage Cyavana, surrounded by hosts of disciples.

2.25.s:
niyantritāntaḥ karaṇaṃ taṃ ca saṃśāntamānasam /
sukanyācāpi tadbhāryāmavandata mahāmanāḥ //
2.25.d:
नियन्त्रितान्तः करणं तं च संशान्तमानसम् ।
सुकन्याचापि तद्भार्यामवन्दत महामनाः ॥
2.25.m: The high-minded one saluted him whose inner faculty was restrained, whose mind was completely tranquil, / and also his wife, Sukanyā.

2.25.s:
tābhyāṃ ca prītiyuktābhyāṃ rāmaḥ samabhinanditaḥ /
aurvāśramaṃ samāpede draṣṭukāmastaponidhim //
2.25.d:
ताभ्यां च प्रीतियुक्ताभ्यां रामः समभिनन्दितः ।
और्वाश्रमं समापेदे द्रष्टुकामस्तपोनिधिम् ॥
2.25.m: Greeted with affection by the two of them, Rāma / went to the hermitage of Ūrva, wishing to see the storehouse of ascetic power.

2.25.s:
taṃ cābhivādya medhāvī tena ca pratinanditaḥ /
uvāsa tatra tatprītyā dināni katicinnṛpa //
2.25.d:
तं चाभिवाद्य मेधावी तेन च प्रतिनन्दितः ।
उवास तत्र तत्प्रीत्या दिनानि कतिचिन्नृप ॥
2.25.m: Having saluted him and been greeted in return by him, the wise one / dwelt there for some days out of affection for him, O king.

2.25.s:
visṛṣṭastena śanakairṛcīkabhavanaṃ mudā /
pratasthe bhārgavaḥ śrīmānakṛtavraṇasaṃyutaḥ //
2.25.d:
विसृष्टस्तेन शनकैरृचीकभवनं मुदा ।
प्रतस्थे भार्गवः श्रीमानकृतव्रणसंयुतः ॥
2.25.m: Permitted by him to leave, the glorious Bhārgava, together with Akṛtavraṇa, / set out slowly and gladly for the dwelling of Ṛcīka.

2.25.s:
avandata pituḥ pitrornatvā pādau pṛthak pṛthak /
tau ca taṃ nṛpa saṃharṣāccāśiṣā pratyanandatām //
2.25.d:
अवन्दत पितुः पित्रोर्नत्वा पादौ पृथक् पृथक् ।
तौ च तं नृप संहर्षाच्चाशिषा प्रत्यनन्दताम् ॥
2.25.m: Bowing down, he saluted the feet of his father's parents individually, / and the two of them with great delight greeted him with blessings, O king.

2.25.s:
pṛṣṭaśca tābhyāmakhilaṃ nijavṛttamudāradhīḥ /
kathayāmāsa rājendra yathāvṛttamanukramāt //
2.25.d:
पृष्टश्च ताभ्यामखिलं निजवृत्तमुदारधीः ।
कथयामास राजेन्द्र यथावृत्तमनुक्रमात् ॥
2.25.m: Asked by the two of them about his entire story, the generous-minded one, / O best of kings, related what had happened in proper sequence.

2.25.s:
sthitvā dināni katicittatrāpi tadanujñayā /
jagāmāvasathaṃ pitrormudā paramayā yutaḥ //
2.25.d:
स्थित्वा दिनानि कतिचित्तत्रापि तदनुज्ञया ।
जगामावसथं पित्रोर्मुदा परमया युतः ॥
2.25.m: Having stayed there too for a few days, with their permission, / he went to the dwelling of his parents, filled with supreme joy.

2.25.s:
abhyetya pitarau rājannāsī nāvāśramottame /
avandata tayoḥ pādau yathāvadbhṛgunandana //
2.25.d:
अभ्येत्य पितरौ राजन्नासी नावाश्रमोत्तमे ।
अवन्दत तयोः पादौ यथावद्भृगुनन्दन ॥
2.25.m: Approaching his parents, O king, who were seated in the excellent hermitage, / the descendant of Bhṛgu duly saluted their feet.

2.25.s:
pādapraṇāmāvanataṃ samutthāpya ca sādaram /
āśliṣya netrasalilairnandantau paryaṣiñcatām //
2.25.d:
पादप्रणामावनतं समुत्थाप्य च सादरम् ।
आश्लिष्य नेत्रसलिलैर्नन्दन्तौ पर्यषिञ्चताम् ॥
2.25.m: Raising him respectfully as he bowed in salutation at their feet, / embracing him, rejoicing, they sprinkled him with tears from their eyes.

2.25.s:
āśīrbhirabhinandyāṅke samāropya suhurmukham /
vikṣantau tasya cāṅgāni parispṛśyāpaturmudam //
2.25.d:
आशीर्भिरभिनन्द्याङ्के समारोप्य सुहुर्मुखम् ।
विक्षन्तौ तस्य चाङ्गानि परिस्पृश्यापतुर्मुदम् ॥
2.25.m: Welcoming him with blessings, placing him on their laps, gazing again and again at his face, / and touching his limbs, they attained joy.

2.25.s:
apṛcchatāñca tau rāmaṃ kalenaitāvatā tvayā /
kiṃ kṛtaṃ putra ko vāyaṃ kutra vā tvamupasthitaḥ //
2.25.d:
अपृच्छताञ्च तौ रामं कलेनैतावता त्वया ।
किं कृतं पुत्र को वायं कुत्र वा त्वमुपस्थितः ॥
2.25.m: And the two asked Rāma: 'During this long time, / what was done by you, son? Who is this [companion]? Where have you been staying?

2.25.s:
kathaṃ saha sakāśe tvamāsthito vātra vāgataḥ /
tvayetadakhilaṃ vatsa kathyatāṃ tathyamāvayoḥ //
iti śrībrahmāṇḍe mahāpurāṇe vāyuprokte madhyabhāge tṛtīya
upoddhātapāder'junopākhyāne bhārgavacarite pañcaviṃśatitamo 'dhyāyaḥ // 25//
2.25.d:
कथं सह सकाशे त्वमास्थितो वात्र वागतः ।
त्वयेतदखिलं वत्स कथ्यतां तथ्यमावयोः ॥
इति श्रीब्रह्माण्डे महापुराणे वायुप्रोक्ते मध्यभागे तृतीय
उपोद्धातपादेर्ऽजुनोपाख्याने भार्गवचरिते पञ्चविंशतितमो ऽध्यायः ॥ 25॥
2.25.m:
How is it that you dwelt in company or arrived here? / Let all this be told truly to us by you, dear child.'

Thus ends the twenty-fifth chapter, entitled 'The Deeds of the Bhārgava' in the Story of Arjuna, in the Upoddhātapāda, the third middle section in the great Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa spoken by Vāyu. // 25

2.26.s:
vaśiṣṭha uvāca
iti pṛṣṭastadā tābhyāṃ rāmo rājankṛtāñjaliḥ /
tayorakathayatsarvamātmanā yadanuṣṭhitam //
2.26.d:
वशिष्ठ उवाच
इति पृष्टस्तदा ताभ्यां रामो राजन्कृताञ्जलिः ।
तयोरकथयत्सर्वमात्मना यदनुष्ठितम् ॥
2.26.m: Vasiṣṭha said: / Asked thus by the two of them at that time, O king, Rāma with palms joined in reverence / told them all that he had performed himself:

2.26.s:
nideśādvai kulagurostapaścaraṇamātmanaḥ /
śaṃbhornideśāttīrthānāmaṭanaṃ ca yathākramam //
2.26.d:
निदेशाद्वै कुलगुरोस्तपश्चरणमात्मनः ।
शंभोर्निदेशात्तीर्थानामटनं च यथाक्रमम् ॥
2.26.m: the practice of his own austerities by the instruction of the family guru, / and the wandering to sacred sites in due order by the instruction of Śambhu,

2.26.s:
tadājñayaiva daityanāṃ vadhaṃ cāmarakāraṇāt /
haraprasādādatrāpi hyakṛtavraṇadarśanam //
2.26.d:
तदाज्ञयैव दैत्यनां वधं चामरकारणात् ।
हरप्रसादादत्रापि ह्यकृतव्रणदर्शनम् ॥
2.26.m: and by his command alone the slaying of the Daityas for the sake of the immortals, / and also by Hara's grace the meeting with Akṛtavraṇa here.

2.26.s:
etatsarvamaśeṣeṇa yadanyaccātmanā kṛtam /
kathayāmāsa tadrāmaḥ pitroḥ saṃprīyamāṇayoḥ //
2.26.d:
एतत्सर्वमशेषेण यदन्यच्चात्मना कृतम् ।
कथयामास तद्रामः पित्रोः संप्रीयमाणयोः ॥
2.26.m: All this in its entirety, and whatever else he had done himself, / Rāma narrated to his parents, who were greatly pleased.

2.26.s:
tau ca tenoditaṃ sarvaṃ śrutvā tatkarma vistaram /
hṛṣṭau harṣāntaraṃ bhūyo rājannāpnuvatāvubhau //
2.26.d:
तौ च तेनोदितं सर्वं श्रुत्वा तत्कर्म विस्तरम् ।
हृष्टौ हर्षान्तरं भूयो राजन्नाप्नुवतावुभौ ॥
2.26.m: And hearing all that had been related by him, the detail of that deed, / both of them, delighted, attained even further joy, O king.

2.26.s:
evaṃ pitrormahārāja śuśrūṣāṃ bhṛgupuṅgavaḥ /
prakurvaṃstadvidheyātmā bhrātṝṇāṃ cāviśeṣataḥ //
2.26.d:
एवं पित्रोर्महाराज शुश्रूषां भृगुपुङ्गवः ।
प्रकुर्वंस्तद्विधेयात्मा भ्रातॄणां चाविशेषतः ॥
2.26.m: Thus, O great king, the foremost of the Bhṛgus, whose mind was obedient to them, / performed service to his parents and equally to his brothers.

2.26.s:
etasminneva kāle tu kadāciddhaihayeśvaraḥ /
ityeṣa mṛgayāṃ gāntuṃ caturaṅgabalānvitaḥ //
2.26.d:
एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु कदाचिद्धैहयेश्वरः ।
इत्येष मृगयां गान्तुं चतुरङ्गबलान्वितः ॥
2.26.m: At that very time, once, the lord of the Haihayas, / accompanied by his fourfold army, went out to hunt.

2.26.s:
saṃrajyamāne gagane bandhūkakusumāruṇaiḥ /
tārājāladyutiharaiḥ samantādaruṇāṃśubhiḥ //
2.26.d:
संरज्यमाने गगने बन्धूककुसुमारुणैः ।
ताराजालद्युतिहरैः समन्तादरुणांशुभिः ॥
2.26.m: As the sky was colored red like bandhūka blossoms / by the crimson rays on all sides that took away the brilliance of the multitude of stars,

2.26.s:
mandaṃ vījati proddhūtaketakīvanarājibhiḥ /
prābhātike gandhavahe kumudākarasaṃspṛśi //
2.26.d:
मन्दं वीजति प्रोद्धूतकेतकीवनराजिभिः ।
प्राभातिके गन्धवहे कुमुदाकरसंस्पृशि ॥
2.26.m: while the morning wind blew gently, shaking rows of ketakī thickets / and touching beds of water lilies,

2.26.s:
vayāṃsi narmadātīratarunīḍāśrayeṣu ca /
vyāharansvākulā vāco manaḥśrotrasukhāvahāḥ //
2.26.d:
वयांसि नर्मदातीरतरुनीडाश्रयेषु च ।
व्याहरन्स्वाकुला वाचो मनःश्रोत्रसुखावहाः ॥
2.26.m: and the birds in the nests resting on the trees of the Narmadā's bank / uttered sweet calls that brought joy to mind and ear,

2.26.s:
narmadātīratīrthaṃ tadavatīryāghahāriṇi /
tattoye munivṛndeṣu gṛṇātsubrahma śāśvatam //
2.26.d:
नर्मदातीरतीर्थं तदवतीर्याघहारिणि ।
तत्तोये मुनिवृन्देषु गृणात्सुब्रह्म शाश्वतम् ॥
2.26.m: the crowds of sages having descended to that sacred ford on the bank of the Narmadā, / in its sin-destroying water, chanted the eternal Brahman,

2.26.s:
vidhivatkṛtamaitreṣu sannivṛtya sarittaṭāt /
āśamaṃ prati gacchatsu munimukhyeṣu karmiṣu //
2.26.d:
विधिवत्कृतमैत्रेषु सन्निवृत्य सरित्तटात् ।
आशमं प्रति गच्छत्सु मुनिमुख्येषु कर्मिषु ॥
2.26.m: and the foremost sages, dutiful in rites, having duly performed their morning prayers, / returned from the riverbank and were walking toward the hermitage,

2.26.s:
pratyekaṃ vīrapatnīṣu vyagrāsu gṛhakarmasu /
homārthaṃ munikalpābhirduhyamānāsu dhenuṣu //
2.26.d:
प्रत्येकं वीरपत्नीषु व्यग्रासु गृहकर्मसु ।
होमार्थं मुनिकल्पाभिर्दुह्यमानासु धेनुषु ॥
2.26.m: while the wives of the heroes were individually occupied with domestic chores, / and cows were being milked by those resembling sages for the oblation,

2.26.s:
sthāne munikumāreṣu taṃ dohaṃ hi nayatsu ca /
agnihotrākule jāte sarvabhūtasukhāvahe //
2.26.d:
स्थाने मुनिकुमारेषु तं दोहं हि नयत्सु च ।
अग्निहोत्राकुले जाते सर्वभूतसुखावहे ॥
2.26.m: and the young sons of sages carried that milk to the sacred place, / and the agnihotra fires, bringing joy to all beings, became fully active,

2.26.s:
vikasatsu sarojeṣu gāyatsu bhramareṣu ca /
vāśatsu nīḍānniṣpatya patatriṣu samantataḥ //
2.26.d:
विकसत्सु सरोजेषु गायत्सु भ्रमरेषु च ।
वाशत्सु नीडान्निष्पत्य पतत्रिषु समन्ततः ॥
2.26.m: while lotus flowers bloomed and bees hummed, / and birds flew out from their nests on all sides, chirping,

2.26.s:
anati vyagramattebhaturaṅgarathagāminām /
gātrālhādavivarddhanyāṃ velāyāṃ mandavāyunā //
2.26.d:
अनति व्यग्रमत्तेभतुरङ्गरथगामिनाम् ।
गात्राल्हादविवर्द्धन्यां वेलायां मन्दवायुना ॥
2.26.m: at that hour when the gentle breeze increased the bodily vigor / of the riders on not-too-hurried rutting elephants, horses, and chariots,

2.26.s:
gacchatsu cāśramopāntaṃ prasūnajalahāriṣu /
svādhyā yadakṣairbahubhirajināṃbaradhāribhiḥ //
2.26.d:
गच्छत्सु चाश्रमोपान्तं प्रसूनजलहारिषु ।
स्वाध्या यदक्षैर्बहुभिरजिनांबरधारिभिः ॥
2.26.m: and many wearing deer-skin garments and skilled in recitation / were going to the edge of the hermitage carrying flowers and water,

2.26.s:
samyak prayojyamāneṣu mantreṣūccāvaceṣu ca /
praiṣeṣūccāryamāṇeṣu hūyamāneṣu vahniṣu //
2.26.d:
सम्यक् प्रयोज्यमानेषु मन्त्रेषूच्चावचेषु च ।
प्रैषेषूच्चार्यमाणेषु हूयमानेषु वह्निषु ॥
2.26.m: and higher and lower mantras were being properly recited, / liturgical directions were being chanted, and oblations were being cast into fires,

2.26.s:
yathā vanmantratantroktakriyāsu vitatāsu ca /
jvaladagniśikhākāre tamastapanatejasi //
2.26.d:
यथा वन्मन्त्रतन्त्रोक्तक्रियासु विततासु च ।
ज्वलदग्निशिखाकारे तमस्तपनतेजसि ॥
2.26.m: and rites prescribed by mantras and tantras were being performed according to rule; / when the splendour of the sun, having the form of a blazing tongue of fire,

2.26.s:
pratihatya diśaḥ sarvā vivṛṇvāne ca medinīm /
savitaryudayaṃ yāti naiśe tamasi naśyati //
2.26.d:
प्रतिहत्य दिशः सर्वा विवृण्वाने च मेदिनीम् ।
सवितर्युदयं याति नैशे तमसि नश्यति ॥
2.26.m: repelled darkness from all directions and revealed the earth, / and as the sun arose and the darkness of night vanished,

2.26.s:
tārakāsu vilīnāsu kāṣṭhāsu vimalāsu ca /
kṛtamaitrādiko rājā mṛgayāṃ haihayeśvaraḥ //
2.26.d:
तारकासु विलीनासु काष्ठासु विमलासु च ।
कृतमैत्रादिको राजा मृगयां हैहयेश्वरः ॥
2.26.m: the stars having faded and the quarters having cleared, / the king, the lord of the Haihayas, having performed his morning prayer and other rites, to hunt

2.26.s:
niryayau nagarāttasmātpurohitasamanvitaḥ /
balaiḥ sarvaiḥ samuditaiḥ savājirathakuñjaraiḥ //
2.26.d:
निर्ययौ नगरात्तस्मात्पुरोहितसमन्वितः ।
बलैः सर्वैः समुदितैः सवाजिरथकुञ्जरैः ॥
2.26.m: went out from that city accompanied by his family priest, / with all his collected forces, accompanied by horses, chariots, and elephants,

2.26.s:
sacivaḥ sahitaḥ śrīmān savayobhiśca rājabhiḥ /
mahatā balabhāreṇa namayanvasudhātalam //
2.26.d:
सचिवः सहितः श्रीमान् सवयोभिश्च राजभिः ।
महता बलभारेण नमयन्वसुधातलम् ॥
2.26.m: the glorious one accompanied by ministers and kings of his own age, / making the surface of the earth bend beneath the great burden of his army,

2.26.s:
nādayanrathaghoṣeṇa kakubhaḥ sarvato nṛpaḥ /
svabalaughapadakṣepaprakṣuṇṇāvanireṇubhiḥ //
2.26.d:
नादयन्रथघोषेण ककुभः सर्वतो नृपः ।
स्वबलौघपदक्षेपप्रक्षुण्णावनिरेणुभिः ॥
2.26.m: making the directions resound on every side with the roar of chariots, the king, / with the dust of the earth crushed under the tread of his host of troops

2.26.s:
yayau saṃcchādayanvyoma vimānaśatasaṃkulam /
saṃpravaśya vanaṃ ghoraṃ vindhyodrerbalasaṃcayaiḥ //
2.26.d:
ययौ संच्छादयन्व्योम विमानशतसंकुलम् ।
संप्रवश्य वनं घोरं विन्ध्योद्रेर्बलसंचयैः ॥
2.26.m: went, covering the sky crowded with hundreds of aerial vehicles; / and entering the dread forest of the Vindhya mountain with his collected forces,

2.26.s:
bhṛśaṃ vilolayā māsa samantādrājasattamaḥ /
parivārya vanaṃ tattu sa rājā nijasainikaiḥ //
2.26.d:
भृशं विलोलया मास समन्ताद्राजसत्तमः ।
परिवार्य वनं तत्तु स राजा निजसैनिकैः ॥
2.26.m: the best of kings stirred it up violently on all sides; / having encircled that forest with his own soldiers,

2.26.s:
mṛgānnānāvidhānhiṃsrānnijaghāna śitaiḥ śaraiḥ /
ākarṇakṛṣṭakodaṇḍayodhamuktaiḥ śiteṣubhiḥ //
2.26.d:
मृगान्नानाविधान्हिंस्रान्निजघान शितैः शरैः ।
आकर्णकृष्टकोदण्डयोधमुक्तैः शितेषुभिः ॥
2.26.m: that king struck down various kinds of fierce wild beasts with sharp arrows. / With sharp arrows released by warriors drawing their bows to the ear,

2.26.s:
nikṛttagātrāḥ śārdūlā nyapatanbhuvi kecana /
udagravegapādātakhaḍgakhaṇḍitavigrahāḥ //
2.26.d:
निकृत्तगात्राः शार्दूला न्यपतन्भुवि केचन ।
उदग्रवेगपादातखड्गखण्डितविग्रहाः ॥
2.26.m: tigers whose limbs were severed fell to the ground; / their bodies cleaved by the swords of swiftly charging foot-soldiers,

2.26.s:
varāhayūthapāḥ kecidrudhirārdrā dharāmaguḥ /
pracaṇḍaśāktikonmuktaśaktinirbhinnamastakāḥ //
2.26.d:
वराहयूथपाः केचिद्रुधिरार्द्रा धरामगुः ।
प्रचण्डशाक्तिकोन्मुक्तशक्तिनिर्भिन्नमस्तकाः ॥
2.26.m: some leader boars covered in blood fell to the earth; / their skulls shattered by spears hurled by fierce spearmen,

2.26.s:
mṛgaughāḥ pratyapadyanta parvatā iva medinīm /
nārācā viddhasarvāṅgāḥ siṃharkṣaśarabhādayaḥ //
2.26.d:
मृगौघाः प्रत्यपद्यन्त पर्वता इव मेदिनीम् ।
नाराचा विद्धसर्वाङ्गाः सिंहर्क्षशरभादयः ॥
2.26.m: herds of beasts collapsed to the ground like mountains; / with all their limbs pierced by iron shafts, lions, bears, śarabhas, and other beasts

2.26.s:
vasudhāmanvakīryanta śoṇitārdrāḥ samantataḥ /
evaṃ savāguraiḥ kaiścitpatadbhiḥ patitairapi //
2.26.d:
वसुधामन्वकीर्यन्त शोणितार्द्राः समन्ततः ।
एवं सवागुरैः कैश्चित्पतद्भिः पतितैरपि ॥
2.26.m: fell scattered upon the earth, drenched in blood on all sides. / Thus, with some caught in nets, some falling, and others already fallen,

2.26.s:
śvabhiścānudrutaiḥ kaiściddhāvamānaistathā mṛgaiḥ /
āttairvikrośamānaiśca bhītaiḥ prāṇabhayāturaiḥ //
2.26.d:
श्वभिश्चानुद्रुतैः कैश्चिद्धावमानैस्तथा मृगैः ।
आत्तैर्विक्रोशमानैश्च भीतैः प्राणभयातुरैः ॥
2.26.m: with some pursued by hounds, and with beasts fleeing in that manner, / seized, screaming, terrified, and tormented by fear for their lives,

2.26.s:
yugāpāye yathātyarthaṃ vanamākulamābabhau /
varāhasiṃhaśārdūlaśvāvicchaśakulāni ca //
2.26.d:
युगापाये यथात्यर्थं वनमाकुलमाबभौ ।
वराहसिंहशार्दूलश्वाविच्छशकुलानि च ॥
2.26.m: the forest appeared exceedingly agitated, as at the end of an age. / And herds of boars, lions, tigers, porcupines, hares,

2.26.s:
camarīrurugomāyugavayarkṣavṛkānbahūn /
kṛṣṇasārāndvīpimṛgānraktakhaḍgamṛgānavi //
2.26.d:
चमरीरुरुगोमायुगवयर्क्षवृकान्बहून् ।
कृष्णसारान्द्वीपिमृगान्रक्तखड्गमृगानवि ॥
2.26.m: camarī cows, ruru deer, jackals, gavayas, bears, many wolves, / blackbucks, leopards, and rhinoceroses,

2.26.s:
vicitrāṅgānmṛgānanyānnyaṅkūnapi ca sarvaśaḥ /
bālānstanandhayānyūnaḥ sthavirānmithunāngaṇān //
2.26.d:
विचित्राङ्गान्मृगानन्यान्न्यङ्कूनपि च सर्वशः ।
बालान्स्तनन्धयान्यूनः स्थविरान्मिथुनान्गणान् ॥
2.26.m: spotted deer, other varied animals, and gazelles on every side— / the young, the sucklings, the mature, the aged, and groups of mated pairs—

2.26.s:
nijaghnurniśitaiḥ śastraiḥ śastravadhyānhi sainikāḥ /
evaṃ hatvā mṛgān ghorānhiṃsraprāyānaśeṣataḥ //
2.26.d:
निजघ्नुर्निशितैः शस्त्रैः शस्त्रवध्यान्हि सैनिकाः ।
एवं हत्वा मृगान् घोरान्हिंस्रप्रायानशेषतः ॥
2.26.m: the soldiers slaughtered with sharp weapons, for they were fit to be killed by arms. / Having thus slain terrifying and mostly fierce beasts without remainder,

2.26.s:
śrameṇa mahatā yuktā babhūvurnṛpasainikāḥ /
madhye dinakare prāpte sasainyaḥ sa tadā nṛpaḥ //
2.26.d:
श्रमेण महता युक्ता बभूवुर्नृपसैनिकाः ।
मध्ये दिनकरे प्राप्ते ससैन्यः स तदा नृपः ॥
2.26.m: the king’s soldiers were overcome by great exhaustion. / When the sun reached mid-day, that king with his army,

2.26.s:
narmadāṃ dharmasaṃtaptaḥ pipāsuragamacchanaiḥ /
avatīya tatastasyāstoye sabalavāhanaḥ //
2.26.d:
नर्मदां धर्मसंतप्तः पिपासुरगमच्छनैः ।
अवतीय ततस्तस्यास्तोये सबलवाहनः ॥
2.26.m: scorched by heat and thirsty, approached the Narmadā slowly. / Then, descending into her waters along with his forces and mounts,

2.26.s:
vijāgāha śubhe rājā kṣuttṛṣṇāparipīḍitaḥ /
snātvā pītvā ca salilaṃ sa tasyāḥ sukhaśītalam //
2.26.d:
विजागाह शुभे राजा क्षुत्तृष्णापरिपीडितः ।
स्नात्वा पीत्वा च सलिलं स तस्याः सुखशीतलम् ॥
2.26.m: afflicted by hunger and thirst, the king plunged into the auspicious [river]. / Having bathed and drunk her pleasantly cool water,

2.26.s:
bisāṃkurāṇi śubhrāṇi svādūni prajaghāsa ca /
vikrīḍya toye suciramuttīrya sabalo nṛpaḥ //
2.26.d:
बिसांकुराणि शुभ्राणि स्वादूनि प्रजघास च ।
विक्रीड्य तोये सुचिरमुत्तीर्य सबलो नृपः ॥
2.26.m: he ate sweet, white lotus shoots; / having disported for a long time in the water, the king emerged with his army

2.26.s:
viśaśrāma ca tattīre tarukhaṇḍopamaṇḍite /
ālaṃbapāne tigmāṃśau sasainyaḥ sānugo nṛpaḥ //
2.26.d:
विशश्राम च तत्तीरे तरुखण्डोपमण्डिते ।
आलंबपाने तिग्मांशौ ससैन्यः सानुगो नृपः ॥
2.26.m: and rested on its bank adorned with groves of trees. / When the hot-rayed sun began to sink, the king, accompanied by his troops and followers,

2.26.s:
niścakrāma puraṃ gantuṃ vindhyādrivanagahvarāt /
sa gacchanneva dadṛśe narmadā tīramāśritam //
2.26.d:
निश्चक्राम पुरं गन्तुं विन्ध्याद्रिवनगह्वरात् ।
स गच्छन्नेव ददृशे नर्मदा तीरमाश्रितम् ॥
2.26.m: set forth to return to his capital from the forest-cavern of the Vindhya mountain. / As he was going, he saw on the bank of the Narmadā

2.26.s:
āśramaṃ puṇyaśīlasya jamadagnermahātmanaḥ /
tato nivṛtya sainyāni dūre 'vasthāpya pārthivaḥ //
2.26.d:
आश्रमं पुण्यशीलस्य जमदग्नेर्महात्मनः ।
ततो निवृत्य सैन्यानि दूरे ऽवस्थाप्य पार्थिवः ॥
2.26.m: the hermitage of the high-souled Jamadagni of virtuous conduct. / Then the king turned back his troops, stationed them far away,

2.26.s:
paricāraiḥ katipathaiḥ sahito 'yāttadāśamam /
gatvā tadāśramaṃ ramyaṃ purohitasamanvitaḥ //
2.26.d:
परिचारैः कतिपथैः सहितो ऽयात्तदाशमम् ।
गत्वा तदाश्रमं रम्यं पुरोहितसमन्वितः ॥
2.26.m: and went to that hermitage accompanied by only a few attendants. / Having reached that lovely hermitage accompanied by his family priest,

2.26.s:
upetya muniśārdūlaṃ nanāma śirasā nṛpaḥ /
abhinaṃ dyāśaṣā taṃ vai jamadagnirnṛpottamam //
2.26.d:
उपेत्य मुनिशार्दूलं ननाम शिरसा नृपः ।
अभिनं द्याशषा तं वै जमदग्निर्नृपोत्तमम् ॥
2.26.m: approaching the tiger among sages, the king bowed his head. / Welcoming that best of kings with a blessing, Jamadagni indeed

2.26.s:
pūjayāmāsa vidhivadarghapādyāsanādibhiḥ /
saṃbhāvayitvā tāṃ pūjāṃ vihitāṃ muninā tadā //
2.26.d:
पूजयामास विधिवदर्घपाद्यासनादिभिः ।
संभावयित्वा तां पूजां विहितां मुनिना तदा ॥
2.26.m: honored him according to rule with arghya, water for washing feet, a seat, and other offerings. / Having accepted that worship performed then by the sage,

2.26.s:
niṣasādāsane śubhra purastasya mahāmuneḥ /
tamāsīnaṃ nṛpavaraṃ kuśāsanagato muniḥ //
2.26.d:
निषसादासने शुभ्र पुरस्तस्य महामुनेः ।
तमासीनं नृपवरं कुशासनगतो मुनिः ॥
2.26.m: he sat down on a bright seat before that great sage. / To the excellent king seated there, the sage, seated on a kuśa grass seat,

2.26.s:
papraccha kuśalapraśnaṃ putramitrādibandhuṣu /
saha saṃkathayaṃstena rājñā munivarottamaḥ //
2.26.d:
पप्रच्छ कुशलप्रश्नं पुत्रमित्रादिबन्धुषु ।
सह संकथयंस्तेन राज्ञा मुनिवरोत्तमः ॥
2.26.m: addressed inquiries of welfare concerning his sons, friends, and other kinsmen. / Conversing with that king, the foremost among the best of sages,

2.26.s:
sthitvā nāticiraṃ kālamātithyārthaṃ nyamantrayat /
tataḥ sa rājā suprīto jamadagni mabhāṣata //
2.26.d:
स्थित्वा नातिचिरं कालमातिथ्यार्थं न्यमन्त्रयत् ।
ततः स राजा सुप्रीतो जमदग्नि मभाषत ॥
2.26.m: having waited not very long, invited him to receive hospitality. / Thereupon, that delighted king spoke to Jamadagni:

2.26.s:
maharṣe dehi me 'nujñāṃ gamiṣyāmi svakaṃ puram /
samagravāhanabalo hyahaṃ tasmānmahāmune //
2.26.d:
महर्षे देहि मे ऽनुज्ञां गमिष्यामि स्वकं पुरम् ।
समग्रवाहनबलो ह्यहं तस्मान्महामुने ॥
2.26.m: “O great sage, grant me permission; I shall go to my own city. / For I have my complete host of mounts and forces; therefore, O great sage,

2.26.s:
kartu na śakyamā tithyaṃ tvayā vanyāśinā vane /
athavā tvaṃ tapaḥśaktyā kartumātithyamadya me //
2.26.d:
कर्तु न शक्यमा तिथ्यं त्वया वन्याशिना वने ।
अथवा त्वं तपःशक्त्या कर्तुमातिथ्यमद्य मे ॥
2.26.m: hospitality cannot be offered by you who subsist on forest fare in the forest. / Or even if you are able to offer me hospitality today by the power of your austerities,

2.26.s:
śaknoṣyapi purīṃ gantuṃ māmanujñāturhasi /
anyathā cetkhalaiḥ sainyairatyarthaṃ munisattama //
2.26.d:
शक्नोष्यपि पुरीं गन्तुं मामनुज्ञातुर्हसि ।
अन्यथा चेत्खलैः सैन्यैरत्यर्थं मुनिसत्तम ॥
2.26.m: you ought to grant me leave to go to my city; / for otherwise, O best of sages, through unruly soldiers

2.26.s:
tapasvināṃ bhavetpīḍā niyamakṣayakārikā /
vasiṣṭha uvāca
ityevamuktaḥ sa munistaṃ prāhasthīyatāṃ kṣaṇam //
2.26.d:
तपस्विनां भवेत्पीडा नियमक्षयकारिका ।
वसिष्ठ उवाच
इत्येवमुक्तः स मुनिस्तं प्राहस्थीयतां क्षणम् ॥
2.26.m: there would be harassment to the ascetics, causing the destruction of their religious vows.” / Vasiṣṭha said: / Thus addressed, that sage said to him: “Stay for a moment;

2.26.s:
sarvaṃ saṃpādayithye 'hamātithyaṃ sānugasya te /
ityuktvāhūya tāṃ dogdhrīmuvācāyaṃ mamātithiḥ //
2.26.d:
सर्वं संपादयिथ्ये ऽहमातिथ्यं सानुगस्य ते ।
इत्युक्त्वाहूय तां दोग्ध्रीमुवाचायं ममातिथिः ॥
2.26.m: I shall provide all hospitality for you along with your followers.” / Having said this, he summoned the milch cow and said: “This is my guest.

2.26.s:
upāga tastvayā tasmātkriyatāmadya satkṛtiḥ /
ityuktā muninā dogdhrī sātitheyamaśeṣataḥ /
dudoha nṛpaterāśu yadyogyaṃ munigauravāt //
2.26.d:
उपाग तस्त्वया तस्मात्क्रियतामद्य सत्कृतिः ।
इत्युक्ता मुनिना दोग्ध्री सातिथेयमशेषतः ।
दुदोह नृपतेराशु यद्योग्यं मुनिगौरवात् ॥
2.26.m:
"He has arrived; therefore, show him hospitality today."
Having been thus addressed by the sage, that milch-cow, out of reverence for the sage, / quickly milked forth everything suitable for hospitality to the king in its entirety.

2.26.s:
athāśramaṃ tatsurarājasadmanikāśamāsīdbhṛgupuṅgavasya /
vibhūtibhedairavicintyarupamananyasādhyaṃ surabhiprabhāvāt //
2.26.d:
अथाश्रमं तत्सुरराजसद्मनिकाशमासीद्भृगुपुङ्गवस्य ।
विभूतिभेदैरविचिन्त्यरुपमनन्यसाध्यं सुरभिप्रभावात् ॥
2.26.m: Then the hermitage of that foremost of the Bhṛgus became like the dwelling of the king of gods, / having unimaginable forms through diverse splendors, impossible to accomplish by any other means, through the power of Surabhi.

2.26.s:
anekaratnojjvalacitrahemaprakāśamālāparivītamuccaiḥ /
pūrṇenduśubhrābhraviṣaktaśṛṅgaiḥ prāsādasaṃghaiḥ parivītamantaḥ //
2.26.d:
अनेकरत्नोज्ज्वलचित्रहेमप्रकाशमालापरिवीतमुच्चैः ।
पूर्णेन्दुशुभ्राभ्रविषक्तशृङ्गैः प्रासादसंघैः परिवीतमन्तः ॥
2.26.m: It was completely surrounded on high by brilliant garlands of various jewels and bright gold, / and encompassed within by multitudes of mansions whose pinnacles touched clouds as bright as the full moon.

2.26.s:
kāṃsyārakūṭārasatāmrahemadurvarṇasaudho paladārumṛdbhiḥ /
pṛthagvimiśrairbhavanairanekaiḥ sadbhāsitaṃ netramanobhirāmaiḥ //
2.26.d:
कांस्यारकूटारसताम्रहेमदुर्वर्णसौधो पलदारुमृद्भिः ।
पृथग्विमिश्रैर्भवनैरनेकैः सद्भासितं नेत्रमनोभिरामैः ॥
2.26.m: It shone brightly with numerous buildings—delightful to the eyes and mind— / made separately and in combination of bronze, brass, iron, copper, gold, silver, stone, timber, and clay,

2.26.s:
mahārharatnojjvalahemavedikāniṣkūṭasopānakuṭīviṭaṅkakaiḥ /
tulākapāṭargalakuḍyadehalīniśāntaśālājiraśobhitairbhṛśam //
2.26.d:
महार्हरत्नोज्ज्वलहेमवेदिकानिष्कूटसोपानकुटीविटङ्ककैः ।
तुलाकपाटर्गलकुड्यदेहलीनिशान्तशालाजिरशोभितैर्भृशम् ॥
2.26.m: Greatly adorned with alters of gold brilliant with priceless gems, with private pleasure-gardens, stairs, cottages, and eaves, / with beams, doors, bolts, walls, thresholds, inner apartments, halls, and courtyards,

2.26.s:
valabhyalindāṅgapācārutoraṇairadabhraparyantacatuṣkikādibhiḥ /
staṃbheṣu kuḍyeṣu ca divyaratnavicitracitraiḥ pariśobhamānaiḥ //
2.26.d:
वलभ्यलिन्दाङ्गपाचारुतोरणैरदभ्रपर्यन्तचतुष्किकादिभिः ।
स्तंभेषु कुड्येषु च दिव्यरत्नविचित्रचित्रैः परिशोभमानैः ॥
2.26.m: With lovely arched gateways on upper chambers and porticos, with extensive surrounding quadrangles and the like, / and resplendent on its pillars and walls with variegated pictures made of heavenly gems,

2.26.s:
uccāvacai ratnavarairvicitrasuvarṇasiṃhāsanapīṭhikādyaiḥ /
sa bhakṣyabhojyādibhi rannapānairupetabhāṇḍopagataikadeśaiḥ //
2.26.d:
उच्चावचै रत्नवरैर्विचित्रसुवर्णसिंहासनपीठिकाद्यैः ।
स भक्ष्यभोज्यादिभि रन्नपानैरुपेतभाण्डोपगतैकदेशैः ॥
2.26.m: With high and low golden thrones and pedestals inlaid with excellent, varied gems, / and with portions furnished with vessels supplied with foods to be chewed and eaten and drinks.

2.26.s:
gṛhairamartyocitasarvasaṃpatsamanvitairnetramano 'bhirāmaiḥ /
tasyāśramaṃ sannagaropamānaṃ babhau vadhūbhiścamanoharābhiḥ //
iti śrībrahmāṇḍe mahāpurāṇe vāyuprokte madhyabhāge tṛtīya
upoddhātapāder'junopākhyāne ṣaḍviṃśatitamo 'dhyāyaḥ // 26//
2.26.d:
गृहैरमर्त्योचितसर्वसंपत्समन्वितैर्नेत्रमनो ऽभिरामैः ।
तस्याश्रमं सन्नगरोपमानं बभौ वधूभिश्चमनोहराभिः ॥
इति श्रीब्रह्माण्डे महापुराणे वायुप्रोक्ते मध्यभागे तृतीय
उपोद्धातपादेर्ऽजुनोपाख्याने षड्विंशतितमो ऽध्यायः ॥ 26॥
2.26.m:
With dwellings endowed with all splendors fit for immortals and delightful to the eyes and mind, / his hermitage, resembling an excellent city, shone with captivating women.

Thus ends the twenty-sixth chapter in the story of Arjuna in the Upoddhātapāda, the third [part], in the middle section of the holy and great Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa proclaimed by Vāyu.
